title: Hadwiger’s exact coloring conjecture
open: Prove that every graph with chromatic number at least \(t\) contains \(K_t\) as a minor, for every \(t\).
status: Proposed in 1943; proved through \(t=6\). Norin–Steiner’s October 2026 preprint establishes a linear bound, leaving the exact coefficient one unresolved.
why: Would connect chromatic complexity to complete-minor structure.
key_works: Norin–Steiner (2026), [*A Proof of the Linear Hadwiger Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05291).

title: Sharp chromatic coefficient for excluded odd minors
open: For \(g(t)=\max\{\chi(G):G\text{ has no odd }K_t\text{ minor}\}\), determine the sharp asymptotic coefficient \(g(t)/t\).
status: The coefficient-one conjecture was refuted in a December 2025 preprint; examples require \((3/2-o(1))t\) colors. A linear upper bound follows from known reductions and the 2026 linear Hadwiger theorem.
why: Supplies the correct quantitative replacement for odd Hadwiger.
key_works: Kühn–Sauermann–Steiner–Wigderson (2025), [*Disproof of the Odd Hadwiger Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.20392).

title: Clique immersion conjecture
open: Does every \(t\)-chromatic graph contain a weak immersion of \(K_t\), with distinct branch vertices connected by pairwise edge-disjoint paths?
status: Open since the late twentieth century. Fox–Pach–Suk establish the conclusion when the graph has at most \((1.64-o(1))t\) vertices.
why: Would force complete communication patterns from chromatic complexity.
key_works: Fox–Pach–Suk (2025), [*Immersions and Albertson’s conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05893).

title: Erdős–Hajnal conjecture
open: For every fixed graph \(H\), prove that every \(n\)-vertex induced-\(H\)-free graph contains a clique or independent set of size \(n^{\varepsilon(H)}\), for some \(\varepsilon(H)>0\).
status: Open since 1977. All five-vertex forbidden graphs are covered; 2026 work reaches additional six-vertex examples.
why: Would distinguish hereditary structure from unrestricted Ramsey behavior.
key_works: Huang–Ju–Zhou (2026), [*Erdős–Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06258).

title: Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture
open: For every fixed tree \(T\), prove that induced-\(T\)-free graphs have chromatic number bounded by a function of their clique number.
status: Originates in the 1970s. Many trees are settled; the 2026 bounded-boxicity theorem does not resolve arbitrary graphs.
why: Would classify single forbidden induced subgraphs that control coloring.
key_works: Davies–Yuditsky (2026), [*Polynomial Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture for graphs of bounded boxicity*](https://igt.centre-mersenne.org/articles/10.5802/igt.17/).

title: Thomassen’s large-girth, large-minimum-degree conjecture
open: For every \(k,g\), does sufficiently large minimum degree force a subgraph with minimum degree at least \(k\) and girth at least \(g\)?
status: Proposed in 1983. Important bounded-girth cases are known; the general statement remains open.
why: Would extract locally sparse structure while retaining substantial connectivity.
key_works: Christoph–Janzer–Petrova–Steiner (2025), [*Extending Thomassen’s conjecture to directed graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11311).

title: Sharp triangle-free extraction threshold
open: Determine the smallest growth rate of \(f(k)\) such that every graph with \(\chi(G)\ge f(k)\) contains a triangle-free \(k\)-chromatic subgraph.
status: Rödl proved existence in 1977. Steiner’s 2026 preprint improves a tower bound to a single exponential; the correct scale remains unknown.
why: Quantifies how much chromatic complexity survives removing triangles.
key_works: Steiner (2026), [*Locally bipartite subgraphs via multicolor Ramsey numbers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02522v2).

title: Domatic growth excluding an induced double star
open: For each fixed diameter-three tree \(T\), must the domatic number of induced-\(T\)-free graphs tend to infinity with minimum degree?
status: An unresolved case of a 2026 classification conjecture. Stars and \(P_4\) admit strong positive results.
why: Would guarantee many disjoint dominating service layers from local density.
key_works: Chuet–Djelloul–La–Pirot–Zaredehabadi (2026), [*A Domatic Analogue of χ-Bounded Graph Classes and the Gyárfás–Sumner Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.02030).

title: Graph reconstruction conjecture
open: Is every finite simple graph with at least three vertices determined, up to isomorphism, by its multiset of vertex-deleted subgraphs?
status: Open since the 1940s. Trees, regular graphs, and numerous other classes are reconstructible.
why: Tests whether complete overlapping partial observations determine a network.
key_works: Dufresne–Jeronimo–Kenkel–Lindo–Villamizar (2026), [*Shuffling the Deck: Invariant Theory and the Graph Reconstruction Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.16567).

title: Edge reconstruction conjecture
open: Is every finite simple graph with at least four edges determined by its edge-deleted deck, retaining isolated vertices?
status: Open since the 1960s; many dense and structured classes are settled.
why: Asks whether observations after every possible single-link failure identify the original graph.
key_works: Calle–Gould (2025), [*A combinatorial K-theory perspective on the Edge Reconstruction Conjecture in graph theory*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14986).

title: Optimal induced-forest density in planar graphs
open: Determine the largest \(c\) such that every planar \(n\)-vertex graph contains an induced forest on at least \(cn-O(1)\) vertices.
status: The historical \(1/2\) conjecture was refuted in 2026 preprints. Current guarantees and constructions leave \(2/5\le c\le25/52\).
why: Determines the intrinsic vertex-deletion cost of eliminating planar cycles.
key_works: Cames van Batenburg–Goedgebeur–Jooken (2026), [*Counterexamples to the Albertson–Berman conjecture: minimum order, connectivity and an improved ratio bound*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23260).

title: Reed’s chromatic-number conjecture
open: Prove \(\chi(G)\le\lceil(\Delta(G)+1+\omega(G))/2\rceil\) for every graph.
status: Proposed in 1998. Weaker universal interpolation bounds and many exact special cases are known.
why: Would sharply combine maximum degree and clique obstructions.
key_works: Reed (1998), [*ω, Δ, and χ*](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/%28SICI%291097-0118%28199804%2927%3A4%3C177%3A%3AAID-JGT1%3E3.0.CO%3B2-K).

title: Borodin–Kostochka conjecture
open: Prove that every graph with \(\Delta\ge9\) and no \(K_\Delta\) is \((\Delta-1)\)-colorable.
status: Proposed in 1977; known for sufficiently large maximum degree. The full range beginning at nine remains open.
why: Would locate the sharp one-color improvement over Brooks’ theorem.
key_works: Dvořák–Kang–Mikšaník (2026), [*On Borodin–Kostochka conjecture for correspondence coloring*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.14427).

title: Total coloring conjecture
open: Color all vertices and edges of every simple graph with at most \(\Delta+2\) colors, respecting every adjacency and incidence conflict.
status: Proposed independently in the 1960s. Numerous classes are settled; dense-graph results do not cover the unrestricted case.
why: Gives the fundamental simultaneous node-and-link scheduling bound.
key_works: Henderschedt–McDonald–Shan (2025), [*Total coloring graphs with large minimum degree*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.05548).

title: List edge-coloring conjecture
open: Prove \(\chi'_\ell(G)=\chi'(G)\) for every loopless multigraph.
status: Open since the 1970s. Galvin settled bipartite multigraphs in 1995; asymptotic and further special-family results are known.
why: Would show that individual edge eligibility lists require no additional colors.
key_works: Jafari (2026), [*The List Edge-Coloring Conjecture for New Infinite Families*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22895).

title: Erdős–Nešetřil strong edge-coloring conjecture
open: Prove strong chromatic index at most \(5\Delta^2/4\) for even \(\Delta\), and \((5\Delta^2-2\Delta+1)/4\) for odd \(\Delta\).
status: Proposed in 1985; five-cycle blow-ups attain these bounds. A 2026 preprint gives \(1.73\Delta^2\) for sufficiently large \(\Delta\).
why: Determines optimal scheduling under distance-two interference.
key_works: Davey–Hurley–de Joannis de Verclos–Kang–Volec (2026), [*Strong edge-colouring via local flag algebras*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17421).

title: Equitable list-coloring conjecture
open: If \(\Delta(G)\le r-1\), do arbitrary lists of \(r\) colors permit a proper coloring using each color at most \(\lceil |V(G)|/r\rceil\) times?
status: Proposed in 2003. Ordinary equitable coloring is settled; the unrestricted list version remains open.
why: Combines individual eligibility with balanced workloads.
key_works: Kostochka–Pelsmajer–West (2003), [*A list analogue of equitable coloring*](https://doi.org/10.1002/jgt.10137).

title: Linear arboricity conjecture
open: Partition every maximum-degree-\(\Delta\) graph into at most \(\lceil(\Delta+1)/2\rceil\) linear forests.
status: Proposed in 1981. Known bounds include \(\Delta/2+O(\sqrt\Delta\log^4\Delta)\); exact rounding remains unresolved.
why: Determines the minimum number of nonbranching routing layers.
key_works: Lang–Postle (2023), [*An Improved Bound for the Linear Arboricity Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.04251); Christoph et al. (2025), [*New bounds for linear arboricity and related problems*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.20500).

title: Cereceda’s quadratic recoloring conjecture
open: Connect any two proper \((d+2)\)-colorings of an \(n\)-vertex \(d\)-degenerate graph by \(O_d(n^2)\) valid single-vertex recolorings.
status: Open since 2007. A general \(O(n^{d+1})\) bound is known; quadratic bounds hold with additional slack or restrictions.
why: Bounds the cost of moving between feasible configurations.
key_works: Bousquet–Heinrich (2019), [*A polynomial version of Cereceda’s conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.05619).

title: Tutte’s 5-flow conjecture
subfield: Flows, perfect matchings, and cycle covers
open: Prove that every bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero integer flow with absolute values at most four.
status: Proposed in 1954. Seymour’s 1981 theorem gives a nowhere-zero 6-flow; the one-unit improvement remains open.
why: Seeks a sharp universal integrality bound for conservative flows.
key_works: Seymour (1981), *Nowhere-zero 6-flows*; Cranston–Li–Su–Wang–Xu (2026), [*Reconfiguration of Nowhere-zero Flows*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24685).

title: Tutte’s 3-flow conjecture
subfield: Flows, perfect matchings, and cycle covers
open: Does every 4-edge-connected graph admit a nowhere-zero integer 3-flow?
status: Proposed in 1972. Six-edge-connectivity suffices; connectivity four remains unresolved.
why: Relates network redundancy to exceptionally economical circulation.
key_works: Lovász–Thomassen–Wu–Zhang (2013), *Nowhere-zero 3-flows and modulo k-orientations*; Li–Li (2026), [*Nowhere-zero 3-flows in graphs with forbidden edge-cuts*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08377).

title: Berge–Fulkerson conjecture
subfield: Flows, perfect matchings, and cycle covers
open: Find six perfect matchings in every bridgeless cubic graph, allowing repetitions, with each edge occurring exactly twice.
status: Open since 1971. Many classes are settled; a 2026 paper relates finite and locally finite infinite versions.
why: Would replace fractional matching decompositions with six exact integral objects.
key_works: Magalhães Júnior–Silva (2026), [*On some perfect matching conjectures in infinite, cubic, bridgeless graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29511).

title: Fan–Raspaud conjecture
subfield: Flows, perfect matchings, and cycle covers
open: Does every bridgeless cubic graph have three perfect matchings with empty common intersection?
status: Proposed in 1994; implied by Berge–Fulkerson. Numerous special cases are known.
why: Isolates a weaker matching-compatibility obstruction.
key_works: Karabáš–Máčajová–Nedela–Škoviera (2026), [*Regular colouring defect of a cubic graph and the conjectures of Fan–Raspaud and Fulkerson*](https://doi.org/10.26493/1855-3974.3291.A20).

title: Alon–Tarsi shortest cycle-cover bound
subfield: Flows, perfect matchings, and cycle covers
open: Cover every bridgeless cubic graph’s \(m\) edges by cycles of total length at most \(7m/5\).
status: Proposed in the 1980s. The target is proved under substantial additional connectivity; general bounds remain larger.
why: Determines the optimal redundancy of closed-route coverage.
key_works: Luo–Hao–Luo–Zhang (2026), [*A Note on Alon–Tarsi Shortest Cycle Cover Conjecture*](https://doi.org/10.1002/jgt.70026).

title: Smallest Petersen-coloring obstruction
subfield: Flows, perfect matchings, and cycle covers
open: Determine the smallest bridgeless cubic graph whose edges cannot map to Petersen-graph edges while preserving each vertex’s incident-edge triple.
status: The universal conjecture was refuted in 2026. The September revision leaves the minimum order between 40 and 52.
why: Identifies the minimal obstruction behind the refutation.
key_works: Goedgebeur–Jooken–Máčajová–Mattiolo–Mazzuoccolo–Ulyanov (2026), [*Disproving the Petersen Coloring Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10028v4).

title: Barnette’s conjecture
open: Prove that every 3-connected cubic bipartite planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle.
status: Proposed in 1969. Special face-size cases and strong approximate Hamiltonian structures are known.
why: Would force spanning tours from planarity, regularity, and connectivity.
key_works: Bekos–Kaufmann–Pfister (2025), [*Approximating Barnette’s Conjecture*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.GD.2025.6).

title: Lovász’s vertex-transitive Hamiltonian-path problem
open: Does every finite connected vertex-transitive graph have a Hamiltonian path?
status: Posed in 1969. Li–Methuku’s September 2026 preprint gives a nearly linear \(n^{1-o(1)}\) cycle-length bound.
why: Asks whether global symmetry eliminates all spanning-path obstructions.
key_works: Li–Methuku (2026), [*A nearly linear bound for the Lovász conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38135).

title: Sheehan’s conjecture
open: Prove that no finite simple 4-regular graph has exactly one Hamiltonian cycle.
status: Proposed in 1975. Odd-degree parity arguments and extensive searches leave the 4-regular case open.
why: Would force multiple spanning tours from modest uniform redundancy.
key_works: Sheehan (1977), [*Graphs with exactly one hamiltonian circuit*](https://doi.org/10.1002/jgt.3190010110); Brinkmann–De Pauw (2024), [*Uniquely hamiltonian graphs for many sets of degrees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.08946).

title: Chvátal’s toughness conjecture
open: Is there a universal \(t\) such that every \(t\)-tough graph is Hamiltonian, where \(|S|\ge t\,c(G-S)\) whenever \(c(G-S)>1\)?
status: Open since 1973. Numerous forbidden-induced-subgraph classes admit sufficient toughness constants.
why: Tests whether bounded strengthening of the separation obstruction captures Hamiltonicity.
key_works: Shan (2025), [*Hamiltonian cycles in tough \((P_4\cup P_1)\)-free graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.08936).

title: Matthews–Sumner conjecture
open: Prove that every 4-connected claw-free graph is Hamiltonian.
status: Proposed in 1984. Every 7-connected claw-free graph is Hamilton-connected; connectivity four remains open.
why: Would turn a local branching prohibition into a sharp spanning-cycle guarantee.
key_works: Ryjáček–Vrána (2011), [*Line graphs of multigraphs and Hamilton-connectedness of claw-free graphs*](https://doi.org/10.1002/jgt.20498).
aliases: Equivalent to Thomassen’s 4-connected line-graph Hamiltonicity conjecture.

title: Erdős–Gyárfás power-of-two cycle conjecture
open: Must every graph of minimum degree at least three contain a cycle whose length is a power of two?
status: Posed in 1995. A 2026 search excludes counterexamples through 40 vertices generally, 48 for cubic graphs, and 66 for bipartite graphs.
why: Forces an exact arithmetic pattern from a weak degree condition.
key_works: Ducoffe–Dumitru (2026), [*Towards a More Structured Search for Erdős–Gyárfás Counter-Examples*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28594).

title: Classification of 2-factor-Hamiltonian cubic bipartite braces
open: Are \(K_{3,3}\) and the Heawood graph the only cubic bipartite braces in which every 2-factor is Hamiltonian?
status: The Pfaffian case was settled in 2025; non-Pfaffian braces remain.
why: Classifies graphs where every spanning degree-two structure is connected.
key_works: Gorsky–Johanni–Wiederrecht (2025), [*A note on the 2-Factor Hamiltonicity Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.08128).

title: Graceful tree conjecture
open: Label every \(n\)-vertex tree bijectively by \(0,\ldots,n-1\), so its edge differences are exactly \(1,\ldots,n-1\).
status: Rosa, 1967. Many families are settled; recent gracesize results obtain almost all required differences.
why: Produces structured cyclic decompositions with no repeated differences.
key_works: Letzter–Pokrovskiy–Williams (2025–2026), [*On the gracesize of trees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.11331).

title: Tree packing conjecture
open: Pack arbitrary trees \(T_i\) with \(|V(T_i)|=i\), \(1\le i\le n\), edge-disjointly into \(K_n\).
status: Proposed in 1976. Almost-linear maximum-degree cases are known; an unrestricted claimed proof was withdrawn in September 2026.
why: Would show that tree orders alone suffice for complete coordinated packing.
key_works: Allen et al., [*The tree packing conjecture for trees of almost linear maximum degree*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.11720); Chalise–Clark–Gnang, [withdrawn proof](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13840).

title: Gallai’s path decomposition conjecture
open: Partition every connected \(n\)-vertex graph’s edges into at most \(\lceil n/2\rceil\) simple paths.
status: Open since the 1960s. Planar graphs, maximum degree at most five, and further classes are settled.
why: Gives an optimal universal bound on nonrepeating route decompositions.
key_works: Chu–Fan–Zhou (2026), [*Gallai’s conjecture and the path number of odd semi-cliques*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2025.114725).

title: Hajós’ cycle decomposition conjecture
open: Partition every simple Eulerian \(n\)-vertex graph’s edges into at most \(\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor\) simple cycles.
status: Originates in the 1960s; numerous classes and all Eulerian graphs through 12 vertices are verified.
why: Determines the sharp universal cost of decomposing even-degree networks into cycles.
key_works: Heinrich–Natale–Streicher (2017), [*Hajós’ cycle conjecture for small graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.08724).

title: Tuza’s triangle packing–covering conjecture
open: Prove \(\tau_\triangle(G)\le2\nu_\triangle(G)\), where the parameters count minimum triangle-hitting edges and maximum edge-disjoint triangles.
status: Proposed in 1981. A 2026 preprint settles maximum degree at most seven; the general factor two remains open.
why: Would sharply relate triangle elimination to disjoint local obstructions.
key_works: Gupta (2026), [*Tuza’s conjecture for graphs of maximum degree at most seven*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06538).

title: Ryser’s hypergraph covering conjecture
open: Prove \(\tau(H)\le(r-1)\nu(H)\) for every \(r\)-partite \(r\)-uniform hypergraph.
status: Open since the 1960s; the full statement is known for \(r\le3\). A September 2026 preprint settles \(r=4,\nu=2\).
why: Extends bipartite matching–cover duality to multipartite hypergraphs.
key_works: White (2026), [*Tuza’s Ryser-conjecture claim for four-partite hypergraphs with matching number two*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14281).

title: Turán’s tetrahedron problem
open: Prove \(\operatorname{ex}(n,K_4^{(3)})=(5/9+o(1))\binom n3\), or determine the correct density.
status: Open since 1941. Construction gives \(5/9\); an October 2026 revision gives a Lean-checked upper bound below \(0.557789\).
why: Is the central first example of genuinely hypergraphic extremal behavior.
key_works: Jeong–Park–Im–Lee–Yang (2026), [*A New Upper Bound for the Turán Density of the Tetrahedron*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27495v2).

title: Codegree threshold for a tetrahedron
open: Prove that minimum pair-degree greater than \((1/2+\varepsilon)n\) forces \(K_4^{(3)}\) in sufficiently large 3-uniform hypergraphs.
status: Matching lower constructions exist. The analogous threshold for \(K_4^{(3)}\) minus an edge is settled; the complete tetrahedron remains open.
why: Measures how local pair abundance forces global consistency.
key_works: Falgas-Ravry–Pikhurko–Vaughan–Volec (2023), [*The codegree threshold of \(K_4^-\)*](https://doi.org/10.1112/jlms.12722).

title: Brown–Erdős–Sós sparse-configuration conjecture
open: For each \(k\ge3\), must every 3-uniform hypergraph with \(\varepsilon n^2\) edges contain \(k\) edges spanning at most \(k+3\) vertices?
status: Proposed in 1973. The \(k=3\) case is the Ruzsa–Szemerédi theorem; four edges on seven vertices is the first unresolved case.
why: Connects sparse hypergraphs to removal and recurrence phenomena.
key_works: Brown–Erdős–Sós (1973), *On the existence of triangulated spheres in 3-graphs, and related problems*; [Erdős’ problem archive](https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~erdosproblems/erdos/newproblems/TripleSystems.html).

title: Erdős’ girth conjecture
open: For every fixed \(k\ge2\), construct arbitrarily large graphs with girth greater than \(2k\) and \(\Omega(n^{1+1/k})\) edges.
status: The upper exponent follows from breadth-first expansion. Matching constructions are known for selected parameters, including \(k=2,3,5\).
why: Would determine the optimal density of graphs without short cycles.
key_works: Parter (2014), [*Bypassing Erdős’ Girth Conjecture: Hybrid Stretch and Sourcewise Spanners*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.6835).

title: Extremal exponent of \(K_{4,4}\)
open: Determine \(\operatorname{ex}(n,K_{4,4})\), especially whether the upper exponent \(7/4\) is attainable.
status: Classical Zarankiewicz gap: constructions give \(\Omega(n^{5/3})\), while Kővári–Sós–Turán gives \(O(n^{7/4})\).
why: Is a small forbidden bipartite graph with unknown extremal exponent.
key_works: Bayer–Mészáros–Rónyai–Szabó (2026), [*Subgraphs of the projective norm graph*](https://doi.org/10.1017/fms.2026.10245).

title: Meyniel’s cop-number conjecture
subfield: Graph parameters and topological graph theory
open: Prove that \(O(\sqrt n)\) cops suffice to capture one robber on every connected \(n\)-vertex graph in the standard perfect-information game.
status: Proposed in the 1980s. The scale is necessary; random graphs satisfy the conjecture, but the universal bound remains open.
why: Determines the sharp universal pursuit resource requirement.
key_works: Prałat–Wormald (2016), [*Meyniel’s conjecture holds for random graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.2841).

title: Vizing’s domination product conjecture
subfield: Graph parameters and topological graph theory
open: Prove \(\gamma(G\square H)\ge\gamma(G)\gamma(H)\) for all graphs.
status: Open since the 1960s. A factor-one-half bound and refinements are known; a 2026 stronger-factor claim was withdrawn.
why: Would show that domination requirements multiply across product coordinates.
key_works: Clark–Suen (2000), [*An Inequality Related to Vizing’s Conjecture*](https://doi.org/10.37236/1542); Suen–Tarr (2012), [*An Improved Inequality Related to Vizing’s Conjecture*](https://doi.org/10.37236/15).

title: Degree-57 Moore graph
subfield: Graph parameters and topological graph theory
open: Construct or rule out a strongly regular graph with parameters \((3250,57,0,1)\).
status: Open since 1960. A June 2026 preprint rules out involutions in its automorphism group.
why: Would complete the diameter-two Moore graph classification.
key_works: Ishida (2026), [*No involutions in the missing Moore graph*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29183).
aliases: Missing Moore graph; Hoffman–Singleton degree-57 problem.

title: Harary–Hill crossing-number conjecture
subfield: Graph parameters and topological graph theory
open: Prove \(\operatorname{cr}(K_n)=\frac14\lfloor n/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-3)/2\rfloor\).
status: Proposed in the 1960s. Matching drawings exist; the lower bound is known for substantial restricted drawing classes.
why: Determines unavoidable crossings in complete interconnection networks.
key_works: Ábrego–Aichholzer–Fernández-Merchant–Ramos–Salazar (2013), [*Shellable drawings and the cylindrical crossing number of \(K_n\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.3665).

title: Zarankiewicz’s crossing-number conjecture
subfield: Graph parameters and topological graph theory
open: Prove \(\operatorname{cr}(K_{m,n})=\lfloor m/2\rfloor\lfloor(m-1)/2\rfloor\lfloor n/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor\).
status: Proposed in 1954. Equality is known when \(\min(m,n)\le6\); general lower bounds remain smaller.
why: Gives the exact crossing cost of complete bipartite interconnections.
key_works: Christian–Richter–Salazar (2013), [*Zarankiewicz’s Conjecture is finite for each fixed m*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jctb.2012.11.001); Brosch–Polak (2024), [semidefinite lower bounds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.02755).

title: Exponential growth of diagonal Ramsey numbers
open: Determine the exponential growth rate of \(R(k,k)\), including whether \(R(k,k)^{1/k}\) converges.
status: Random constructions give base at least \(\sqrt2\); the classical upper base four has been improved, but a large exponential gap remains.
why: Measures the maximum persistence of binary relations without large homogeneous sets.
key_works: Campos–Griffiths–Morris–Sahasrabudhe (2026), [*An exponential improvement for diagonal Ramsey*](https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2026.203.3.4).

title: Leading constant in \(R(3,t)\)
open: Determine whether \(R(3,t)\sim c\,t^2/\log t\), and find \(c\).
status: The order was settled in 1995. A 2025–2026 preprint raises the lower constant to \(1/2\); the upper constant remains one.
why: Would precisely quantify triangle-free graphs with bounded independence number.
key_works: Hefty–Horn–King–Pfender, [*Improving \(R(3,k)\) in just two bites*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.19718).

title: Logarithmic factors in fixed-clique off-diagonal Ramsey numbers
open: For each fixed \(s\ge4\), determine the logarithmic factors in \(R(s,t)\).
status: Bradač’s 2026 preprint gives \(\Omega_s(t^{s-1}/\log^{2s-4}t)\); the upper bound is \(O_s(t^{s-1}/\log^{s-2}t)\).
why: Would close the remaining scale gap after matching polynomial exponents.
key_works: Bradač (2026), [*Off-diagonal Ramsey numbers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28793).

title: Exact value of \(R(5,5)\)
open: Determine the least \(N\) forcing a monochromatic \(K_5\) in every red–blue coloring of \(K_N\).
status: The verified interval is \(43\le R(5,5)\le46\); four candidate values remain.
why: Is the next unresolved diagonal graph Ramsey number.
key_works: Angeltveit–McKay (2026), [*\(R(5,5)\le46\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15709).

title: Sharp growth of multicolor triangle Ramsey numbers
open: Determine the asymptotic value, or limit behavior, of \(\log R_q(K_3)/(q\log q)\).
status: The exponential-versus-superexponential question was resolved in 2026. Bounds leave coefficients between \(1/3\) and one.
why: Establishes the true cost of increasing the number of colors.
key_works: Steiner (2026), [*Locally bipartite subgraphs via multicolor Ramsey numbers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02522v2).

title: Tower height of diagonal 3-uniform Ramsey numbers
open: Establish doubly exponential lower growth for \(r_3(t,t)\), or substantially reduce its doubly exponential upper bound.
status: The fundamental gap remains \(2^{\Omega(t^2)}\) versus \(2^{2^{O(t)}}\).
why: Controls a central tower-height distinction between graphs and hypergraphs.
key_works: Mubayi–Suk (2020), [*A survey of hypergraph Ramsey problems*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.04229).

title: Worst-case ordered matching Ramsey numbers
open: Determine the largest ordered \(q\)-color Ramsey number among \(n\)-vertex matchings, for fixed \(q\ge2\).
status: A September 2026 lower bound is \(\exp(c_q(\log n)^q/(\log\log n)^{q-1})\), against \(\exp(O_q((\log n)^q))\).
why: Quantifies how vertex order amplifies unavoidable-pattern complexity.
key_works: Li (2026), [*Multicolor Ramsey numbers of ordered matchings*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08157).

title: Polynomial superlinearity for bounded-degree size-Ramsey numbers
open: Do fixed \(\Delta,\varepsilon>0\) permit \(n\)-vertex maximum-degree-\(\Delta\) graphs with size-Ramsey number at least \(n^{1+\varepsilon}\)?
status: Linear growth is false. Known subcubic constructions require \(n\exp(c\sqrt{\log n})\), still subpolynomial above linear.
why: Tests whether bounded local complexity can force polynomial hosting overhead.
key_works: Tikhomirov (2024), [*On bounded degree graphs with large size-Ramsey numbers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.05818).

title: Ramsey multiplicity constant of \(K_4\)
open: Determine the minimum asymptotic proportion of monochromatic four-vertex cliques in red–blue complete graphs.
status: Thomason refuted the random-coloring value \(1/32\) in 1989. Current constructions and lower bounds do not coincide.
why: Measures unavoidable abundance beyond Ramsey existence.
key_works: Parczyk–Pokutta–Spiegel–Szabó (2025), [*New Ramsey Multiplicity Bounds and Search Heuristics*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.04036).

title: Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture
open: Must every \(n\)-vertex digraph of minimum outdegree at least \(r\) contain a directed cycle of length at most \(\lceil n/r\rceil\)?
status: Proposed in 1978. Even the exact triangle threshold near \(n/3\) remains open.
why: Would infer short feedback loops from one-sided expansion.
key_works: Aharoni–Berger–Chudnovsky–Guo–Zerbib (2021), [*Non-uniform degrees and rainbow versions of the Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.11183).

title: Seymour’s second-neighborhood conjecture
open: Does every finite oriented graph have a vertex with at least as many distinct vertices at directed distance exactly two as at distance one?
status: Proposed in 1990; known for tournaments and several other classes. A 2026 preprint settles minimum outdegree seven.
why: Seeks unavoidable directed expansion without uniform degree assumptions.
key_works: Sadhukhan–Sandeep–Sen (2026), [minimum-outdegree-seven theorem](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30588).

title: Bermond–Thomassen disjoint-cycle conjecture
open: Does minimum outdegree at least \(2k-1\) force \(k\) vertex-disjoint directed cycles?
status: Proposed in 1981; known for \(k\le3\). A 2026 relaxation permits reversing one arc in each selected cycle.
why: Would give the sharp local threshold for independent feedback loops.
key_works: Bessy–Muis–Sereni–Steiner–Wiederrecht (2026), [*A relaxation of the Bermond–Thomassen conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12948).

title: Hoàng–Reed directed cactus conjecture
open: Does minimum outdegree \(d\) force directed cycles \(C_1,\ldots,C_d\), each meeting the preceding union in at most one vertex?
status: Proposed in the 1980s; the cases through \(d=3\) are known.
why: Would produce tightly controlled branching arrangements of directed cycles.
key_works: Welhan (2010), [*The Hoàng–Reed Conjecture for \(\delta^+=3\)*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2010.03.001).

title: Woodall’s disjoint-dijoin conjecture
open: If every nonempty directed cut has at least \(k\) edges, can the graph’s edges contain \(k\) disjoint sets each meeting every directed cut?
status: Proposed in 1976. Fractional duality and several structural cases are known; integral packing remains open.
why: Would turn cut redundancy into disjoint global connectivity certificates.
key_works: Gutiérrez (2024), [*Towards a Dual Version of Woodall’s Conjecture for Partial 3-Trees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.05703).

title: Neumann-Lara’s planar dichromatic conjecture
open: Partition every oriented planar graph’s vertices into two sets inducing acyclic digraphs.
status: Proposed in 1985. Many girth-restricted cases are settled; arbitrary planar orientations remain open.
why: Would bound planar directed cyclic complexity by two layers.
key_works: Steiner (2019), [*A Note on Graphs of Dichromatic Number 2*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00351).

title: Erdős–Neumann-Lara orientation conjecture
open: For every \(k\), does sufficiently large undirected chromatic number force an orientation of dichromatic number at least \(k\)?
status: Originates in the 1970s. A 2026 preprint proves the corresponding list version; the ordinary version remains open.
why: Asks whether undirected incompatibility can always generate directed feedback complexity.
key_works: Harutyunyan–Picasarri-Arrieta–Puig i Surroca (2026), [*On the list version of a conjecture of Erdős and Neumann-Lara*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01020).

title: Sidorenko’s conjecture
subfield: Graph homomorphisms, invariants, and zero-error information
open: Prove \(t_H(G)\ge t_{K_2}(G)^{e(H)}\) for every bipartite \(H\), where \(t_H(G)=\operatorname{hom}(H,G)/|V(G)|^{|V(H)|}\).
status: Proposed around 1991–1993. Many families are settled; a May 2026 spectral equivalence is a reformulation rather than a general proof.
why: Would make random-like graphs universal minimizers of bipartite pattern densities.
key_works: Li–Lin–Liu–Zhang (2026), [*Spectral Sidorenko inequalities and edge-spectral supersaturation*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26614).

title: Quasirandom forcing conjecture
subfield: Graph homomorphisms, invariants, and zero-error information
open: For every bipartite \(H\) containing a cycle, prove that \(t_{K_2}(W)=p\) and \(t_H(W)=p^{e(H)}\), \(0<p<1\), force graphon \(W=p\) almost everywhere.
status: Studied since the late 1980s. It holds when some vertex of \(H\) is adjacent to the entire opposite part.
why: Would certify full quasirandomness using two statistics.
key_works: Li–Szegedy (2011/2026), [*On the logarithmic calculus and Sidorenko’s conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.1153).

title: Stanley’s tree-distinguishing conjecture
subfield: Graph homomorphisms, invariants, and zero-error information
open: Prove that nonisomorphic trees have distinct chromatic symmetric functions \(X_T=\sum_\kappa\prod_v x_{\kappa(v)}\), summing over proper colorings.
status: Posed in 1995. Many classes and all trees through 29 vertices are verified; stronger invariants distinguish trees but do not settle this invariant.
why: Would make a natural algebraic invariant a complete tree description.
key_works: Nishimura (2026), [*The Kneser chromatic function distinguishes trees*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2026.115009); Awan (2026), [derivative reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13464).

title: Shannon capacity of the seven-cycle
subfield: Graph homomorphisms, invariants, and zero-error information
open: Determine \(\Theta(C_7)=\sup_m\alpha(C_7^{\boxtimes m})^{1/m}\).
status: The 2026 lower bound is \(3.258805369885\ldots\); Lovász’s upper bound is approximately \(3.317668\).
why: Gives the exact zero-error rate of the smallest unresolved odd-cycle channel.
key_works: Shannon (1956), *The zero error capacity of a noisy channel*; Buys–Polak–Zuiddam (2026), [*Lean-verified lower bounds for the Shannon capacity of odd cycles*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29681).

title: Integer sum–product conjecture
open: For every \(\varepsilon>0\), prove \(\max(|A+A|,|AA|)\ge c_\varepsilon|A|^{2-\varepsilon}\) for finite \(A\subset\mathbb Z\).
status: Erdős–Szemerédi, 1983. Exponents above \(4/3\) are known; the 2026 real-number counterexample does not settle integers.
why: Quantifies incompatibility of additive and multiplicative structure.
key_works: Erdős–Szemerédi (1983), *On sums and products of integers*; Bloom–Sawin–Schildkraut–Zhelezov (2026), [real counterexample](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28781).

title: Optimal real sum–product exponent
open: For \(m(n)=\min_{A\subset\mathbb R,\ |A|=n}\max(|A+A|,|AA|)\), determine \(\liminf\log m(n)/\log n\).
status: A 2026 construction puts the exponent strictly below two; matching lower and upper exponents are unknown.
why: Identifies the correct replacement for the refuted real conjecture.
key_works: Bloom–Sawin–Schildkraut–Zhelezov (2026), [*The sum-product conjecture is false for real numbers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28781).

title: Polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa over general abelian groups
open: If \(|A+A|\le K|A|\), cover \(A\) by \(K^{O(1)}\) translates of a convex coset progression of dimension \(O(\log K)\) and size \(K^{O(1)}|A|\).
status: Bounded-characteristic cases are solved. Raghavan’s 2026 revision gives losses controlled by \((\log K)^{1+\varepsilon}\).
why: Would provide quantitatively efficient structure for approximate additive groups.
key_works: Raghavan (2025/2026), [*Improved Bounds for the Freiman–Ruzsa Theorem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.11217).

title: Dense infinite Sidon sequences
open: Construct an infinite Sidon set \(A\subset\mathbb N\) with \(|A\cap[1,N]|=N^{1/2-o(1)}\) for all sufficiently large \(N\).
status: Open since the mid-twentieth century. Ruzsa’s exponent \(\sqrt2-1\) remains the benchmark reported in 2026.
why: Separates finite optimal packings from compatible infinite constructions.
key_works: Ruzsa (1998), [*An Infinite Sidon Sequence*](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022314X97921922); Táfula (2026), [*Infinite Sidon-type sets for zero-sum linear forms*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20753).

title: Erdős–Turán additive-basis conjecture
open: If \(A\subseteq\mathbb N_0\) represents every sufficiently large integer as \(a+b\), prove that the ordered representation counts are unbounded.
status: Posed in 1941. Fixed lower bounds, including eight, do not establish unboundedness.
why: Would rule out uniformly sparse representations in an additive basis.
key_works: Borwein–Choi–Chu (2006), [*An old conjecture of Erdős–Turán on additive bases*](https://www.sfu.ca/~schoia/paper/erdos.pdf).
prize: Historical Erdős offer: US$500; current administration unverified.

title: Distinct subset sums
open: Prove that \(n\) positive integers with all subset sums distinct have largest element at least \(c2^n\), for an absolute \(c>0\).
status: Erdős, 1930s. Lower bounds remain on the \(2^n/\sqrt n\) scale.
why: Determines the compression limit for uniquely decodable additive encodings.
key_works: Dubroff–Fox–Xu (2021), *A note on the Erdős distinct subset sums problem*; Costa–Della Fiore (2026), [bandwidth refinement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27941).

title: Cap-set exponential growth constant
open: Determine \(\lim_n c_n^{1/n}\), where \(c_n\) is the largest progression-free subset of \(\mathbb F_3^n\).
status: Upper base approximately 2.756; constructions exceed 2.2203. A 2026 preprint shows products of any fixed cap set are asymptotically suboptimal.
why: Tests sharpness of slice-rank methods and constructions.
key_works: Ellenberg–Gijswijt (2016), [large progression-free subsets](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.09223); Hametner–Tyrrell (2026), [*Beating Product Constructions for Linear Equations Over Finite Fields*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12194).

title: Chowla’s cosine minimum
open: Prove every \(n\)-element \(A\subset\mathbb N\) has a real \(t\) with \(\sum_{a\in A}\cos(2\pi at)\le-c\sqrt n\).
status: A decades-old target. Shankar’s September 2026 preprint proves a negative excursion of order \(n^{1/5}\).
why: Would sharply control negative excursions of sparse trigonometric polynomials.
key_works: Bedert (2025), [*Polynomial bounds for the Chowla Cosine Problem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.05260); Shankar (2026), [log-free bound](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05338).

title: Sharp Roth bounds
open: Determine the correct asymptotic scale of the largest three-term-progression-free subset \(r_3(N)\) of \([N]\).
status: Roth, 1953. Raghavan’s 2026 dissertation reports upper saving \(\exp[-(\log N)^{1/6-o(1)}]\); constructions have square-root logarithmic scale.
why: Measures the density possible without the simplest additive pattern.
key_works: Kelley–Meka (2023), *Strong bounds for 3-progressions*; Raghavan (2026), [*Quantitative Topics in Arithmetic Combinatorics*](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/3f10x5g1).

title: Sharp four-term progression bounds
open: Determine the asymptotic scale of \(r_4(N)\).
status: Density convergence was proved in 1969. The verified benchmark is \(r_4(N)\ll N(\log N)^{-c}\), far from constructions.
why: Isolates the first major quantitative gap involving quadratic structure.
key_works: Green–Tao (2017), [*New bounds for Szemerédi’s theorem, III: A polylogarithmic bound for \(r_4(N)\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.01703).

title: Sharp Szemerédi bounds for longer progressions
open: Determine the correct asymptotic scale of \(r_k(N)\) for each fixed \(k\ge5\).
status: Existence settled in 1975. Leng–Sah–Sawhney give \(N\exp[-(\log\log N)^{c_k}]\); a large gap remains.
why: Would make higher-order Fourier analysis quantitatively predictive.
key_works: Leng–Sah–Sawhney (2024), [*Improved Bounds for Szemerédi’s Theorem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17995).

title: Divergent reciprocal sums force long progressions
open: If \(\sum_{a\in A}1/a=\infty\), must \(A\subset\mathbb N\) contain arithmetic progressions of every finite length?
status: Erdős, 1970s. The three-term case follows from modern bounds; already four terms remains open.
why: Extends additive structure beyond positive density.
key_works: Green (2026), [*Arithmetic progressions at the Journal of the LMS*](https://doi.org/10.1112/jlms.70483).

title: Polynomial saving for square-difference-free sets
open: Does an absolute \(c>0\) force \(|A|\le N^{1-c}\) whenever \(A\subset[N]\) has no nonzero square difference?
status: Furstenberg–Sárközy proves density decay; Green–Sawhney obtain \(N\exp(-c\sqrt{\log N})\).
why: Would reveal much stronger nonlinear additive expansion.
key_works: Green–Sawhney (2024/2025), [*New bounds for the Furstenberg–Sárközy theorem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.17448).

title: Sharp corners bounds
open: Determine the maximum size of \(A\subset[N]^2\) avoiding \((x,y),(x+d,y),(x,y+d)\), \(d\ne0\).
status: Ajtai–Szemerédi, 1974. A 2025 theorem gives density at most \(\exp[-(\log N)^{\Omega(1)}]\).
why: Connects multidimensional avoidance to communication complexity.
key_works: Jaber–Liu–Lovett–Ostuni–Sawhney (2025), [*Quasipolynomial bounds for the corners theorem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07006).

title: Quantitative axis-parallel squares
open: Determine the largest subset of \([N]^2\) avoiding all four corners of every nondegenerate axis-parallel square.
status: Multidimensional density theorems imply \(o(N^2)\); satisfactory quantitative bounds remain missing.
why: Tests recurrence beyond three-point configurations.
key_works: Green (2026), [*Arithmetic progressions at the Journal of the LMS*](https://doi.org/10.1112/jlms.70483).

title: Quantitative density Hales–Jewett
open: Determine the least dimension \(N(k,\delta)\) forcing a combinatorial line in every density-\(\delta\) subset of \([k]^N\).
status: Existence was proved in 1991. For three letters, Polymath gives a tower of height \(O(\delta^{-3})\); matching scales are remote.
why: Quantifies a foundational density and recurrence principle.
key_works: D. H. J. Polymath (2009/2012), [*A new proof of the density Hales–Jewett theorem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.3926).

title: Sixth Schur number
open: Determine the largest \(N=S(6)\) admitting a six-coloring of \([N]\) without a monochromatic \(x+y=z\).
status: The lower bound \(S(6)\ge536\) remains cited in July 2026 work; \(S(5)=160\) is settled.
why: Is a concrete frontier for exhaustive arithmetic search.
key_works: Heule (2018), [*Schur Number Five*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.08076); Bengone et al. (2026), [*Shifted S-templates and improved lower bounds for Schur numbers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15034).

title: Van der Waerden number \(W(2,7)\)
open: Determine the least \(N\) forcing a monochromatic seven-term progression in every two-coloring of \([N]\).
status: \(W(2,7)\ge3704\); no matching upper certificate is known. The preceding value is \(W(2,6)=1132\).
why: Is the next exact two-color arithmetic-progression frontier.
key_works: Rabung–Lotts (2012), [*Improving the Use of Cyclic Zippers in Finding Lower Bounds for van der Waerden Numbers*](https://doi.org/10.37236/2363).

title: Hales–Jewett number \(HJ(3,3)\)
open: Determine the least \(n\) forcing a monochromatic combinatorial line in every three-coloring of \(\{1,2,3\}^n\).
status: Mouhib’s 2026 work gives \(HJ(3,3)\ge22\) through checkable coloring certificates.
why: Converts a high-dimensional existence theorem into an exact finite target.
key_works: Mouhib (2026), [*Lower Bounds for the Hales–Jewett Numbers via Symmetric and One-Weight Colorings*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22155).

title: Hindman’s mixed sum–product quadruple
open: Must every finite coloring of \(\mathbb N\) contain distinct \(x,y\) with \(x,y,x+y,xy\) all the same color?
status: Posed in 1979. Two colors and rational-number analogues are settled; arbitrary finite natural-number colorings remain open.
why: Requires simultaneous additive and multiplicative recurrence.
key_works: Richter (2025/2026), [*Sums and products in sets of positive density*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.00515).

title: Arbitrarily large finite sums-and-products configurations
open: For every finite coloring of \(\mathbb N\) and every \(k\), find \(k\) distinct numbers whose nonempty subset sums and products are all one color.
status: Hindman, 1979. The rational analogue is proved; requiring one infinite set is false.
why: Tests the extent of compatibility between two algebraic operations.
key_works: Alweiss (2023/2026), [*Monochromatic Sums and Products over \(\mathbb Q\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08901); Richter, [density approach](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.00515).

title: Lonely runner conjecture
open: For nonzero integer speeds \(v_1,\ldots,v_k\), find \(t\) with \(\|tv_i\|\ge1/(k+1)\) for every \(i\).
status: Wills, 1960s. A 2026 computer-assisted preprint reports the cases through \(k=12\).
why: Links simultaneous avoidance to lattice coverings and scheduling.
key_works: Sungkawichai–Trakulthongchai (2026), [*Eleven, twelve, and thirteen lonely runners*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23906); Beck–Everett (2026), [*Lonely Runner Relations*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06259).

title: Sunflower conjecture
open: For fixed \(r\ge3\), does every family of more than \(C_r^k\) distinct \(k\)-sets contain \(r\) sets with identical pairwise intersections?
status: Erdős–Rado, 1960. General bounds have the form \((Cr\log k)^k\); removing the logarithm remains open.
why: Would strengthen a pervasive combinatorial compression principle.
key_works: Alweiss–Lovett–Wu–Zhang (2021), *Improved sunflower bounds*; Rao (2026), [*The story of sunflowers*](https://doi.org/10.1112/jlms.70380).

title: Union-closed sets conjecture
open: Prove that every finite union-closed family containing a nonempty set has an element occurring in at least half its members.
status: Frankl, 1979. An October 2026 preprint reports universal proportion \(0.3828852549667978\).
why: Asks whether closure forces a frequent coordinate.
key_works: Gilmer (2022), *A constant lower bound for the union-closed sets conjecture*; Costa–Sadhu (2026), [*Beyond Liu’s 0.382709 threshold*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02295).

title: Chvátal’s hereditary-family conjecture
open: In every finite hereditary family containing a nonempty set, is some maximum intersecting subfamily a star?
status: Proposed in 1974. Many structured hereditary families are settled; the unrestricted nonuniform case remains open.
why: Extends Erdős–Ko–Rado to arbitrary down-sets.
key_works: Chvátal (1974), *Intersecting families of edges in hypergraphs having the hereditary property*; Kupavskii (2023), [uniform hereditary families](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.02246).

title: Borg’s uniform hereditary-family conjecture
open: If every maximal member of a hereditary family has size at least \(2k\), is a largest intersecting family of its \(k\)-sets a star?
status: Known results require larger maximal-set size; Kupavskii reduces the sufficient threshold to order \(k\log k\).
why: Seeks the sharp local-dimension condition for intersection extremality.
key_works: Kupavskii (2023), [*Intersection theorems for uniform subfamilies of hereditary families*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.02246).

title: Erdős matching conjecture
open: For \(n\ge k(s+1)\), prove that matching number at most \(s\) forces at most \(\max\{\binom nk-\binom{n-s}k,\binom{k(s+1)-1}k\}\) edges.
status: Proposed in 1965; \(k=3\) is settled. A September 2026 revision proves \(k=4\) when \(s\ge6004\).
why: Would identify the extremal obstructions to many disjoint choices.
key_works: Hou–Hu–Liu (2026), [*The Erdős Matching Conjecture for 4-uniform hypergraphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26060).

title: Additive-square avoidance
open: Does an infinite word over some finite integer alphabet avoid every pair of consecutive equal-length, equal-sum blocks?
status: Posed around 2000. Additive cubes and a two-dimensional alphabet analogue can be avoided; one-dimensional squares remain open.
why: Separates arithmetic repetition from exact and anagram repetition.
key_works: Vukusic (2025), [*A Lebesgue variant of the additive square problem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21200).

title: Mäkelä’s ternary abelian-square conjecture
open: Construct an infinite ternary word whose only abelian-square factors are \(00,11,22\), or prove impossibility.
status: Open for decades. Avoidance of all sufficiently long abelian squares is known, but this sharp restriction is not.
why: Determines an exact alphabet-versus-repetition boundary.
key_works: Fici–Puzynina (2023), [*Abelian Combinatorics on Words: a Survey*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.09937), Conjecture 20.

title: Additive cubes on \(\{0,1,2,3\}\)
open: Does an infinite word on \(\{0,1,2,3\}\) avoid three consecutive equal-length blocks with equal sums?
status: Explicitly open in 2025; other four-element integer alphabets outside the arithmetic-progression equivalence class admit constructions.
why: Completes a precise four-letter alphabet classification.
key_works: Andrade–Mol (2025), [*Avoiding abelian and additive powers in rich words*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.15390).

title: Exact cyclic abelian repetition thresholds
open: Find the least integer \(A(d)\) such that every length \(n\) admits a \(d\)-letter word whose periodic repetition avoids abelian \(A(d)\)-powers with block length below \(n\).
why: Distinguishes circular from ordinary infinite-word avoidance.
key_works: Peltomäki–Whiteland (2020), [*Avoiding abelian powers cyclically*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.06307).

title: Černý’s reset-word conjecture
open: Prove every complete synchronizing deterministic \(n\)-state automaton has a reset word of length at most \((n-1)^2\).
status: Posed in 1964; the bound is attained by Černý automata. General upper bounds remain cubic.
why: Determines worst-case blind synchronization cost.
key_works: Shitov (2019), *An improvement to a recent upper bound for synchronizing words of finite automata*; Zhu (2026), [one-cluster preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19675).

title: Kolakoski density
open: Prove that the self-run-length sequence \(122112122\ldots\) has limiting frequency \(1/2\) for the symbol 1.
status: Oldenburger, 1939; Kolakoski, 1965. Even existence of the limit is unproved; liminf and limsup are tightly constrained.
why: Tests statistical regularity of a simple self-referential process.
key_works: Chvátal (1993/1994), [*Notes on the Kolakoski Sequence*](https://archive.dimacs.rutgers.edu/TechnicalReports/abstracts/1993/93-84.html).

title: Long even Barker sequences
open: Does a binary sequence of even length greater than four have every nonzero-shift aperiodic autocorrelation in \(\{-1,0,1\}\)?
status: Barker, 1953. Odd lengths beyond thirteen are excluded; severe restrictions leave the even case open.
why: Determines whether ideal binary pulse-compression sequences can be longer.
key_works: Willms (2021), [*A note on Barker sequences of even length*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.00502).

title: Asymptotic binary merit factor
open: Determine \(\limsup_n\max_a n^2/(2\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}C_k(a)^2)\) for binary sequences and their aperiodic correlations \(C_k\).
status: Littlewood–Golay problem, developed since the 1960s. Constructions reach approximately 6.34206; even finiteness of the optimum remains open.
why: Sets the ultimate aggregate sidelobe suppression of long binary signals.
key_works: Jedwab–Katz–Schmidt (2013), [*Littlewood Polynomials with Small \(L^4\) Norm*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.0260).

title: Eventual periodicity of finite octal games
open: Does every impartial take-and-break game specified by a finite octal code have an eventually periodic Sprague–Grundy sequence?
status: A longstanding Guy problem; many individual codes have certified periods, but the universal statement remains open.
why: Would reduce infinitely many heap positions to finite strategy tables.
key_works: Dailly–Duchêne–Larsson–Paris (2020), [*Partition games*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.02621); Guy–Nowakowski, [*Unsolved problems in combinatorial games*](https://library.slmath.org/books/Book71/files/GONC6-04.pdf) (edition year verify).

title: Infinite three-dimensional Chomp
open: Determine the winner from \(\mathbb N_0^3\), with poisoned origin and moves deleting a chosen point and every coordinatewise larger point.
status: Gale’s question remains unresolved; finite-board strategy stealing does not decide this infinite position.
why: Tests strategy extraction from well-founded infinite position structure.
key_works: Gale (1974), *A curious Nim-type game*; Guy–Nowakowski, [open game problems](https://library.slmath.org/books/Book71/files/GONC6-04.pdf), D1.
prize: Historical Gale offer: US$300; current administration unverified.

title: Exact logical strength of Hindman’s theorem
open: Determine the reverse-mathematical strength of Hindman’s finite-sums theorem over \(\mathsf{RCA}_0\), particularly whether \(\mathsf{ACA}_0\) proves it.
status: Blass–Hirst–Simpson placed it between \(\mathsf{ACA}_0\) and \(\mathsf{ACA}_0^+\) in 1987; the gap remains.
why: Identifies the infinitary resources required by a fundamental theorem.
key_works: Blass–Hirst–Simpson (1987), *Logical analysis of some theorems of combinatorics and topological dynamics*; Carlucci et al. (2020), [restricted Hindman principles](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.06095).

title: Positive combinatorial rule for Kronecker coefficients
open: Give a uniform positive counting rule for every symmetric-group Kronecker coefficient \(g_{\lambda\mu\nu}\), using explicitly defined finite combinatorial objects.
status: Open for decades. Special families have rules; recent two-row and rectangular results do not cover arbitrary partitions.
why: Would explain tensor-product multiplicities without cancellation.
key_works: Pak–Panova–Swanson (2025), [*A combinatorial interpretation for certain plethysm and Kronecker coefficients*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02312).

title: Positive combinatorial rule for plethysm
open: Give a general positive combinatorial formula for Schur coefficients of \(s_\lambda[s_\mu]\).
status: A longstanding problem; available rules cover restricted outer, inner, or target partitions.
why: Would make composed representation multiplicities structurally understandable.
key_works: Pak–Panova–Swanson (2025), [*A combinatorial interpretation for certain plethysm and Kronecker coefficients*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02312).

title: Foulkes’ plethysm conjecture
open: Prove that \(h_n[h_m]-h_m[h_n]\) is Schur-positive whenever \(1\le m\le n\).
status: Proposed in 1950. Many bounded-parameter and special-representation cases are established; the general comparison remains open.
why: Would impose a fundamental ordering on composed symmetric powers.
key_works: Foulkes (1950), *Concomitants of the quintic and sextic up to degree four in the coefficients of the ground form*; Gangl–Gutiérrez–Szwej (2026), [generalized divisibility cases](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.06220v3).

title: Gaussian coefficient \(q\)-Foulkes positivity
open: For \(a\le c\le d\le b\) and \(ab=cd\), prove coefficientwise nonnegativity of \(\binom{c+d}{c}_q-\binom{a+b}{a}_q\).
status: Generalized Foulkes positivity remains open. The corrected July 2026 preprint establishes divisibility cases.
why: Compares partition counts in equal-area rectangles.
key_works: Gangl–Gutiérrez–Szwej (2026), [*On the generalised Foulkes conjecture for \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)\) under divisibility conditions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.06220v3).

title: Stanley’s Jack Littlewood–Richardson positivity
open: Prove \(\langle J_\mu^{(\alpha)}J_\nu^{(\alpha)},J_\lambda^{(\alpha)}\rangle_\alpha\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}[\alpha]\), using integral Jack normalization and \(\langle p_\rho,p_\sigma\rangle_\alpha=\delta_{\rho\sigma}z_\rho\alpha^{\ell(\rho)}\).
status: Proposed in 1989. Special parameters and families are understood; general positivity remains open in the 2026 literature.
why: Would provide positive deformed multiplication and convolution laws.
key_works: Stanley (1989), [*Some combinatorial properties of Jack symmetric functions*](https://doi.org/10.1016/0001-8708(89)90015-7); Cuenca–Dołęga, [Jack generating functions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13098).

title: Combinatorial Schur expansion of modified Macdonald polynomials
open: Give an explicit positive combinatorial formula for every coefficient \(\widetilde K_{\lambda\mu}(q,t)\) in \(\widetilde H_\mu\)’s Schur expansion.
status: Haiman proved positivity geometrically in 2001; a general positive combinatorial rule is still missing.
why: Would explain two-parameter multiplicities through discrete objects.
key_works: Haiman (2001), *Hilbert schemes, polygraphs and the Macdonald positivity conjecture*; Assaf (2018), [*Toward the Schur Expansion of Macdonald Polynomials*](https://doi.org/10.37236/7419).

title: Garsia–Bergeron science-fiction conjecture
open: For corner deletions \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_k\) of \(\mu\vdash n+1\), prove the predicted Macdonald interpolation formula for the Frobenius characteristic of \(\bigcap_iV_{\lambda_i}\), including dimension \(n!/k\).
status: Originates in the 1990s. Recent shuffle identities do not establish the full module-intersection interpretation.
why: Would explain compatibility among Garsia–Haiman modules.
key_works: Kim–Lee–Oh (2025), [*Shuffle formula in science fiction for Macdonald polynomials*](https://doi.org/10.1112/S0010437X25007122).

title: Valley Delta conjecture
open: Prove that \(\Delta'_{e_{n-k-1}}e_n\) equals the prescribed weighted sum over labelled Dyck paths with \(k\) decorated contractible valleys.
status: Proposed in 2015. The rise version is proved; the valley version remains open.
why: Connects Macdonald eigenoperators to decorated parking functions.
key_works: Haglund–Remmel–Wilson (2015/2018), *The Delta conjecture*; Shin (2026), [*Exchange identities and symmetric slices of the valley Delta conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14877).

title: Symmetry of the valley Delta generating function
open: Prove symmetry in the label variables of the valley Delta generating function, independently of the full operator identity.
status: A distinct intermediate problem. Shin’s 2026 preprint proves the area-zero and area-one slices.
why: Symmetry is necessary for a representation-theoretic interpretation.
key_works: Shin (2026), [*Exchange identities and symmetric slices of the valley Delta conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14877).

title: Explicit \(q,t\)-Catalan symmetry bijection
open: Construct a direct uniform Dyck-path bijection exchanging area and bounce, or the corresponding area–dinv statistics.
status: Open since the 1990s. Algebraic symmetry and special-family bijections are known.
why: Would reveal the mechanism behind a fundamental two-statistic symmetry.
key_works: Lee–Li–Loehr (2018), [*A Combinatorial Approach to the Symmetry of \(q,t\)-Catalan Numbers*](https://doi.org/10.1137/16M1059916); Qu–Zhang, [refined variants](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08196).

title: Trivariate diagonal-harmonic dimension
open: Prove \(\dim DH_n^{(3)}=2^n(n+1)^{n-2}\), ideally identifying the predicted symmetric-group character.
status: A longstanding Haiman prediction. Corresponding Tamari enumeration is proved; identification with the trivariate module is not.
why: Extends the diagonal-harmonics correspondence to three variable sets.
key_works: Bergeron–Préville-Ratelle (2012), [*Higher Trivariate Diagonal Harmonics via generalized Tamari Posets*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.3738).

title: Exact type-\(B\) diagonal-coinvariant dimensions
open: Determine the dimension and bigraded character of \(\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_n]/\langle\mathbb C[x,y]^{B_n}_+\rangle\).
status: Studied since the 1990s. The familiar \((2n+1)^n\) lower bound is not exact generally; improved lower bounds lack matching formulas.
why: Tests how type-\(A\) phenomena extend to other reflection groups.
key_works: Ajila–Griffeth (2024), [*Representation theory and the diagonal coinvariant ring of the type B Weyl group*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.03077).

title: General positive Schubert multiplication rule
open: Give a uniform positive counting rule for all complete-flag Schubert structure constants \(c_{uv}^w\).
status: Open for decades despite geometric nonnegativity; many special descent and permutation classes have rules.
why: Would calculate intersection multiplicities using explicit discrete objects.
key_works: Gao–Zhu (2024/2025), [*Boolean Schubert Structure Coefficients*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05527); Pak–Robichaux (2025), [signed interpretations](https://doi.org/10.5802/alco.413).

title: Combinatorial invariance of Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
open: Prove that isomorphic Bruhat intervals have identical Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials, even across Coxeter groups.
status: Lusztig–Dyer, around 1983. A 2026 result proves invariance of the coefficient of \(q\), settling intervals of length at most six.
why: Would recover local intersection cohomology from abstract order data.
key_works: Barkley–Gaetz–Lam (2026), [*Combinatorial invariance for the coefficient of \(q\) in Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.07793).

title: BBDVW recurrence for arbitrary Bruhat intervals
open: Prove the hypercube-decomposition recurrence for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials of all symmetric-group Bruhat intervals.
status: Introduced in 2021. Lower intervals \([e,v]\) are settled; arbitrary lower endpoints remain open.
why: Offers a concrete recursive route toward combinatorial invariance.
key_works: Barkley–Gaetz (2026), [*The BBDVW Conjecture for Kazhdan–Lusztig Polynomials of Lower Intervals*](https://doi.org/10.1093/imrn/rnag022).

title: Vanishing density of character-table zeros
open: For independently uniform partitions \(\lambda,\mu\vdash n\), prove or refute \(\Pr[\chi^\lambda(\mu)=0]\to0\).
status: Large-scale experiments support the conjecture. Related zero-pattern theorems do not establish overall density.
why: Determines the global sparsity of symmetric-group character tables.
key_works: Miller–Scheinerman (2025), [*Large-scale Monte Carlo simulations for zeros in character tables of symmetric groups*](https://doi.org/10.1090/mcom/3964); Peluse–Soundararajan (2026), [*Zeros in the character table of the symmetric group*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28510).

title: Subpolynomially many zero-free character columns
open: If \(D(n)\) counts zero-free columns of the \(S_n\) character table, prove \(D(n)=O_\varepsilon(n^\varepsilon)\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\).
status: Conjectured in August 2026. The proved general bound is \(D(n)\ll n^{3/4}\).
why: Quantifies exceptional conjugacy classes seen nontrivially by every irreducible character.
key_works: Defant–Hariharan–Lau–Ono (2026), [*Zero-free columns in character tables of symmetric groups*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27718).

title: Natural ASM–TSSCPP bijection
open: Give a direct structural bijection between \(n\times n\) alternating-sign matrices and totally symmetric self-complementary plane partitions in the corresponding \(2n\)-box.
status: Equal enumeration is known since the 1990s; a natural general bijection remains missing.
why: Would explain a striking correspondence between integrable combinatorial models.
key_works: Holmlund–Striker, [magog matrices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03564); Bansal–Striker (2026), [*The Many Faces of Magog Matrices*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00079).

title: Exact enumeration of \(1324\)-avoiders
open: Determine a usable exact generating function or structural recurrence for all \(1324\)-avoiding permutations.
status: The outstanding length-four single-pattern enumeration problem. Recent inversion-refined formulas cover only part of the parameter range.
why: Tests the limits of permutation-class decomposition.
key_works: Linusson–Verkama (2025), [*Enumerating 1324-Avoiders with Few Inversions*](https://doi.org/10.37236/13387).

title: \(1324\) Stanley–Wilf limit
open: Determine \(L(1324)=\lim_n|\operatorname{Av}_n(1324)|^{1/n}\).
status: Existence is proved; the verified interval reported in 2025 is \(10.271<L(1324)<13.5\).
why: Gives a concrete unresolved entropy constant.
key_works: Bevan (2015), [*Permutations avoiding 1324 and patterns in Łukasiewicz paths*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.2890); Linusson–Verkama (2025), [inversion-refined enumeration](https://doi.org/10.37236/13387).

title: Inversion-refined monotonicity for \(1324\)-avoiders
open: Prove \(\operatorname{av}_n^k(1324)\le\operatorname{av}_{n+1}^k(1324)\) for every \(n,k\).
status: Proposed in 2012; verified in the region \(n\ge(k+7)/2\). General validity would improve the growth upper bound to approximately 13.002.
why: Turns refined monotonicity into a global enumeration improvement.
key_works: Claesson–Jelínek–Steingrímsson (2012), *Upper bounds for the Stanley–Wilf limit of 1324 and other layered patterns*; Linusson–Verkama (2025), [recent progress](https://doi.org/10.37236/13387).

title: Rank-unimodality of permutation-pattern intervals
open: Prove that rank sizes in every finite interval of the classical permutation-pattern poset form a unimodal sequence.
status: McNamara–Steingrímsson, 2015. The consecutive-pattern analogue is known; ordinary containment remains unresolved.
why: Would reveal regularity despite complicated interval topology.
key_works: McNamara–Steingrímsson (2015), [*On the topology of the permutation pattern poset*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcta.2015.02.009).

title: Two unrestricted stacks in series
open: Determine the generating function or asymptotic enumeration of permutations sortable by some sequence of operations through two stacks in series.
status: Studied since Tarjan’s 1972 work. This differs from the solved enumeration for two iterations of West’s deterministic stack-sorting map.
why: Measures the power of a minimal compositional storage model.
key_works: Tarjan (1972), *Sorting Using Networks of Queues and Stacks*; [*Permutations sortable by two stacks in series*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.08663).

title: \(9/16\) derangement limit for \(123\)-avoiders
open: Prove that the proportion of \(123\)-avoiders with no fixed points tends to \(9/16\).
status: Pantone’s conjecture, recorded in 2026, is supported by analysis of 200 terms; available multiple sums have not yielded the limit.
why: Would identify an exact constrained fixed-point law.
key_works: Vatter (2026), [*An assortment of problems in permutation patterns*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16355), Conjecture 4.1.

title: Vanishing derangement density for \(231\)-avoiders
open: Prove or refute that the fraction of \(231\)-avoiding permutations without fixed points tends to zero.
status: Explicitly open in Vatter’s 2026 list; continued fractions and finite computations do not establish the limit.
why: Separates fixed-point behavior in equinumerous Catalan classes.
key_works: Vatter (2026), [*An assortment of problems in permutation patterns*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16355), Question 4.2.

title: \(1/3\)–\(2/3\) balanced-pair conjecture
open: Every finite non-total poset should have incomparable \(x,y\) with \(\Pr[x<y]\in[1/3,2/3]\) under a uniform random linear extension.
status: Open since the 1960s. The classical universal constant is approximately 0.2764; a September 2026 preprint announces a strict improvement.
why: Would guarantee a balanced comparison in sorting with partial information.
key_works: Aires–Chan–Pak–Panova (2026), [*Breaking the Infinite Barrier in the \(1/3\)–\(2/3\) Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30888).

title: Symmetric chains in rectangular partition lattices
open: Decompose \(L(m,n)\), partitions inside an \(m\times n\) rectangle, into saturated chains with endpoint ranks summing to \(mn\).
status: A longstanding Stanley conjecture. Several small widths are known; a 2026 preprint supplies \(L(6,n)\).
why: Would explain Gaussian unimodality through explicit chains.
key_works: Stanley (1980), *Weyl groups, the hard Lefschetz theorem, and the Sperner property*; Wen (2026), [*\(L(6,n)\) decomposition*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23042).

title: Real-rooted Durfee polynomials
open: Prove \(D_n(z)=\sum_d p(n,d)z^d\) has only real roots, where \(p(n,d)\) counts partitions of \(n\) with Durfee-square side \(d\).
status: Conjectured in 1998. Asymptotic normality and extensive evidence do not establish real-rootedness.
why: Would impose strong regularity on the full Durfee-size distribution.
key_works: Canfield–Corteel–Savage (1998), [*Durfee Polynomials*](https://doi.org/10.37236/1370).

title: Rota’s basis conjecture
open: Rearrange \(n\) labelled bases of a rank-\(n\) matroid into \(n\) disjoint bases, each using one occurrence from every original basis.
status: Proposed in 1989. Asymptotically optimal packing and covering are known; exact \(n\)-by-\(n\) rearrangement remains open.
why: Unifies rainbow decomposition and simultaneous independence.
key_works: Montgomery–Sauermann (2025), [asymptotically tight packing and covering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05601); Arndt et al. (2026), [approximation algorithms](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.03735).

title: Gabow’s serial symmetric exchange conjecture
open: Order two disjoint bases so that swapping paired elements once each exchanges the bases while both remain bases after every step.
status: Posed in 1976. The regular-matroid case is settled; the general statement survives recent counterexamples to stronger exchange properties.
why: Would provide exceptionally short feasible reconfiguration paths.
key_works: Gabow (1976), *Decomposing symmetric exchanges in matroid bases*; Bérczi–Mátravölgyi–Schwarcz (2026), [*Reconfiguration of basis pairs in regular matroids*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jctb.2025.10.009).

title: Cyclic orderability of uniformly dense matroids
open: If \(|E|r(X)\ge r(E)|X|\) for all \(X\subseteq E\), cyclically order \(E\) so every \(r(E)\) consecutive elements form a basis.
status: Kajitani–Ueno–Miyano, 1980s. Coprime size/rank, sparse-paving, and further special cases are known.
why: Converts fractional density into sliding-window independence.
key_works: Bérczi–Jánosik–Mátravölgyi (2026), [*Cyclic Ordering of Split Matroids*](https://doi.org/10.37236/13537).

title: Cyclic orders preserving prescribed basis blocks
open: Given a partition into matroid bases, find a cyclic order keeping each basis contiguous and making every rank-sized window a basis.
status: Explicitly proposed in recent split-matroid work; proved for split matroids, open generally.
why: Allows continuously interchangeable feasible batches without destroying their grouping.
key_works: Bérczi–Jánosik–Mátravölgyi (2026), [*Cyclic Ordering of Split Matroids*](https://doi.org/10.37236/13537), Conjecture 3.

title: List coloring the intersection of two matroids
open: Prove \(\chi_\ell(M_1\cap M_2)=\chi(M_1\cap M_2)\), where each color class must be independent in both matroids.
status: A longstanding extension of matroid list coloring. A factor-two upper bound and special partition-matroid cases are known.
why: Would eliminate extra cost from item-specific eligibility.
key_works: Aharoni–Berger–Guo–Kotlar (2024), [*Coloring, list coloring, and fractional coloring in intersections of matroids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.08789).

title: Infinite matroid intersection
open: For arbitrary matroids \(M,N\) on possibly infinite \(E\), find common independent \(I=I_M\sqcup I_N\) with \(\operatorname{cl}_M(I_M)\cup\operatorname{cl}_N(I_N)=E\).
status: Nash-Williams, around 1990. Significant special cases and new augmentation tools leave the unrestricted statement open.
why: Extends min–max duality beyond finite cardinality arguments.
key_works: Bowler (2018), [survey](https://matroidunion.org/?p=2374); Joó (2025), [*Hindrance from a wasteful common independent set*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.04342).

title: Weak White quadratic generation
open: Prove that every matroid basis toric ideal is generated by arbitrary quadratic binomials.
status: White, 1980. Symmetric-exchange generation was refuted in July 2026; arbitrary quadratic generation explicitly remains open.
why: Would bound relation complexity despite failure of the stronger exchange rule.
key_works: White (1980), [*A unique exchange property for bases*](https://doi.org/10.1016/0024-3795(80)90209-8); Larson (2026), [*Counterexamples to two conjectures about matroids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.02208).

title: Koszulness of every matroid base ring
open: Determine whether every matroid base ring is Koszul, meaning its residue field has a linear minimal free resolution.
status: Asked by Herzog–Hibi in 2002. Quadratic Gröbner bases need not exist, but Koszulness remains open, including for the Fano base ring.
why: Constrains all higher syzygies of matroid toric varieties.
key_works: Backman–Cheung–Lasoń–Liu–Michałek (2026), [*The Gröbner Version of White’s Conjecture is False*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13960).

title: Quadratic Gröbner basis for \(T_8\)
open: Decide whether the rank-four, eight-element matroid \(T_8\) has a quadratic Gröbner basis for its basis toric ideal.
status: Isolated in June 2026 after a computational classification settled the other eight-element Fano/dual-Fano-minor-free cases.
why: Tests the boundary of the first known algebraic obstructions.
key_works: Backman et al. (2026), [*The Gröbner Version of White’s Conjecture is False*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13960), Problem 6.3.

title: Stanley’s pure-\(O\)-sequence conjecture
open: Realize every matroid independence-complex \(h\)-vector as the degree sequence of a finite pure monomial order ideal.
status: Proposed in 1977. Numerous classes are settled; 2026 relaxed-coparking constructions retain an unresolved fibre-existence condition.
why: Would give an exact discrete model for matroid Hilbert functions.
key_works: Oh (2026), [*Relaxed coparking functions and Stanley’s conjecture for matroid \(h\)-vectors*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17446).

title: Real-rootedness of matroid \(Z\)-polynomials
open: Prove \(Z_M(t)=\sum_Ft^{r(F)}P_{M/F}(t)\) has only real roots for every matroid.
status: Proudfoot–Xu–Young, 2010s. Sparse paving matroids were settled in a September 2026 preprint; the general case remains open.
why: Strengthens cohomological positivity to global root control.
key_works: Xie–Zhang (2026), [*Real-rootedness of the \(Z\)-polynomials of sparse paving matroids and strict interlacing for uniform matroids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.07636).

title: Points–lines–planes inequality
open: Prove \(W_2^2\ge W_1W_3\) for every simple matroid, where \(W_i\) counts rank-\(i\) flats.
status: A low-rank remnant of Mason’s 1972 conjectures. The 2026 high-rank counterexample to general flat-count log-concavity does not settle it.
why: Tests whether local incidence retains log-concavity.
key_works: Seymour (1995), *On the points-lines-planes conjecture*; Larson (2026), [matroid counterexamples](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.02208).

title: Almost all matroids are sparse paving
open: Prove \(s_n/m_n\to1\), where \(s_n\) counts labelled sparse paving matroids and \(m_n\) all labelled matroids.
status: Formalized in 2011. Only logarithmic equivalence, \(\log s_n/\log m_n\to1\), is established.
why: Would identify the typical finite independence system.
key_works: Pendavingh–van der Pol (2015), [*On the number of matroids compared to the number of sparse paving matroids*](https://research.tue.nl/en/publications/on-the-number-of-matroids-compared-to-the-number-of-sparse-paving-2/).

title: Leading constant in matroid enumeration
open: Determine \(\log_2m_n\) to relative error \(1+o(1)\), especially its coefficient of \(n^{-1}\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\).
status: Knuth’s lower construction and later upper bounds leave the coefficient between one and \(2+o(1)\).
why: Determines the entropy of finite matroids.
key_works: Knuth (1974), *The asymptotic number of geometries*; Bansal–Pendavingh–van der Pol (2013/2015), [*On the number of matroids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.6270).

title: Hadamard existence conjecture
open: Construct a sign matrix \(H\) of order \(4m\) satisfying \(HH^{\mathsf T}=4mI\), for every positive integer \(m\).
status: Usually dated to Paley, 1933. Extensive infinite constructions and finite databases do not establish every admissible order.
why: Supplies optimal orthogonal signals, designs, and codes.
key_works: Paley (1933), *On orthogonal matrices*; Cati–Pasechnik (2024/2025), [*A database of constructions of Hadamard matrices*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.18897).

title: Skew-Hadamard existence
open: Construct a Hadamard matrix of every order \(4m\) satisfying \(H+H^{\mathsf T}=2I\).
status: A longstanding strengthening of ordinary existence; known skew constructions do not cover every admissible order.
why: Connects orthogonal matrices to regular directed incidence structures.
key_works: Cati–Pasechnik (2024/2025), [*A database of constructions of Hadamard matrices*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.18897).

title: Circulant Hadamard conjecture
open: Prove that no circulant Hadamard matrix has order greater than four.
status: Ryser, 1960s. Arithmetic and field-descent restrictions exclude enormous ranges without proving universal nonexistence.
why: Would establish a sharp limit on perfectly orthogonal periodic binary signals.
key_works: Leung–Schmidt (2012), [*New restrictions on possible orders of circulant Hadamard matrices*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10623-011-9493-1); Borwein–Mossinghoff (2013), [*Wieferich pairs and Barker sequences, II*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.0045).

title: Ryser’s odd-order transversal conjecture
open: Prove that every odd-order Latin square has a full transversal.
status: Proposed in 1967. Near-transversals and almost-everywhere transversal decompositions do not settle every odd-order square.
why: Would guarantee simultaneous distinctness in rows, columns, and symbols.
key_works: Montgomery (2024), [*Transversals in Latin Squares*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.19873); Bowtell–Montgomery (2025), [almost-everywhere decomposition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.05438).

title: Remaining finite cases of Brualdi–Stein
open: Prove that every Latin square of every order \(n\) has a partial transversal of size \(n-1\).
status: The sufficiently-large-\(n\) case is proved; eliminating all remaining finite exceptions is unresolved.
why: Converts an asymptotic guarantee into an exact all-order theorem.
