key_works: Stein (1975), *Transversals of Latin squares and their generalizations*; Montgomery (2024), [*Transversals in Latin Squares*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.19873).

title: Three mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order ten
open: Construct three pairwise orthogonal Latin squares of order ten, or certify nonexistence.
status: A pair has been known since 1959. Restricted SAT investigations in 2026 leave the unrestricted triple open.
why: Tests the first unresolved improvement in a fundamental orthogonal-design table.
key_works: Bright–Keita–Stevens (2026), [*Myrvold’s Results on Orthogonal Triples of \(10\times10\) Latin Squares: A SAT Investigation*](https://doi.org/10.37236/13960).

title: Alon–Tarsi Latin-square parity conjecture
open: Prove that the signed sum of order-\(n\) Latin squares is nonzero for every even \(n\), equivalently that \([\prod_{ij}x_{ij}](\det X)^n\ne0\).
status: Proposed in 1992. Orders \(p-1\) and \(p+1\), for odd primes \(p\), are established.
why: Supplies powerful algebraic certificates for decomposition existence.
key_works: Alon–Tarsi (1992), *Colorings and orientations of graphs*; Xu (2026), [Weingarten-calculus formulation](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/6g574562).

title: Minimum critical sets in Latin squares
open: Prove that the smallest minimal uniquely completable partial Latin square of order \(n\) has \(\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor\) entries.
status: Conjectured from 1979 onward. A positive constant times \(n^2\) lower bound is known, far from \(1/4\).
why: Determines the least information that uniquely specifies a Latin square.
key_works: Hatami–Qian (2016), [*Teaching dimension, VC dimension, and critical sets in Latin squares*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.00032).

title: Finiteness of biplanes
open: Determine whether only finitely many nontrivial symmetric \(2\)-\((v,k,2)\) designs exist.
status: A longstanding fixed-\(\lambda\) design problem; known examples and symmetry classifications do not give a universal bound.
why: Would distinguish projective-plane abundance from repeated-pair symmetric designs.
key_works: Kaski–Östergård (2008), [*There are exactly five biplanes with \(k=11\)*](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcd.20145); Chen et al. (2025/2026), [double Hall graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10903).

title: Existence of \(S(3,5,41)\)
open: Construct 1,066 five-element blocks on 41 points so that every triple occurs exactly once, or prove impossibility.
status: A longstanding admissible parameter gap retained in the 2025–2026 construction table.
why: Fills an early unresolved small Steiner-system case.
key_works: Kiermaier–Krčadinac–Wassermann, [*Steiner 3-designs as extensions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23483); [maintained table](https://web.math.pmf.unizg.hr/~krcko/results/steiner3.html).

title: Existence of \(S(3,6,46)\)
open: Construct 759 six-element blocks on 46 points with every triple covered exactly once, or prove nonexistence.
status: Arithmetic conditions hold, but the 2025–2026 table leaves existence unresolved.
why: Tests the gap between admissibility and realizability.
key_works: Kiermaier–Krčadinac–Wassermann, [*Steiner 3-designs as extensions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23483); [construction table](https://web.math.pmf.unizg.hr/~krcko/results/steiner3.html).

title: Prime-power order conjecture
open: Prove that every finite projective plane has prime-power order, or construct a counterexample.
status: Open for decades. Order ten is excluded; order twelve remains unresolved despite strong automorphism restrictions.
why: Asks whether finite-field arithmetic controls the existence spectrum.
key_works: Lam (1991), *The search for a finite projective plane of order 10*; Akiyama–Suetake–Tanaka (2023), [order-twelve restrictions](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcd.21869).

title: Uniqueness of prime-order projective planes
open: Prove every plane of prime order \(p\) is isomorphic to \(\mathrm{PG}(2,p)\), or produce a non-Desarguesian example.
status: A longstanding conjecture. Coding-theoretic uniqueness under extra weight-enumerator hypotheses does not settle the unrestricted statement.
why: Would establish rigidity at prime orders.
key_works: Bagchi (2019), [*A coding theoretic approach to the uniqueness conjecture for projective planes of prime order*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10623-019-00623-y).

title: Binary \(q\)-Fano plane
open: Construct 381 three-dimensional subspaces of \(\mathbb F_2^7\), each two-dimensional subspace lying in exactly one, or prove impossibility.
status: Decades of structural restrictions and partial constructions have not settled existence.
why: Resolves the first vector-space analogue of the Fano plane.
key_works: Honold–Kiermaier (2015), [putative \(q\)-Fano planes](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.06688); Kiermaier (2021), [alpha-points](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.00365).

title: Classification of hyperovals
open: Classify all \((q+2)\)-point sets in \(\mathrm{PG}(2,q)\), \(q\) even, with no three collinear, up to projective semilinear equivalence.
status: Many infinite and exceptional families are known; low-degree polynomial classifications do not cover arbitrary hyperovals.
why: Classifies extremal arcs and associated optimal codes.
key_works: Caullery–Schmidt (2015), [*On the classification of hyperovals*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aim.2015.07.016).

title: Classification of even-characteristic ovoids
open: Classify all \((q^2+1)\)-point caps in \(\mathrm{PG}(3,q)\) for even \(q\).
status: Elliptic quadrics and Tits ovoids are known; the general even-characteristic classification remains open.
why: Controls extremal finite incidence structures and projective codes.
key_works: Tits (1962), *Ovoides et groupes de Suzuki*; Hirschfeld–Thas (2025), [*Arcs, Caps and Generalisations in a Finite Projective Space*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.06243).

title: Regularity of pseudo-ovals
open: Must every pseudo-oval of \(q^n+1\) mutually disjoint \((n-1)\)-spaces in \(\mathrm{PG}(3n-1,q)\), any three spanning, arise by field reduction?
status: All known examples are regular; positive theorems require additional spread hypotheses.
why: Asks whether a larger geometric category contains fundamentally new objects.
key_works: Hirschfeld–Thas (2025), [*Arcs, Caps and Generalisations in a Finite Projective Space*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.06243), Open Problem 3.

title: Linearity of small minimal blocking sets
open: Prove every minimal \(k\)-blocking set in \(\mathrm{PG}(n,q)\) of size below \(3(q^k+1)/2\) is a linear set over a subfield.
status: Cubic-field cases and dimension reductions are established; general prime-power cases remain.
why: Would derive algebraic structure from a small incidence condition.
key_works: Van de Voorde (2010), [higher-dimensional reductions](https://biblio.ugent.be/publication/2917400); Lavrauw–Storme–Van de Voorde (2011), [cubic-field theorem](https://biblio.ugent.be/publication/1261642).

title: Linear MDS conjecture over nonprime fields
open: Prove linear \([N,k]\) MDS codes over \(\mathbb F_q\), \(2\le k\le q-1\), satisfy \(N\le q+1\), except the known even-\(q\) exceptions permitting \(q+2\).
status: Prime fields are settled. A 2026 preprint extends the odd-characteristic dimension range but leaves unrestricted extension fields.
why: Determines maximum length of optimally redundant linear erasure codes.
key_works: Ball–Lavrauw (2020), [*Arcs in finite projective spaces*](https://doi.org/10.4171/EMSS/33); Fan (2026), [linear-in-\(q\) range](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03740).

title: Exact binary rate–distance tradeoff
open: Determine \(R_2(\delta)=\limsup_n n^{-1}\log_2 A_2(n,\lceil\delta n\rceil)\).
status: Gilbert–Varshamov lower bounds and linear-programming upper bounds still leave exponential gaps.
why: Establishes the packing capacity of binary Hamming space.
key_works: Coregliano–Jeronimo–Jones–Linial–Loyfer (2026), [*Higher-Order Delsarte Dual LPs: Lifting, Constructions and Completeness*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITCS.2026.44).

title: Explicit binary codes meeting Gilbert–Varshamov
open: Deterministically construct binary linear codes of relative distance \(\delta\) and rate at least \(1-H_2(\delta)-\varepsilon\), in polynomial blocklength time.
status: Random codes achieve the existential target. Recent trace-code approaches require stronger character-sum estimates.
why: Would make the probabilistic benchmark reproducibly constructible.
key_works: Cohen–Doron–Goldgraber–Manket (2026), [*Tracing AG Codes: Toward Meeting the Gilbert–Varshamov Bound*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.08788).

title: Asymptotically good binary cyclic codes
open: Can binary cyclic linear codes have both rate and relative distance bounded below by positive constants along unbounded lengths?
status: Open since the 1960s. Good quasi-cyclic constructions do not settle cyclic codes.
why: Tests compatibility of maximal shift symmetry with efficient error correction.
key_works: Aliabadi–Kalaycı–Zadehdabbagh (2026), [*Asymptotic performance of double circulant and four circulant codes with small hull dimension*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s12095-025-00861-z).

title: Extremal binary self-dual code of length 72
open: Construct a doubly even self-dual binary \([72,36,16]\) code, or prove none exists.
status: Sloane, 1973. Known examples reach distance 12; extensive symmetry restrictions do not decide distance 16.
why: Resolves a central finite code parameter with design and lattice consequences.
key_works: Sloane (1973), [*Is there a \((72,36)\), \(d=16\) self-dual code?*](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1973.1054975); Hannusch–Major (2025), [small automorphism groups](https://www.preprints.org/manuscript/202506.2100).

title: Optimal unit-distance growth
open: Determine the largest possible number of unit-distance pairs among \(n\) planar points, to matching asymptotic scale.
status: The old \(n^{1+o(1)}\) conjecture was refuted in 2026. Sawin gives \(n^{1.014}\) constructions; the general upper scale remains \(n^{4/3}\).
why: Identifies the correct planar incidence exponent.
key_works: Sawin (2026), [*An explicit lower bound for the unit distance problem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20579); Guth (2026), [survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10791).

title: Sharp Erdős distinct-distance bound
open: Prove every \(n\)-point planar set determines \(\Omega(n/\sqrt{\log n})\) distinct distances.
status: Erdős, 1946. Guth–Katz prove \(\Omega(n/\log n)\); lattice constructions give the conjectured upper scale.
why: Would close the remaining logarithmic gap in planar distance diversity.
key_works: Guth–Katz (2015), [*On the Erdős distinct distance problem in the plane*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.4105).

title: Hadwiger–Nelson problem
open: Determine the chromatic number of the plane when points one unit apart must have different colors.
status: The current interval is five to seven; de Grey established the lower bound five in 2018.
why: Connects finite coloring obstructions to Euclidean geometry.
key_works: de Grey (2018), [*The chromatic number of the plane is at least 5*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.02385).

title: Exact Erdős–Szekeres convex-polygon numbers
open: Prove that \(2^{k-2}+1\) planar points in general position force \(k\) in convex position.
status: Proposed in 1935. Exact cases through \(k=6\) and asymptotic \(2^{k+o(k)}\) bounds are known; \(k\ge7\) remains open.
why: Determines exact unavoidable convex structure.
key_works: Suk (2017), [*On the Erdős–Szekeres convex polygon problem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.08657); Holmsen–Mojarrad–Pach–Tardos (2020), [*Two extensions of the Erdős–Szekeres problem*](https://ems.press/journals/jems/articles/17088).

title: Heilbronn’s triangle-area asymptotics
open: Determine the largest achievable minimum triangle area among \(n\) points in a unit square.
status: Open since the 1940s. Known lower scale is \((\log n)/n^2\); recent upper bounds reach \(n^{-7/6+o(1)}\).
why: Quantifies unavoidable near-collinearity.
key_works: Cohen–Pohoata–Zakharov (2024), [*Lower bounds for incidences*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07658); [earlier triangle-area work](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18253).

title: Planar \(k\)-set complexity
open: Determine the maximum number of \(k\)-element subsets of an \(n\)-point planar set separable by a line.
status: Decades-old gap. Dey’s upper bound is \(O(nk^{1/3})\); known lower constructions are substantially smaller.
why: Controls levels in arrangements and geometric selection complexity.
key_works: Dey (1998), *Improved bounds on planar k-sets and related problems*; [The Open Problems Project, problem 7](https://topp.openproblem.net/p7).

title: Danzer’s finite-density hitting set
open: Does a set of finite upper density in \(\mathbb R^d\), \(d\ge2\), intersect every convex body of volume one?
status: Open since the 1960s. Dense forests and weaker visibility constructions do not solve Danzer’s condition.
why: Would give a sparse universal geometric sampling set.
key_works: Adiceam (2020), [*Around the Danzer Problem and the Construction of Dense Forests*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.06756).

title: Levi–Hadwiger illumination conjecture
open: Prove every convex body in \(\mathbb R^d\) can be illuminated by at most \(2^d\) directions.
status: Proposed in the mid-twentieth century; the unrestricted case remains open even in dimension three.
why: Determines universal covering and illumination complexity.
key_works: Arman–Kaire–Prymak (2026), [*Illumination number of 3-dimensional cap bodies*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2026.115025).

title: Complex illumination conjecture
open: Prove that every unit ball of a complex norm on \(\mathbb C^d\) can be illuminated by at most \(2^{d+1}-1\) directions.
status: Proposed in 2024, published in 2026. Complex zonoid and other special cases are settled.
why: Identifies how complex symmetry changes covering complexity.
key_works: Rotem–Schejter–Slomka (2026), [*The complex Illumination problem*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00493-025-00195-7).

title: Fractional complex illumination
open: Prove that the fractional illumination number of every complex norm ball in \(\mathbb C^d\) is at most \(2^d\).
status: Proposed in 2024. Known complex-zonoid results leave arbitrary norm balls unresolved.
why: Seeks the sharp weighted relaxation of complex illumination.
key_works: Rotem–Schejter–Slomka (2026), [*The complex Illumination problem*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00493-025-00195-7), Conjecture 1.2.

title: Borsuk’s problem in four dimensions
open: Determine the least \(b(4)\) such that every bounded subset of \(\mathbb R^4\) partitions into \(b(4)\) smaller-diameter pieces.
status: The remaining interval is \(5\le b(4)\le8\), following a 2026 upper-bound preprint.
why: Resolves a low-dimensional frontier after high-dimensional counterexamples.
key_works: Tolmachev–Voronov (2026), [*Reducing the upper bound for the Borsuk number in \(\mathbb R^4\) to 8*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19068).

title: Five-dimensional kissing number
open: Determine the maximum number of unit spheres simultaneously tangent to another unit sphere in \(\mathbb R^5\).
status: The verified interval remains 40–44. Recent constructions produce inequivalent 40-point configurations without closing it.
why: Resolves the next low-dimensional exact sphere-contact problem.
key_works: Cohn–Rajagopal (2026), [*Variations on Five-Dimensional Sphere Packings*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-026-00841-x).

title: Lebesgue’s universal covering constant
open: Determine the minimum area of a convex planar set containing an isometric copy of every diameter-one planar set.
status: Open since 1914. Bounds are approximately 0.832 to 0.8440935944.
why: Determines the smallest universal geometric container.
key_works: Gibbs (2018), [*An Upper Bound for Lebesgue’s Covering Problem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.10089); Arman et al. (2025), [covering bounds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.04023).

title: Convex Moser worm problem
open: Determine the minimum area of a convex planar set containing every unit-length planar arc, up to rigid motion.
status: Open since the 1960s. A September 2026 preprint reports bounds approximately 0.239–0.24633.
why: Finds the optimal universal container for flexible one-dimensional objects.
key_works: Keller (2026), [*Improved bounds for universal convex covers of unit arcs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21968).

title: Shortest opaque barrier for a square
open: Determine the minimum total length of a planar barrier meeting every line that intersects a unit square.
status: A longstanding opacity problem; improved lower bounds still do not match the best barriers.
why: Measures the minimum material needed for omnidirectional obstruction.
key_works: Kiderlen–Pausinger (2025), [*Explicit lower bounds for opaque sets of unit square and unit disc*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08842).

title: Dürer’s edge-unfolding conjecture
open: Cut every convex polyhedron along a spanning tree of edges so its faces unfold into a nonoverlapping planar polygon.
status: The underlying question is centuries old. General unfoldings and affine-transformation results do not settle edge-only unfolding.
why: Guarantees fabrication patterns for arbitrary convex polyhedra.
key_works: O’Rourke (2019), [edge-unfolding discussion](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.07152); [The Open Problems Project, problem 9](https://topp.openproblem.net/p9).

title: Geometric tetrahedral flip connectivity
open: Are the geometric triangulations of every finite point set in \(\mathbb R^3\) connected through valid bistellar flips?
status: Open even for important restricted configurations; higher-dimensional disconnected examples do not settle three dimensions.
why: Determines whether local retriangulation can explore every tetrahedral mesh.
key_works: [The Open Problems Project, problem 28](https://topp.openproblem.net/p28); Wagner–Welzl (2022), [triangulation study](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-022-00436-2).

title: Voronoi diagrams of lines in three dimensions
open: Determine the maximum combinatorial complexity of the Euclidean Voronoi diagram of \(n\) lines in \(\mathbb R^3\).
status: Quadratic lower bounds and essentially cubic upper bounds remain separated; near-quadratic growth is conjectured.
why: Controls basic proximity computation for spatial line structures.
key_works: Sharir (1994), relevant envelope bounds; [The Open Problems Project, problem 3](https://topp.openproblem.net/p3).

title: Polynomial-time sum-of-square-roots comparison
open: Decide the sign of a difference of sums of square roots of binary-encoded integers in polynomial time.
status: Studied since at least the 1980s; exact arithmetic complexity remains unresolved.
why: Removes a foundational bottleneck in exact geometric optimization.
key_works: Burnikel–Fleischer–Mehlhorn–Schirra (2000), separation bounds; [The Open Problems Project, problem 33](https://topp.openproblem.net/p33).

title: Uniform quadratic-time sorting of \(X+Y\)
open: Given two \(n\)-element real sets, sort all \(n^2\) pairwise sums in uniform \(O(n^2)\) time.
status: Fredman’s 1976 comparison-tree bound is quadratic; a uniform algorithm attaining it remains unknown.
why: Separates comparison complexity from executable algorithmic complexity.
key_works: Fredman (1976), *How good is the information theory bound in sorting?*; [The Open Problems Project, problem 41](https://topp.openproblem.net/p41).

title: Polynomial Hirsch conjecture
open: Bound every \(d\)-polytope’s graph diameter by a polynomial in its number of facets, uniformly in dimension.
status: The original linear Hirsch conjecture is false; general polynomial diameter remains unproved.
why: Would constrain the combinatorial difficulty of navigating linear programs.
key_works: Kalai–Kleitman (1992), *A quasi-polynomial bound for the diameter of graphs of polyhedra*; Santos (2012), [*A counterexample to the Hirsch conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.2814).

title: Oda’s integer-decomposition conjecture
open: Prove every smooth lattice polytope \(P\) has the integer-decomposition property: every lattice point of \(kP\) is a sum of \(k\) lattice points of \(P\).
status: Posed in 1997. Numerous classes and low-dimensional cases are known.
why: Connects local smoothness to global integral decomposability.
key_works: Hofscheier–Kasprzyk (2025), [*Is there a smooth lattice polytope which does not have the integer decomposition property?*](https://doi.org/10.14760/SNAP-2025-008-EN).

title: Koszulness of smooth lattice polytopes
open: Prove that the lattice-point semigroup algebra of every smooth lattice polytope is Koszul.
status: Bøgvad’s longstanding conjecture; extensive special-family results leave the general case open.
why: Would tightly control syzygies of smooth toric embeddings.
key_works: Beck–Delgado–Gubeladze–Michałek (2015), [*Very ample and Koszul segmental fibrations*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.7422).

title: Unimodular triangulations of smooth polytopes
open: Does every smooth lattice polytope admit a unimodular triangulation?
status: Known for many classes; general dilation theorems do not supply a triangulation of the original polytope.
why: Would give exact lattice decompositions and squarefree algebraic degenerations.
key_works: Haase–Paffenholz–Piechnik–Santos (2021), [*Existence of unimodular triangulations—positive results*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.1687).

title: Oda’s mixed Minkowski-sum question
open: If \(Q\) is smooth and its normal fan refines that of lattice polytope \(P\), must every lattice point in \(P+Q\) split as a lattice point of each summand?
status: A longstanding mixed strengthening; known special cases do not settle arbitrary smooth \(Q\).
why: Governs multiplication of ample and nef toric sections.
key_works: Crespo–Pelayo–Santos (2026), [*Ewald’s Conjecture and integer points in algebraic and symplectic toric geometry*](https://doi.org/10.1112/plms.70144).

title: Ewald’s symmetric lattice-basis conjecture
open: Prove that \(P\cap(-P)\) contains a lattice basis whenever \(P\) is a smooth reflexive lattice polytope.
status: Proposed in 1988. Verified through dimension seven and for further infinite families; arbitrary dimensions remain open.
why: Would force strong lattice symmetry from toric smoothness.
key_works: Crespo–Pelayo–Santos (2026), [*Ewald’s Conjecture and integer points in algebraic and symplectic toric geometry*](https://doi.org/10.1112/plms.70144).

title: Gal’s gamma-nonnegativity conjecture
open: Prove the gamma-vector is nonnegative for every flag homology sphere.
status: Proposed in 2005 after stronger real-rootedness failed; many low-dimensional and structured cases are settled.
why: Would reveal hidden positivity in face enumeration.
key_works: Gal (2005), [*Real Root Conjecture fails for five and higher dimensional spheres*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0501046).

title: Charney–Davis conjecture
open: For every flag homology \((2d-1)\)-sphere, prove \((-1)^d h(-1)\ge0\).
status: Proposed in 1995. Low-dimensional cases are known; higher-dimensional generality remains open.
why: Connects face enumeration to curvature and Euler-characteristic signs.
key_works: Charney–Davis (1995), [*The Euler characteristic of a nonpositively curved, piecewise Euclidean manifold*](https://people.math.osu.edu/davis.12/old_papers/euler95.pdf).

title: Nevo–Petersen realization of gamma-vectors
open: Realize gamma-vectors of flag homology spheres as face vectors of simplicial complexes, ideally balanced complexes.
status: Proposed in the late 2000s. Barycentric subdivisions and other classes are established.
why: Would turn gamma-positivity into an explicit combinatorial realization.
key_works: Nevo–Petersen (2011), [*On gamma-vectors satisfying the Kruskal–Katona inequalities*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.0694); [balanced realizations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1003.2544).

title: Bárány–Larman colored Tverberg conjecture
open: Partition \(d+1\) color classes of \(r\) points in \(\mathbb R^d\) into \(r\) rainbow tuples whose convex hulls intersect.
status: Proposed in 1992. A September 2026 preprint proves the prime-\(r\) topological case; general affine composite cases remain.
why: Would give the optimal balanced colorful intersection theorem.
key_works: Bárány–Larman (1992), [colored Tverberg theorem](https://doi.org/10.1112/jlms/s2-45.2.314); Soberón (2026), [prime-number theorem](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37876).

title: Sierksma’s Tverberg-partition count
open: Prove every \((r-1)(d+1)+1\)-point configuration in \(\mathbb R^d\) has at least \(((r-1)!)^d\) Tverberg partitions.
status: A longstanding strengthening of existence; special parameter cases are known.
why: Quantifies the minimum abundance of intersecting partitions.
key_works: Soberón (2026), [*An elementary proof of Sierksma’s conjecture for seven points in the plane*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18485).

title: Zeeman’s collapsibility conjecture
open: Does every finite contractible two-dimensional complex \(K\) have a collapsible triangulation of \(K\times I\)?
status: Proposed in 1963. Results using more interval factors and reductions to special polyhedra do not settle one factor.
why: Would connect contractibility to explicit combinatorial simplification.
key_works: Adiprasito–Benedetti, [products and collapsibility](https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.6606); Dynnikov (2026), [*On Zeeman’s collapsibility conjecture for non-standard polyhedra*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23331).

title: Komlós vector-balancing conjecture
open: For vectors \(v_i\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(\|v_i\|_2\le1\), choose signs so \(\|\sum_i\varepsilon_i v_i\|_\infty\le C\), with absolute \(C\).
status: Open since the 1960s. Recent bounds reach \(O((\log n)^{1/4}(\log\log n)^{7/4})\).
why: Would establish dimension-independent discrepancy rounding.
key_works: Bansal–Jiang, [*Decoupling via Affine Spectral-Independence*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03961); [2026 exposition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.28452).

title: Beck–Fiala in the remaining sparse regime
open: Prove discrepancy \(O(\sqrt t)\) for every set system in which each element belongs to at most \(t\) sets.
status: Proposed in 1981. Recent work resolves \(t\ge\log^2 n\); the full sparse regime remains open.
why: Would make discrepancy depend optimally on column sparsity.
key_works: Bansal–Jiang (2025/2026), [*Decoupling via Affine Spectral-Independence: Beck–Fiala and Komlós Bounds Beyond Banaszczyk*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03961).

title: Tusnády’s box-discrepancy problem
open: Determine the worst-case discrepancy of axis-parallel boxes on \(n\) points in fixed dimension \(d\).
status: The 2026 monograph records lower \(\Omega(\log^{d-1}n)\) and upper \(O(\log^{d-1/2}n)\) bounds.
why: Controls geometric sampling and range-counting error.
key_works: Nikolov (2017), [*Tighter Bounds for the Discrepancy of Boxes and Polytopes*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.05532); Bansal–Nikolov (2026), [*Discrepancy Theory*](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.00140v1).

title: Optimal star-discrepancy exponent
open: Determine the logarithmic exponent in the minimum star discrepancy of \(n\) points in \([0,1]^d\), for each fixed \(d\ge3\).
status: Classical lower and upper powers of \(\log n\) remain separated; dimension two behaves differently.
why: Would identify optimal deterministic integration accuracy.
key_works: Clément–Doerr–Klamroth–Paquete (2025), [*Searching permutations for constructing uniformly distributed point sets*](https://doi.org/10.1090/bproc/254).

title: Scalable certificates for optimal discrepancy point sets
open: Develop globally certified star-discrepancy optimization reaching roughly ten times the currently certified point counts under fixed precision and resource budgets.
status: Proposed engineering target. Published exact certificates reach 21 points in dimension two and eight in dimension three.
why: Would turn numerical sampling designs into provably optimal configurations.
key_works: Clément–Doerr–Klamroth–Paquete (2025), [*Searching permutations for constructing uniformly distributed point sets*](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12002279/).

title: Strongly polynomial linear programming
open: Solve arbitrary rational linear programs with an operation count polynomial in dimensions and constraints, independent of coefficient bit lengths.
status: Open for decades; weakly polynomial algorithms do not meet this requirement.
why: Would resolve a central complexity question in optimization.
key_works: Smale (1998), *Mathematical problems for the next century*; [The Open Problems Project, problem 8](https://topp.openproblem.net/p8).

title: Approximate counting of bipartite independent sets
open: Determine whether unrestricted \(\#\mathrm{BIS}\) admits a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme.
status: A central unresolved approximate-counting problem; bounded-degree and uniqueness-region results do not settle arbitrary bipartite graphs.
why: Would classify a major intermediate family of counting problems.
key_works: Chen–Liu–Yin (2023), [*Uniqueness and Rapid Mixing in the Bipartite Hardcore Model*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00186).

title: Deterministic FPTAS for the nonnegative permanent
open: Approximate every nonnegative matrix permanent within relative error \(\varepsilon\), deterministically in time polynomial in input size and \(1/\varepsilon\).
status: A randomized scheme exists. September 2026 work improves deterministic approximation factors but does not give an FPTAS.
why: Would derandomize a landmark approximate-counting algorithm.
key_works: Kudria–Luo–Majid (2026), [*Subexponential Approximation of the Permanent in Deterministic Polynomial Time*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10516).

title: FPRAS for perfect matchings in general graphs
open: Approximately count perfect matchings in arbitrary nonbipartite graphs in randomized polynomial time.
status: Bipartite graphs are settled; direct extensions can mix torpidly, while restricted nonbipartite cases are known.
why: Would extend efficient approximation to general dimer systems.
key_works: Štefankovič–Vigoda–Wilmes (2017), [*On Counting Perfect Matchings in General Graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.07504).

title: Four-thirds subtour-LP conjecture
open: Prove the metric symmetric-TSP subtour relaxation has integrality gap at most \(4/3\).
status: Lower examples approach \(4/3\); the best general upper bound is below \(3/2\) but remains larger.
why: Would expose the exact strength of the standard TSP relaxation.
key_works: Karlin–Klein–Oveis Gharan (2021), [*A (Slightly) Improved Bound on the Integrality Gap of the Subtour LP for TSP*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.10043).

title: Constant additive gap for bin packing
open: Bound the integral optimum minus the configuration-LP optimum by an absolute constant.
status: The known general additive bound is \(O(\log\mathrm{OPT})\); constant loss remains open.
why: Would nearly eliminate rounding waste in packing and cutting stock.
key_works: Hoberg–Rothvoss (2017), [*A Logarithmic Additive Integrality Gap for Bin Packing*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.08796).

title: Zigzag fluctuations of random-graph chromatic number
open: Determine the fluctuation scale and limiting distributions of \(\chi(G(n,1/2))\) across all \(n\), including the predicted oscillating scale.
status: Large fluctuations along subsequences are proved; a complete all-\(n\) law is missing.
why: Describes the irregular uncertainty of a basic random optimization parameter.
key_works: Heckel–Riordan (2021/2023), [*How does the chromatic number of a random graph vary?*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14014).

title: Exact independence density of random regular graphs
open: Determine the limiting maximum-independent-set density in random \(d\)-regular graphs for fixed degrees such as \(d=3\).
status: Limits and increasingly sharp bounds are known; exact fixed-degree values and general replica predictions remain unproved.
why: Would validate sparse disordered-optimization predictions.
key_works: Harangi (2023), [replica-symmetry-breaking bounds](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10955-022-03062-7); [2025 refinement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09458).

title: Planted clique below the square-root scale
open: Find a polynomial-time algorithm detecting or recovering a planted clique of size \(n^{1/2-\delta}\), for some fixed \(\delta>0\), or prove a suitable complexity barrier.
status: Decades-old gap. September 2026 algorithms improve constants at the \(\Theta(\sqrt n)\) scale.
why: Is a central model of computational-statistical separation.
key_works: Kunisky–Mao (2026), [*Improved polynomial-time algorithms for detecting and recovering planted \(\Theta(\sqrt n)\)-cliques*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24780).

title: Exact random 3-SAT threshold
open: Determine the limiting satisfiability threshold \(\alpha_3\), particularly whether the statistical-physics prediction approximately 4.267 is correct.
status: Classical bounds leave approximately 3.52–4.490. An October 5, 2026 preprint claims threshold existence, not its exact value.
why: Would rigorously identify a fundamental random-constraint phase transition.
key_works: Hajiaghayi–Sorkin (2003), threshold upper bound; Carenini (2026), [*A polynomial scaling window for random k-SAT and a proof of the satisfiability conjecture*](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/229/).

title: Rapid mixing of colorings at \(q\ge\Delta+2\)
open: Prove polynomial mixing of single-site Glauber dynamics for proper \(q\)-colorings of arbitrary maximum-degree-\(\Delta\) graphs whenever \(q\ge\Delta+2\).
status: Decades of progress lower sufficient color counts; general results remain around \(1.809\Delta\), above the conjectured threshold.
why: Would enable efficient sampling close to minimal color availability.
key_works: Carlson–Vigoda (2024), [*Flip Dynamics for Sampling Colorings: Improving \((11/6-\varepsilon)\) Using a Simple Metric*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.04870).

title: Square-lattice connective constant
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Determine the exact connective constant \(\mu=\lim_n c_n^{1/n}\) for square-lattice self-avoiding walks.
status: Numerical estimates are near 2.63815853; a rigorous upper bound is 2.662343.
why: Gives the exact exponential entropy of planar self-avoiding walks.
key_works: Couronné (2022), [*New upper bound for the connective constant for square-lattice self-avoiding walks*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.16146).

title: Planar SAW counting exponent \(43/32\)
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove that planar self-avoiding-walk counts have exponent \(\gamma=43/32\), in \(c_n=\mu^n n^{\gamma-1+o(1)}\).
status: Predicted by Nienhuis in 1982; rigorous exponential growth does not determine this polynomial correction.
why: Would validate a central two-dimensional universality prediction.
key_works: Nienhuis (1982), *Exact critical point and critical exponents of O(n) models in two dimensions*; Grimmett–Li, [*Self-avoiding walks and connective constants*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.05884).

title: Planar SAW displacement exponent \(3/4\)
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove that the characteristic displacement of an \(n\)-step planar self-avoiding walk scales as \(n^{3/4+o(1)}\).
status: The exponent is strongly supported by physics and computation. Sub-ballisticity is rigorous but much weaker.
why: Determines universal polymer swelling.
key_works: Duminil-Copin–Hammond (2013), [*Self-avoiding walk is sub-ballistic*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.0401).

title: SAW convergence to \(\mathrm{SLE}_{8/3}\)
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove convergence of suitably rescaled planar lattice self-avoiding walks to \(\mathrm{SLE}_{8/3}\).
status: Predicted in the early 2000s; extensive numerical agreement does not establish the scaling limit.
why: Would connect discrete polymer geometry to conformal probability.
key_works: Lawler–Schramm–Werner (2004), relevant SLE characterization; Kennedy (2002), [*Monte Carlo Tests of SLE Predictions for the 2D Self-Avoiding Walk*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0112246).

title: Four-dimensional strict-SAW logarithmic corrections
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove the predicted logarithmic corrections, including the \(1/4\) exponent, for strict self-avoiding walk on \(\mathbb Z^4\).
status: Rigorous weakly self-avoiding results do not settle the strict model; simulations support the prediction.
why: Resolves behavior at the upper critical dimension.
key_works: Bauerschmidt–Brydges–Slade (2014), weak-model analysis; Fang–Deng–Zhou (2021), [four-dimensional numerical study](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevE.104.064108).

title: Conformal invariance of square-lattice bond percolation
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove that critical square-lattice bond-percolation interfaces converge to \(\mathrm{SLE}_6\).
status: The triangular-site model is settled; the square-bond universality transfer remains open.
why: Would establish lattice-independent critical geometry.
key_works: Duminil-Copin (2018), [*Sixty years of percolation*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.04651).

title: Strict convexity of the first-passage limit shape
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove strict convexity and differentiability of the limit shape for ordinary planar first-passage percolation, for example with independent exponential edge weights.
status: The shape theorem is classical; global curvature properties remain unresolved.
why: Would control directional passage times and geodesic geometry.
key_works: Auffinger–Damron–Hanson (2017), [*50 years of first passage percolation*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.03262).

title: KPZ exponents for ordinary first-passage percolation
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove the predicted passage-time fluctuation exponent \(1/3\) and geodesic wandering exponent \(2/3\) for standard planar FPP.
status: Solvable last-passage models exhibit these exponents; ordinary FPP remains unresolved.
why: Tests KPZ universality outside integrable models.
key_works: Auffinger–Damron–Hanson, [*50 years of first passage percolation*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.03262); [recent primary discussion](https://doi.org/10.1093/imrn/rnae168).

title: Absence of planar FPP bigeodesics
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove almost surely that planar FPP with a standard continuous independent weight law has no doubly infinite geodesic.
status: Directional and conditional nonexistence results are known; unrestricted all-direction nonexistence remains open.
why: Would classify the global structure of optimal paths.
key_works: Damron–Hanson (2017), [*Bigeodesics in first-passage percolation*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.00804).

title: BKS midpoint problem in dimension three
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove that the probability the origin lies on the geodesic between \(-ne_1\) and \(ne_1\) tends to zero in standard FPP on \(\mathbb Z^3\).
status: The planar problem has quantitative solutions; dimensions at least three remain unresolved.
why: Measures delocalization of long optimal paths.
key_works: Dembin–Elboim–Peled (2022), [*Coalescence of geodesics and the BKS midpoint problem in planar first-passage percolation*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.02332).

title: Fractal dimension of planar DLA
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove an asymptotic mass–radius exponent for planar diffusion-limited aggregation and determine its value.
status: Simulations suggest dimension near 1.71; rigorous growth and arm bounds do not establish the exponent.
why: Explains a canonical nonequilibrium fractal-growth process.
key_works: Losev–Smirnov (2023), [*How long are the arms in DBM?*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.14931).

title: Exact square-lattice hard-core critical activity
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Determine the uniqueness-to-nonuniqueness transition activity \(\lambda_c\) for the hard-core model on \(\mathbb Z^2\).
status: Rigorous upper and lower thresholds remain separated; the numerical prediction is approximately 3.796.
why: Establishes a basic nonintegrable lattice-gas critical point.
key_works: Vera–Vigoda–Yang (2013), [*Improved Bounds on the Phase Transition for the Hard-Core Model in 2-Dimensions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.0431).

title: Algebraicity of hard-square entropy
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Determine whether the hard-square entropy constant, approximately 1.503048…, is algebraic or transcendental.
status: The arithmetic nature remains unknown. A 2026 preprint develops criteria without resolving the constant.
why: Connects lattice-model entropy to arithmetic classification.
key_works: Svoray (2026), [*The Algebraicity Problem for Hard-Core Entropy Constants on the Discrete Hypertori*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.28332).

title: Versioned open-problem identity and status graph
subfield: Computational research, data, and sustaining infrastructure
open: Build a public registry linking equivalent statements, stronger variants, special cases, counterexamples, withdrawn proofs, and evidence-backed status histories.
status: Proposed target. Existing problem databases and MaRDI provide components; combinatorics-wide reconciliation remains substantial work.
why: Prevents a million-entry census from multiplying aliases and obsolete claims.
key_works: Bloom, *Erdős Problems*; MaRDI, [*Mission*](https://mardi.imftr.de/about/mission) and [*Portal*](https://mardi.imftr.de/portal/portal).

title: Independently checkable extremal-witness archive
subfield: Computational research, data, and sustaining infrastructure
open: Archive record graphs, designs, codes, colorings, and set systems with canonical encodings, provenance, hashes, and independent property checkers.
status: Proposed cross-resource target; existing repositories support parts of the workflow.
why: Makes computational records reusable mathematical evidence.
key_works: MaRDI, [*Services*](https://portal.mardi4nfdi.de/wiki/MaRDI_Services); Heule (2018), [*Schur Number Five* certificates](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~marijn/Schur/).

title: Tenfold cheaper combinatorial proof checking
subfield: Computational research, data, and sustaining infrastructure
open: Achieve at least \(10\times\) lower storage, verification time, or measured energy on a preregistered combinatorial SAT-proof corpus, retaining full certification.
status: Proposed moonshot. Freeze a competitive checker/version, corpus, hardware, and accounting protocol before comparison; petabyte-scale Schur certification supplies motivating context.
why: Makes exhaustive proofs independently auditable at far lower cost.
key_works: Heule (2018), [*Schur Number Five*](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v32i1.12209); [*Brute trust*](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~mheule/publications/NAW18.pdf).

title: Robust exactification of flag-algebra computations
subfield: Computational research, data, and sustaining infrastructure
open: Automatically convert large, ill-conditioned numerical flag-algebra solutions into exact certificates, including nullspaces and equality conditions.
status: Proposed extension of existing capability. Flagmatic already certifies supported cases; degenerate optima and scaling are the target.
why: Turns numerical extremal evidence into inspectable theorems.
key_works: Vaughan, [*Flagmatic User’s Guide*](https://lidicky.name/flagmatic/UsersGuide.pdf); [Flagmatic repository](https://github.com/FordUniver/flagmatic).

title: Contamination-resistant research-combinatorics benchmark
subfield: Computational research, data, and sustaining infrastructure
open: Create time-stamped held-out research tasks with independent checking and separate scores for novelty, correctness, and computational cost.
status: Proposed target. CombiBench supplies 100 formalized problems; construction-search systems demonstrate complementary capabilities.
why: Measures new mathematical progress rather than retrieval of known answers.
key_works: Liu et al. (2025), [*CombiBench*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03171); Charton–Ellenberg–Wagner–Williamson (2024), [*PatternBoost: Constructions in Mathematics with a Little Help from AI*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.00566).

title: Semantic audit of formalized conjectures
subfield: Computational research, data, and sustaining infrastructure
open: Build and validate a workflow detecting missing hypotheses, incorrect quantifiers, convention mismatches, and vacuous formalizations against expert-adjudicated examples.
status: Proposed engineering target. Proof checking alone does not establish that the formal statement matches the intended question.
why: Prevents correct proofs of unintended statements from becoming false solution claims.
key_works: Liu et al. (2025), [*CombiBench*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03171); [*Formal Conjectures* repository](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures).

title: Sustained funding and credit for mathematical data stewardship
subfield: Computational research, data, and sustaining infrastructure
open: Establish durable funding, recognition, and service commitments for maintaining catalogs, certificates, software dependencies, and independent replication.
status: Proposed policy target, not an allegation that a named project lacks funding. Published infrastructure programs identify sustainability and adoption as continuing needs.
why: Preserves evidence and curator expertise beyond individual grants.
key_works: MaRDI (2025), [NFDI continuation-program letter](https://www.dfg.de/resource/blob/359426/nfdi-2025-mardi.pdf); NFDI, [MaRDI consortium](https://www.nfdi.de/mardi/?lang=en).

title: Golomb–Welch perfect Lee-code conjecture
open: For every dimension \(n\ge3\) and integer radius \(r\ge2\), prove that \(\mathbb Z^n\) cannot be partitioned into translates of the Lee ball \(\{x\in\mathbb Z^n:\sum_i|x_i|\le r\}\).
status: Open since 1968. Several low-dimensional and large-radius cases are settled. Leung–Zhou exclude lattice tilings by radius-two Lee balls in every dimension at least three; arbitrary translational tilings need not be lattice tilings.
why: Determines where perfect error correction in the Manhattan metric becomes impossible.
key_works: Peter Horak and Dongryul Kim (2018), [*50 Years of the Golomb–Welch Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03589); Ka Hin Leung and Yue Zhou (2020), [*No lattice tiling of \(\mathbb Z^n\) by Lee sphere of radius 2*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcta.2019.105157).

title: Six-match football-pool covering number
open: Determine \(K_3(6,1)\), the smallest number of ternary strings of length six whose radius-one Hamming balls cover all \(3^6=729\) strings. A solution requires either an improved covering construction or a matching certified lower bound.
status: The established interval is \(71\le K_3(6,1)\le73\). Recent semidefinite and polyhedral methods improve covering-code bounds, but this small football-pool instance remains unresolved.
why: Provides a compact, difficult benchmark for exact covering, symmetry reduction, and certifiable integer optimization.
key_works: Dion Gijswijt and Sven Polak (2025/2026), [*Semidefinite lower bounds for covering codes*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01932); Javier Marenco and Pablo Rey (2026), [*An initial polyhedral study of the football pool problem*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disopt.2026.100946).

title: Exact binary deletion-channel capacity
open: Determine the capacity \(C_{\mathrm{del}}(d)\) of the channel that independently deletes each input bit with probability \(d\). A complete solution should characterize capacity-achieving inputs and supply a matching converse.
status: Open since Dobrushin’s 1967 framework. Papailiopoulos’s September 2026 computer-assisted bounds give a midpoint estimate with error below \(0.0095\) bits uniformly in \(d\); the exact capacity function remains unknown.
why: Quantifies the optimal communication rate when the receiver loses symbol alignment.
key_works: Roland Dobrushin (1967), *Shannon’s theorems for channels with synchronization errors*; Dimitris Papailiopoulos (2026), [*Binary Deletion Channel Capacity to Within One Hundredth of a Bit*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19412), with [computational certificates](https://github.com/anadim/binary-deletion-channel-capacity).

title: Binary adversarial-deletion zero-rate threshold
open: Determine the supremum \(\delta_*\) of deletion fractions for which binary codes of positive asymptotic rate can uniquely correct every pattern of \(\lfloor\delta n\rfloor\) deletions.
status: Constructions approach \(\sqrt2-1\approx0.4142\). Guruswami–He–Li prove that \(\delta_*<1/2\) by an absolute amount, disproving the former conjectural threshold \(1/2\). The exact threshold remains open.
why: Determines the maximum resilience of positive-rate binary communication against adversarial loss of synchronization.
key_works: Boris Bukh, Venkatesan Guruswami and Johan Håstad (2017), [*An improved bound on the fraction of correctable deletions*](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2015/117/); Venkatesan Guruswami, Xiaoyu He and Ray Li (2021), [*The zero-rate threshold for adversarial bit-deletions is less than \(1/2\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.05250).

title: Packing-scale binary two-deletion codes
open: Construct binary length-\(n\) codes correcting two arbitrary deletions with redundancy \((2+o(1))\log_2 n\), or prove that the packing-bound coefficient two cannot be attained.
status: The packing bound gives leading coefficient two. Eyal En Gad’s September 2026 preprint claims an existential upper bound \(3\log_2 n+O(\log\log n)\); Guruswami–Håstad’s explicit construction has leading coefficient four. The coefficient-two target remains unresolved.
why: Determines the true information cost of correcting even two synchronization errors.
key_works: Vladimir Levenshtein (1966), *Binary codes capable of correcting deletions, insertions, and reversals*; Venkatesan Guruswami and Johan Håstad (2021), [*Explicit two-deletion codes with redundancy matching the existential bound*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.10592); Eyal En Gad (2026), [*Polynomially larger deletion codes by linear hashing of substring counts*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19493).

title: Exponential growth rate of trifferent codes
open: Determine the asymptotic exponential growth rate of the largest \(C\subseteq\{0,1,2\}^n\) such that every three distinct codewords exhibit all three symbols in at least one coordinate.
status: The problem originates in work on distinguishable differences and perfect hashing. Bhandari–Khetan improve the upper bound to \(O(n^{-2/5}(3/2)^n)\); constructions still do not match the upper exponential base.
why: Isolates the basic three-object separation problem underlying perfect-hash families.
key_works: Siddharth Bhandari and Manik Dhar Khetan (2024), [*Improved Upper Bound for the Size of a Trifferent Code*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.02390); Bishnoi, Kielak, Kovács, Nagy, Somlai, Vizer and Zheng (2026), [*The generalized trifference problem*](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.2026.3665439).

title: Maximum nonlinearity of a nine-variable Boolean function
open: Determine \(\max_f\min_{\ell\text{ affine}}d_H(f,\ell)\) for \(f:\mathbb F_2^9\to\mathbb F_2\). Equivalently, determine the covering radius of the first-order Reed–Muller code \(RM(1,9)\).
status: Kavut–Yücel constructed functions of nonlinearity \(242\) in 2008; the upper bound is \(244\). A function attaining \(243\) or \(244\), or an impossibility proof closing the gap, remains unknown.
why: Determines the strongest possible resistance to affine approximation at a small but computationally challenging truth-table size.
key_works: Selçuk Kavut and Melek D. Yücel (2008/2010), [*9-variable Boolean Functions with Nonlinearity 242 in the Generalized Rotation Class*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.0684); Claude Carlet (2021), *Boolean Functions for Cryptography and Coding Theory*.
aliases: Covering radius of the first-order Reed–Muller code of length \(512\).

title: APN permutations in even dimensions above six
open: Construct an almost-perfect-nonlinear permutation of \(\mathbb F_2^m\) for some even \(m\ge8\), or prove that none exists in any such dimension. APN means that \(F(x+a)+F(x)=b\) has at most two solutions for every \(a\ne0\) and every \(b\).
status: Dillon’s dimension-six construction remains the only known even-dimensional example. Extensive dimension-eight searches and exclusions of substantial algebraic classes leave the unrestricted existence question open.
why: Would produce bijective binary substitution boxes with optimal differential behavior, or establish a fundamental obstruction to them.
key_works: Christof Beierle, Marcus Brinkmann and Gregor Leander (2020), [*Linearly Self-Equivalent APN Permutations in Small Dimension*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.12006).

title: Complete census of quadratic APN functions in dimension eight
open: Enumerate every CCZ-equivalence class of quadratic APN maps \(\mathbb F_2^8\to\mathbb F_2^8\), with canonical representatives and a checkable completeness certificate. CCZ equivalence means that an invertible affine map of \(\mathbb F_2^{16}\) sends one function’s graph onto the other’s.
status: A 2025 construction supplies \(3{,}775{,}599\) inequivalent examples and estimates roughly six million classes. The catalogue and estimate do not constitute a complete classification.
why: Would provide an exhaustive small-dimensional search space for nonlinear functions, associated codes, and exceptional cryptographic constructions.
key_works: Christof Beierle, Philippe Langevin, Gregor Leander, Alexandr Polujan and Shahram Rasoolzadeh (2025), [*Millions of inequivalent quadratic APN functions in eight variables*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04644).

title: Exceptional APN classification
open: Prove that every polynomial over a characteristic-two finite field that remains APN over infinitely many extensions is CCZ-equivalent to a Gold or Kasami–Welch monomial, or construct another exceptional family.
status: The Aubry–McGuire–Rodier conjecture remains open. Agrinsoni–Janwa–Delgado resolve the Gold-degree case in 2025 and advance the Kasami–Welch-degree case in 2026; the complete classification remains unavailable.
why: Would classify nonlinear difference structures that persist over arbitrarily large field extensions.
key_works: Agrinsoni, Janwa and Delgado (2025), [*Resolution of the exceptional APN conjecture in the Gold degree case*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10623-025-01607-x); the same authors (2026), [*Toward resolution of the exceptional APN conjecture in the Kasami–Welch degree case*](https://doi.org/10.1142/S0219498825410269).

title: A Costas array of order thirty-two
open: Find a permutation \(\pi\) of \(\{0,\ldots,31\}\) whose displacement vectors \((j-i,\pi(j)-\pi(i))\), for \(i<j\), are all distinct, or certify that no such permutation exists.
status: Order thirty-two is a longstanding gap in existence tables. Known algebraic constructions skip it, and complete unrestricted enumeration reaches order twenty-nine.
why: Would fill the first missing ideal discrete time-frequency ambiguity pattern.
key_works: Konstantinos Drakakis (2011), [*Open problems in Costas arrays*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.5727); Gulec and Abolghasemi (2026), [*Universal Costas Matrices: Towards a General Framework for Costas Array Construction*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03407).

title: Complete enumeration of Costas arrays of order thirty
open: Enumerate all order-thirty Costas permutations, including every orbit under square rotations and reflections, with a replayable completeness argument.
status: Full enumeration has stopped at order twenty-nine since 2011; the February 2026 account confirms that boundary. Enumerations of symmetric subclasses at larger orders do not establish completeness for unrestricted order thirty.
why: Would measure the persistence of sporadic arrays and provide a demanding benchmark for exact permutation search.
key_works: Konstantinos Drakakis, Francesco Iorio, Scott Rickard and John Walsh (2011), *Results of the enumeration of Costas arrays of order 29*; Gulec and Abolghasemi (2026), [*Universal Costas Matrices: Towards a General Framework for Costas Array Construction*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03407).

title: The true asymptotic diamond-free constant
open: Determine the asymptotic maximum size \(\operatorname{La}(n,Q_2)\) of a family in \(2^{[n]}\) containing no four distinct sets \(A,B,C,D\) with \(A\subset B\subset D\) and \(A\subset C\subset D\). In particular, determine whether \(\operatorname{La}(n,Q_2)/\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\) converges and identify its limit; this is weak containment, so \(B,C\) need not be incomparable.
status: The longstanding proposed constant \(2\) was disproved by Tompkins’s July 2026 construction, which gives \(2.147908-o(1)\). The published upper bound is \(2.20711+o(1)\).
why: Tests how far forbidden-poset extremal families can depart from unions of consecutive Boolean levels.
key_works: Dániel Tompkins (2026), [*An Improved Lower Bound for Diamond-Free Families*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09497); Dániel Grósz, Abhishek Methuku and Dániel Tompkins (2018), [*An upper bound on the size of diamond-free families of sets*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.06332).

title: Existence of forbidden-poset density limits
open: For every fixed finite poset \(P\), does \(\operatorname{La}(n,P)/\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\) have a limit, where containment means an injective order-preserving map? Resolve convergence without assuming that the limit is an integer.
status: Known for several classes, including posets whose Hasse diagram is a tree. The 2026 diamond counterexample invalidates stronger predictions about the value but does not settle general convergence.
why: Would assign a stable extremal density invariant to every finite forbidden order pattern.
key_works: Boris Bukh (2009), [*Set families with a forbidden subposet*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0803.3840); Jerrold R. Griggs and Wei-Tian Li (2017), [*Progress on poset-free families of subsets*](https://people.math.sc.edu/griggs/Survey20171001.pdf).

title: Simonyi’s sandglass conjecture
open: Suppose \(\mathcal A,\mathcal B\subseteq2^{[n]}\) are recovering: \(A\setminus B=A'\setminus B'\) implies \(A=A'\), and \(B\setminus A=B'\setminus A'\) implies \(B=B'\). Prove \(|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|\le2^n\).
status: Proposed in 1989. Costa’s October 2026 preprint gives the upper bound \(2.23949^n\). The separate conjecture about cancellative pairs was resolved in September 2026; the stronger recovery requirement leads to this still-open target.
why: Determines how much information two set families can jointly encode when each message must remain recoverable after taking a set difference.
key_works: S. Costa (2026), [*An Improved Upper Bound for Recovering Pairs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03851); N. Mond, V. Souza and L. Versteegen (2025), [*The sandglass conjecture beyond cancellative pairs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.21819).

title: Frein–Lévêque–Sebő disjoint \(k\)-generator conjecture
open: Suppose every subset of \([n]\) is a disjoint union of at most \(k\) members of \(\mathcal G\subseteq2^{[n]}\setminus\{\varnothing\}\). For \(n=qk+r\), \(0\le r<k\), prove
status: Proposed in 2008. Balanced partitions attain the bound. It is known for \(k=2\) and sufficiently large \(n\), and for fixed \(k\) when \(n\) is a sufficiently large multiple of \(k\).
why: Identifies the optimal dictionary for representing arbitrary sets using a bounded number of disjoint pieces.
key_works: David Ellis (2008), [*Note on generating all subsets of a finite set with disjoint unions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.3022); David Ellis and Benny Sudakov (2011), [*Generating all subsets of a finite set with disjoint unions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.4877).

title: Frankl–Wang higher-trace conjecture
open: Partition \(n\) into \(\ell\) integers \(a_i\) differing by at most one. If \(|\mathcal F|>\prod_{i=1}^{\ell}(a_i+1)\), must some \((\ell+1)\)-element set \(Y\) satisfy
status: The general question remains for \(\ell\ge4\). Frankl–Wang prove the four-element trace case, \(\ell=3\), for \(n\ge25\), extending the lower-dimensional cases.
why: Seeks sharp thresholds for forcing many distinguishable local patterns beyond the usual complete-shattering threshold.
key_works: Peter Frankl and Jian Wang (2023), [*Four-vertex traces of finite sets*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.05830).

title: Curling-number termination conjecture
open: For a nonempty finite integer sequence \(S\), let \(k(S)\) be the largest \(k\) for which \(S=XY^k\) with \(Y\ne\varnothing\). Repeatedly append \(k(S)\); prove that a \(1\) eventually appears, whatever the starting sequence.
status: Formulated in the 2000s. Even starts consisting only of \(2\) and \(3\) remain unresolved. Published exhaustive searches cover initial lengths through \(48\); some longer computational conclusions rely on conjectural reductions.
why: Would establish universal termination for a simple string rule whose dependence on its entire history makes conventional induction difficult.
key_works: Benjamin Chaffin and N. J. A. Sloane (2009), [*Curling Numbers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.2382); Benjamin Chaffin, J. P. Linderman, N. J. A. Sloane and A. R. Wilks (2013), [*On Curling Numbers of Integer Sequences*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.6102).

title: Recurrence of the Kolakoski sequence
open: Does every finite factor of the self-run-length-encoding sequence \(122112122\ldots\) occur infinitely often?
status: The sequence appears in Oldenburger’s 1939 work and Kolakoski’s 1965 rediscovery. Nonperiodicity is known; recurrence remains open and would imply reversal invariance.
why: Determines whether every pattern that appears once must persist throughout the infinite word.
key_works: Alessandro Della Corte (2020), [*Kolakoski Sequence: Links between Recurrence, Symmetry and Limit Density*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.08306).

title: Complement symmetry of the Kolakoski language
open: Whenever a finite word \(w\) occurs in the Kolakoski sequence, must the word obtained by exchanging every \(1\) and \(2\) also occur?
status: Open despite extensive finite evidence. Complement symmetry implies recurrence; it is a separate assertion from reversal symmetry or equality of digit densities.
why: Would establish a global symmetry that is not apparent from the sequence’s asymmetric initial condition.
key_works: F. Michel Dekking (1997), *What is the Long Range Order in the Kolakoski Sequence?*; Alessandro Della Corte (2020), [*Kolakoski Sequence: Links between Recurrence, Symmetry and Limit Density*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.08306).

title: Irreducible unimodular Pisot substitution conjecture
open: Prove that the dynamical system of every primitive substitution whose incidence matrix has irreducible characteristic polynomial, determinant \(\pm1\), and Pisot Perron eigenvalue has pure discrete spectrum.
status: A longstanding conjecture from the 1980s. Many classes are settled, including Pisot \(\beta\)-substitutions; arbitrary irreducible unimodular Pisot substitutions remain outside those results.
why: Would connect an algebraic property of a finite substitution rule to quasiperiodic spectral order.
key_works: Marcy Barge (2015), [*The Pisot Conjecture for \(\beta\)-substitutions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.04408); Valérie Berthé and Michel Rigo, editors (2016), *Combinatorics, Words and Symbolic Dynamics*.

title: Strong coincidence for irreducible Pisot substitutions
open: For every pair of letters \(a,b\) of a primitive irreducible unimodular Pisot substitution \(\sigma\), prove that some iterates satisfy \(\sigma^k(a)=pcu\) and \(\sigma^k(b)=qcv\), where the common letter \(c\) is preceded by prefixes \(p,q\) with identical letter-count vectors.
status: Verified for substantial special classes and large computational families. No general proof or counterexample is known.
why: Would supply a finite combinatorial mechanism behind spectral and tiling properties of substitution systems.
key_works: Marcy Barge and Luca Q. Zamboni (2013), [*Central sets and substitutive dynamical systems*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.5745); Scott Balchin (2017), [*A Computational Method for Large Scale Searching of Counterexamples to the Strong Coincidence Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.05277).

title: Eventual periodicity of Grundy’s unequal-splitting game
status: Open since the classical development of impartial games. Flammenkamp reports computations through heap size \(284{,}944{,}236{,}543\), without an established eventual period; observed sparse-value behavior gives conditional approaches.
why: Tests whether a very elementary splitting rule can produce permanently nonperiodic game values.
key_works: Patrick M. Grundy (1939), *Mathematics and games*; Achim Flammenkamp, [*Grundy’s Game*](https://wwwhomes.uni-bielefeld.de/achim/grundy.html), computational tables and commentary.

title: Complete misère analysis of Dawson’s chess
open: Describe the full misère quotient \((Q,P)\) of Dawson’s chess: its monoid operation, losing subset \(P\), and heap-class map \(\Phi(n)\) for arbitrary \(n\). These data should uniformly determine outcomes and winning moves in finite sums.
status: Open since Dawson’s 1935 formulation. For the equivalent heap game \(0.07\), the quotient restricted to heaps of size at most \(33\) has \(638\) elements; a full description remains unknown.
why: Would extend practical misère algebra to one of its oldest major test cases.
key_works: Thane E. Plambeck and Aaron N. Siegel (2008), [*Misère quotients for impartial games*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0609825); Richard J. Nowakowski (2025), [*Unsolved problems in combinatorial games*](https://library.slmath.org/books/Book71/files/GONC6-04.pdf), problem A15.
prize: US$500 offered by Plambeck, reported in the 2025 survey; present administration has not been independently confirmed.

title: The wild quaternary game \(0.3102\)
open: Describe the full misère quotient, its losing classes, and the heap-class map for the game with these moves: remove one token freely; remove two only when doing so empties the heap; or remove four while leaving a nonempty heap.
status: Retained in the 2025 problem list. The partial quotient through heap size \(11\) has \(74\) elements; no complete quotient description is known.
why: Exhibits difficult misère behavior without even allowing heaps to split.
key_works: Thane E. Plambeck and Aaron N. Siegel (2008), [*Misère quotients for impartial games*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0609825), Appendix A.4; Richard J. Nowakowski (2025), [*Unsolved problems in combinatorial games*](https://library.slmath.org/books/Book71/files/GONC6-04.pdf), A15.
prize: US$200 offered by Plambeck, reported in the 2025 survey; present administration has not been independently confirmed.

title: Recognizing infinite misère quotients
open: Given a finite, explicitly represented collection of finite impartial games, decide whether the misère quotient of its closure under followers and disjunctive sums is infinite. Establish a general decision algorithm or prove undecidability.
status: Listed by Plambeck–Siegel and retained in Nowakowski’s 2025 survey. Existing quotient algorithms handle many finite cases but provide no general termination guarantee when the quotient is infinite.
why: Would establish whether a major failure mode of automated game analysis can be recognized algorithmically.
key_works: Thane E. Plambeck and Aaron N. Siegel (2007), [*Misère quotients for impartial games: Supplementary material*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.2404); Richard J. Nowakowski (2025), [*Unsolved problems in combinatorial games*](https://library.slmath.org/books/Book71/files/GONC6-04.pdf).

title: Pair-sum periods for three-move subtraction games
open: Let \(S=\{a,b,c\}\), with \(2\le a<b<c\), \(\gcd(a,b,c)=1\), and \(c\ne a+b\). If the associated Sprague–Grundy sequence is periodic from the start, must its least period belong to \(\{a+b,a+c,b+c\}\)?
status: Explicitly conjectured by Manabe in September 2026. His rotation criterion establishes pure periodicity and exact periods in substantial regions; a necessity result handles period \(a+b\) when \(c\ge2(a+b)\).
why: Would constrain the global behavior of a game sequence using only three elementary numerical combinations of its legal moves.
key_works: H. Manabe (2026), [*Purely Periodic Three-move Subtraction Games*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05358).

title: Symmetric Mahler volume-product conjecture
open: For every origin-symmetric convex body \(K\subset\mathbb R^d\), prove
status: Originates in Mahler’s 1930s work. Iriyeh–Shibata prove the three-dimensional symmetric case, including equality. Unconditional bodies and other structured classes are known; general reverse Santaló inequalities give the dimensional scale without the sharp constant.
why: Would determine the smallest possible volume product of a norm ball and its dual.
key_works: Hiroshi Iriyeh and Masataka Shibata (2020), [*Symmetric Mahler’s conjecture for the volume product in the three dimensional case*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.01749); Jean Bourgain and Vitali Milman (1987), *New volume ratio properties for convex symmetric bodies in \(\mathbb R^n\)*.

title: Nonsymmetric Mahler volume-product conjecture
open: For every convex body \(K\subset\mathbb R^d\), prove
status: A classical conjecture attributed to Mahler. Chen–Li–Xi–Xu’s May–June 2026 preprint announces the three-dimensional theorem using a shadow-flow method. The general conjecture remains unresolved for \(d\ge4\).
why: Would identify the extremal relation between a convex body and its polar without assuming symmetry.
key_works: Shibing Chen, Yuanyuan Li, Dongmeng Xi and Zhe-Feng Xu (2026), [*The Mahler Conjecture in Three Dimensions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09334); Mathieu Meyer and Shlomo Reisner (2006), *Shadow systems and volumes of polar convex bodies*.

title: Logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski conjecture
open: For origin-symmetric convex bodies \(K,L\) and \(0<t<1\), prove
status: Formulated in the early 2010s. The planar case, unconditional bodies, and several local or symmetry-restricted cases are established. Iffland’s 2026 work proves further local results for bodies of revolution.
why: Would strengthen volume concavity and constrain interpolation between convex bodies.
key_works: Károly Böröczky, Erwin Lutwak, Deane Yang and Gaoyong Zhang (2012), *The log-Brunn–Minkowski inequality*; Luca Iffland (2026), [*The local logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequality for bodies of revolution*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17912).

title: Ulam’s least-dense-packing conjecture
open: Prove that every three-dimensional convex body admits a packing by congruent copies of density at least \(\pi/\sqrt{18}\), the optimal sphere-packing density. Arbitrary rotations are allowed.
status: Recorded as Ulam’s conjecture in the 1970s. Kallus proves that the ball is a local pessimum among origin-symmetric convex bodies, covering sufficiently small symmetric deformations. Arbitrary convex shapes remain unresolved.
why: Would establish a universal lower packing efficiency for convex particles and identify the sphere as the global worst case.
key_works: Yoav Kallus (2014), [*The 3-ball is a local pessimum for packing*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.2551); Thomas Hales (2005), *A proof of the Kepler conjecture*.

title: Meissner’s minimum-volume constant-width problem
open: Prove that among convex bodies of constant width one in \(\mathbb R^3\), minimum volume is attained by a Meissner tetrahedron, or find a smaller body and identify the correct minimizers.
status: A longstanding three-dimensional Blaschke–Lebesgue problem. The planar analogue is solved. Bogosel’s 2026 work develops explicit volume formulas for Meissner polyhedra and necessary conditions for minimizing examples, without establishing global optimality.
why: Determines how little volume can support the same width in every direction and provides a precise target for certified shape optimization.
key_works: Beniamin Bogosel (2026), [*Volume Computation for Meissner Polyhedra and Applications*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-024-00688-0); Bogosel (2026), [*Dangling points in area-minimizing Meissner polyhedra*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19747).

title: Optimal packing density of regular tetrahedra
open: Determine the supremal density of packings of congruent regular tetrahedra in \(\mathbb R^3\), allowing arbitrary rotations and nonperiodic arrangements. In particular, is \(4000/4671\) globally optimal?
status: Chen–Engel–Glotzer construct a dimer crystal of density \(4000/4671\approx0.856347\) in 2010. Rigorous upper bounds remain far from certifying this value; optimization over small periodic cells cannot exclude larger cells or nonperiodic improvements.
why: Would determine a basic packing optimum for nonspherical particles and calibrate computational crystal searches.
key_works: Elizabeth Chen, Michael Engel and Sharon Glotzer (2010), [*Dense crystalline dimer packings of regular tetrahedra*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.0586); Simon Gravel, Veit Elser and Yoav Kallus (2011), [*Upper bound on the packing density of regular tetrahedra and octahedra*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.2830).

title: Voronoi’s parallelohedron conjecture
open: Prove that every convex polytope tiling \(\mathbb R^d\) by translations is affinely equivalent to the Dirichlet–Voronoi cell of a lattice.
status: Posed in 1908. Many structural classes are known. Garber’s proof for all five-dimensional parallelohedra was published in 2025; the universal cases in dimensions at least six remain open.
why: Would classify convex translational tiles through quadratic forms and nearest-lattice-point geometry.
key_works: Alexey Garber (2025), [*Voronoi conjecture for five-dimensional parallelohedra*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.05193); Alexey Garber, Andrey Gavrilyuk and Alexander Magazinov (2014), [*The Voronoi conjecture for parallelohedra with simply connected \(\delta\)-surface*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1019).

title: Kalai’s \(3^d\) face conjecture
open: Prove that every centrally symmetric \(d\)-dimensional convex polytope has at least \(3^d\) nonempty faces, counting the polytope itself and excluding the empty face.
status: Proposed in 1989. Hanner polytopes, including cubes and crosspolytopes, attain the bound. Chambers–Portnoy establish the conjecture for unconditional polytopes in their August 2026 publication; general central symmetry remains unresolved.
why: Would identify the minimum total combinatorial complexity forced by central symmetry.
key_works: Gregory Chambers and Elia Portnoy (2026), [*A Note on Kalai’s \(3^d\) Conjecture*](https://doi.org/10.37236/13956); Raman Sanyal, Axel Werner and Günter Ziegler (2009), *On Kalai’s conjectures concerning centrally symmetric polytopes*.

title: Gilbert–Pollak Steiner-ratio conjecture
open: Prove that for every finite planar point set, the Euclidean Steiner minimum tree has length at least \(\sqrt3/2\) times the Euclidean minimum spanning tree length. Equilateral triangles attain equality.
status: Proposed in 1968. A famous claimed complete proof contains a gap. Ke and collaborators’ published 2026 work reports the certified partial lower bound \(0.8559\), below the conjectured \(0.866025\ldots\).
why: Determines the largest possible saving obtained by introducing additional junctions into a shortest connecting network.
key_works: Edgar Gilbert and Henry Pollak (1968), *Steiner minimal trees*; Yisi Ke, Tianyu Huang, Yankai Shu, Di He, Jingchu Gai and Liwei Wang (2026), [*Towards Solving the Gilbert-Pollak Conjecture via Large Language Models*](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/ke26a.html).

title: Kneser–Poulsen volume-contraction conjecture
open: If the centers of finitely many Euclidean balls move so that every pairwise distance weakly decreases, while each radius stays fixed, must the volume of their union weakly decrease? Settle dimensions at least three without assuming that the endpoints are joined by a continuous distance-decreasing motion.
status: Independently formulated in the 1950s. Bezdek–Connelly prove the planar case in 2002; continuous contractions and various restricted configurations are known. Aishwarya–Li’s September 2026 heat-flow approach recovers principal known cases and proposes stronger analytic inequalities.
why: Would convert pairwise metric information into a global bound on occupied volume.
key_works: Károly Bezdek and Robert Connelly (2002), *Pushing disks apart—The Kneser–Poulsen conjecture in the plane*; Gautam Aishwarya and Dongbin Li (2026), [*Gaussian Convolution, Internal Energies, and the Kneser–Poulsen Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.07041).

title: Unbounded fatness of convex four-polytopes
status: Highlighted by Eppstein–Kuperberg–Ziegler in 2003. Constructions exceed bounds available for simple or simplicial polytopes. Strongly regular cell decompositions of the three-sphere can have unbounded fatness, but convex realizability remains the crucial additional constraint.
why: Would resolve a major qualitative uncertainty about realizable face vectors in dimension four.
key_works: David Eppstein, Greg Kuperberg and Günter Ziegler (2003), [*Fat 4-polytopes and fatter 3-spheres*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0204007); Günter Ziegler (2004), *Face numbers of 4-polytopes and 3-spheres*.

title: Optimal size of planar weak epsilon-nets
open: Determine the smallest worst-case size \(f_2(\epsilon)\) of a set piercing every convex region containing at least an \(\epsilon\) fraction of a given finite planar point set. Piercing points may lie outside the input set.
status: Studied since the early 1990s. Rubin gives \(f_2(\epsilon)=O(\epsilon^{-3/2-\gamma})\) for every fixed \(\gamma>0\). The lower bound \(\Omega(\epsilon^{-1}\log(1/\epsilon))\) leaves an exponent gap.
why: Determines how efficiently all large convex ranges can be represented by a small set of witnesses.
key_works: Natan Rubin (2022), [*An Improved Bound for Weak Epsilon-Nets in the Plane*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.02686); Boris Bukh, Jiří Matoušek and Gabriel Nivasch (2011), *Lower bounds for weak epsilon-nets and stair-convexity*.

title: Exact planar Hadwiger–Debrunner \((4,3)\) piercing number
open: Determine the least integer \(h\) such that every finite family of planar convex sets, among every four of which some three intersect, can be pierced by \(h\) points. The conjectured value is three.
status: A concrete case of the 1957 Hadwiger–Debrunner program. The \((p,q)\) theorem establishes finiteness. McGinnis improves the universal upper bound from thirteen to nine; examples require three, leaving \(3\le h\le9\).
why: Would quantify exactly how a local intersection condition restricts a global transversal.
key_works: Daniel McGinnis (2022), [*A family of convex sets in the plane satisfying the \((4,3)\)-property can be pierced by nine points*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.13195); András Gyárfás, Daniel Kleitman and Géza Tóth (2001), *Convex sets in the plane with three of every four meeting*.

title: Polynomial-time colorful Carathéodory search
open: Given \(d+1\) finite rational point sets in \(\mathbb R^d\), each having the origin in its convex hull, find one point of each color whose convex hull contains the origin in time polynomial in the input bit length.
