status: The existence theorem dates to Bárány’s 1982 work. Meunier–Mulzer–Sarrabezolles–Stein place the search problem in \(\mathrm{PPAD}\cap\mathrm{PLS}\), now known to equal \(\mathrm{CLS}\). General exact polynomial-time search remains unresolved.
why: Would make a fundamental existential convexity theorem efficiently usable in geometric optimization and related reductions.
key_works: Frédéric Meunier, Wolfgang Mulzer, Pauline Sarrabezolles and Yannik Stein (2017), [*The Rainbow at the End of the Line—A PPAD Formulation of the Colorful Carathéodory Theorem with Applications*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.01921).

title: Polynomial-time rotation distance
open: Determine whether the minimum number of rotations transforming one ordered rooted binary tree into another with the same ordered leaves can be computed in polynomial time. Equivalently, compute exact flip distance between triangulations of a convex polygon.
status: Open since the classical 1980s work on rotation distance. Constant-factor approximation and fixed-parameter algorithms in the distance are known; Cleary–St. John obtain a linear-size kernel. General polynomial-time exact computation remains unresolved.
why: Would settle the complexity of a fundamental local reconfiguration metric used in data structures and associahedron geometry.
key_works: Sean Cleary and Katherine St. John (2009), [*Rotation distance is fixed-parameter tractable*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ipl.2009.04.023); Anoop S. K. M. and Jayalal Sarma (2023), [*On Rotation Distance of Rank Bounded Trees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03985).

title: Conway’s thrackle conjecture
open: Prove that a drawing of a finite simple graph in the plane in which every pair of distinct edges meets exactly once—at a shared endpoint or a proper crossing—has at most as many edges as vertices.
status: Posed in the late 1960s. Straight-line thrackles satisfy the conjecture. Xu’s 2021 general improvement gives coefficient \(1.393\) in the corresponding connected bound; unrestricted drawings with curved edges remain unresolved.
why: Tests how strongly an extreme pairwise crossing rule constrains a graph’s global size.
key_works: Radoslav Fulek and János Pach (2017), [*Thrackles: An Improved Upper Bound*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.08037); Yian Xu (2021), [*A New Upper Bound for Conway’s Thrackles*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.amc.2020.125573).

title: Optimal universal Komlós constant
status: September 2026 proof preprints establish finiteness of \(K_*\). Kunisky’s constructions give \(K_*\ge1+\sqrt2\); Akbas–Sra’s revised September/October 2026 preprint reports \(K_*<6.9013\). The exact value remains unknown.
why: Determines the unavoidable cost of balancing Euclidean-normalized constraints and sharpens every reduction through Komlós balancing.
key_works: Dmitriy Kunisky (2023), [*The Discrepancy of Unsatisfiable Matrices and a Lower Bound for the Komlós Conjecture Constant*](https://doi.org/10.1137/22M149819X); Emrullah Akbas and Suvrit Sra (2026), [*Tighter bounds on Komlós discrepancy: existence and algorithmic results*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27172).

title: Strong prefix Komlós conjecture
open: Is there an absolute \(C\) such that every finite ordered sequence \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\), with \(\|v_i\|_2\le1\), admits signs satisfying
status: A longstanding strengthening of Komlós balancing. The September 2026 proof controls the final sum, and its elementary exposition explicitly leaves simultaneous control of all prefixes open.
why: Would balance every intermediate state of a process, giving guarantees beyond control of its final total.
key_works: Sankeerth Rao Karingula and Shachar Lovett (2026), [*An elementary proof of the Komlós conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20979); Nikhil Bansal and Aleksandar Nikolov (2026), [*Discrepancy Theory: An Algorithmic and Geometric Perspective*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00140).

title: Euclidean Steinitz square-root conjecture
open: Does every finite zero-sum family of vectors in the Euclidean unit ball of \(\mathbb R^d\) admit an ordering whose every partial sum has Euclidean norm at most \(C\sqrt d\), for an absolute \(C\) independent of the number of vectors?
status: Square-root-scale confinement goes back to Bergström’s 1931 work. Lower bounds have this order. Banaszczyk gives \(O(\sqrt d+\sqrt{\log n})\); Dutta–Jha–Jiang’s April 2026 constructive result reaches \(O(\sqrt d)\) when \(d\) is at least a sufficiently large multiple of \(\log^7 n\).
why: Determines the smallest unavoidable intermediate imbalance when rearranging a perfectly balanced vector family.
key_works: Kunal Dutta, Agastya Vibhuti Jha and Haotian Jiang (2026), [*Near-Optimal Constructive Bounds for \(\ell_2\) Prefix Discrepancy and Steinitz Problems via Affine Spectral Independence*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.13355).

title: Cube-norm Steinitz square-root conjecture
open: For vectors \(v_i\in[-1,1]^d\) summing to zero, can they always be permuted so that every partial sum lies in \([-C\sqrt d,C\sqrt d]^d\), for an absolute constant \(C\)?
status: The classical Steinitz lemma gives a linear-in-\(d\) universal bound. Square-root growth remains an explicit open target in Ambrus–Heck’s 2026 work. Euclidean unit-ball results do not directly give this scale for cube vectors.
why: Would sharpen simultaneous cumulative-load bounds in scheduling and strengthen geometric tools used in integer optimization.
key_works: Gergely Ambrus and Rainie Heck (2026), [*A note on the Steinitz lemma*](https://doi.org/10.1112/mtk.70085); Nikhil Bansal and Aleksandar Nikolov (2026), [*Discrepancy Theory: An Algorithmic and Geometric Perspective*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00140).

title: Explicit point sets with optimal linear dimension dependence
open: Construct, in deterministic time polynomial in \(d\) and \(1/\epsilon\), rational point sets \(P\subset[0,1]^d\) of size \(O(d\epsilon^{-2})\) with star discrepancy at most \(\epsilon\), uniformly for \(d\ge1\) and \(0<\epsilon<1\). Star discrepancy measures the largest error over all axis-parallel boxes anchored at the origin.
status: Heinrich–Novak–Wasilkowski–Woźniakowski prove existence in 2001 by probabilistic methods. Dick–Pillichshammer’s 2025/2026 work obtains almost-optimal dimension dependence using randomly shifted lattice constructions. A deterministic polynomial-time construction attaining the stated bound remains open.
why: Would turn optimal high-dimensional integration guarantees into efficiently reproducible deterministic point sets.
key_works: Stefan Heinrich, Erich Novak, Grzegorz Wasilkowski and Henryk Woźniakowski (2001), *The inverse of the star-discrepancy depends linearly on the dimension*; Josef Dick and Friedrich Pillichshammer (2025/2026), [*The star discrepancy of a union of randomly digitally shifted Korobov polynomial lattice point sets depends polynomially on the dimension*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.15877).

title: Whitehead’s asphericity conjecture
open: Must every connected subcomplex of an aspherical two-dimensional CW complex be aspherical? Here aspherical means that all homotopy groups in dimensions at least two vanish.
status: Open since Whitehead’s 1941 work. Diagrammatic methods establish many special classes, including suitable labeled oriented trees. Rational and \(p\)-adic analogues have advanced, but the original integral conjecture remains open.
why: Would explain when deleting cells preserves the absence of higher homotopy, connecting cell combinatorics with group presentations.
key_works: Stephan Rosebrock (2026), [*Labelled Oriented Trees and the Whitehead Conjecture*](https://www.mathematik.uni-mainz.de/en/2026/01/12/mathematics-colloquium-15-1-26-stephan-rosebrock-karlsruhe-labelled-oriented-trees-and-the-whitehead-conjecture/); A. M. Mikhovich (2025), [*Rational and \(p\)-adic analogues of J. H. C. Whitehead’s conjecture*](https://www.mathnet.ru/eng/im9597).

title: Andrews–Curtis conjecture
open: Can every balanced presentation of the trivial group be transformed into the standard presentation using inversion of relators, multiplication of one relator by another, and conjugation of relators? The original problem allows no addition of generator–relator pairs.
status: Formulated in 1965. Computations simplify many proposed counterexamples. Lackenby’s June 2026 preprint proves the conjecture for thickenable balanced presentations and bounds stable simplifications for that class; arbitrary presentations remain unresolved.
why: Determines whether algebraic triviality always admits a prescribed sequence of local combinatorial simplifications.
key_works: James Andrews and Morton Curtis (1965), *Free groups and handlebodies*; Marc Lackenby (2026), [*The stable Andrews-Curtis conjecture and thickenable presentations of the trivial group*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06122).

title: Decidability of four-sphere recognition
open: Is there an algorithm that, given a finite triangulation of a closed PL four-manifold, always decides whether it is PL-homeomorphic to the standard four-sphere? A terminating general algorithm or an undecidability theorem would settle the question.
status: Three-sphere recognition is decidable, while sphere recognition in dimensions at least five is undecidable. Dimension four remains exceptional. Discrete-Morse and bistellar-flip searches handle many examples but give no universally terminating procedure.
why: Determines whether complete automated recognition is possible for the most basic four-dimensional manifold.
key_works: Michael Joswig, Davide Lofano, Frank H. Lutz and Mimi Tsuruga (2022), [*Frontiers of sphere recognition in practice*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s41468-022-00092-8), [arXiv:1405.3848](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.3848).

title: Decidability of embedding two-complexes in four-space
open: Given a finite two-dimensional simplicial complex, decide whether it admits a PL embedding into \(\mathbb R^4\), or prove that no such decision algorithm exists.
status: A longstanding exceptional case in algorithmic embedding theory. The problem is NP-hard, and deleted-product obstructions are incomplete. Georgakopoulos–Winter’s 2024 work develops embeddability-preserving operations without settling decidability.
why: Would locate a fundamental limit of finite topological computation in a critical codimension.
key_works: Agelos Georgakopoulos and Martin Winter (2024), [*On 2-complexes embeddable in 4-space, and the excluded minors of their underlying graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12681); Jiří Matoušek, Martin Tancer and Uli Wagner (2011), *Hardness of embedding simplicial complexes in \(\mathbb R^d\)*.

title: Deterministic fully polynomial approximation for DNF counting
open: Given a Boolean formula in disjunctive normal form and \(0<\epsilon<1\), deterministically approximate its number of satisfying assignments within relative error \(\epsilon\) in time polynomial in the formula length and \(1/\epsilon\).
status: Karp–Luby’s randomized scheme dates to the 1980s. Deterministic methods handle structural restrictions, but no fully polynomial deterministic scheme handles unrestricted DNF formulas. The 2026 scalable algorithms continue to use randomization.
why: Would remove randomness from a central approximate-counting primitive used in reliability estimation and probabilistic databases.
key_works: Richard Karp and Michael Luby (1983), *Monte-Carlo algorithms for enumeration and reliability problems*; Salil Vadhan (2012), [*Pseudorandomness*](https://people.seas.harvard.edu/~salil/pseudorandomness/pseudorandomness-Apr11.pdf), Open Problems 2.36 and 7.31; Paul Burkhardt, David Harris and Kevin Schmitt (2026), [*Scalable Algorithms for Approximate DNF Model Counting*](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2026/244).

title: FPRAS for unrestricted integer contingency tables
open: Approximate the number of nonnegative integer matrices with specified row and column sums within relative error \(\epsilon\), with high probability, in time polynomial in the binary input length and \(1/\epsilon\). Both dimensions must be allowed to grow.
status: Studied intensively since the 1990s. FPRAS algorithms exist when one dimension is fixed and in sufficiently large-margin regimes. No known method gives the required uniform guarantee for arbitrary margins and unbounded row and column counts.
why: Would support certified counting, sampling, and exact-margin statistical tests without restrictive assumptions on the table.
key_works: Martin Dyer, Ravi Kannan and John Mount (1997), *Sampling contingency tables*; Mary Cryan, Martin Dyer and Dana Randall (2010), [*Approximately Counting Integral Flows and Cell-Bounded Contingency Tables*](https://doi.org/10.1137/060650544).

title: Two-gap conjecture for the asymmetric traveling-salesman LP
open: Prove that every directed metric traveling-salesman instance has a tour costing at most twice its subtour-LP optimum, or construct an instance with a larger ratio.
status: Longstanding. Constant-factor rounding is established; the 2026 literature records a universal upper bound of seventeen and lower bounds approaching two. Small-instance computations do not close the gap.
why: Would determine the strength of a foundational routing relaxation.
key_works: Ola Svensson, Jakub Tarnawski and László Végh (2020), *A constant-factor approximation algorithm for the asymmetric traveling salesman problem*; Alessandro Sosso, Ambrogio Maria Bernardelli and Stefano Gualandi (2026), [*The cloven traveling salesman: cycle covers and the integrality gap of small ATSP instances*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11590-026-02312-x).

title: Dynamic optimality of splay trees
open: Prove that splay trees serve every access sequence within a universal constant factor of the optimal offline binary-search-tree execution, allowing the customary initialization additive term, or exhibit a family with unbounded competitive ratio.
status: Conjectured by Sleator–Tarjan in 1985. Chmel and collaborators’ July 2026 preprint proves \(O(\log\log n\,\log^2\log\log n)\) competitiveness. This major improvement remains superconstant.
why: Would show that a simple adaptive data structure exploits every access pattern that any binary-search-tree algorithm can exploit.
key_works: Daniel Sleator and Robert Tarjan (1985), *Self-adjusting binary search trees*; Petr Chmel, Bernhard Haeupler, Richard Hladík, Michal Koucký, Antti Roeyskoe, Václav Rozhoň, Ondřej Sladký and Robert Tarjan (2026), [*Splay trees are almost dynamically optimal*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18498).

title: Unique Games conjecture
open: For every \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), is there an alphabet size for which it is NP-hard to distinguish permutation-constraint instances with optimum at least \(1-\epsilon\) from those with optimum at most \(\epsilon\)?
status: Proposed by Khot in 2002. Subexponential algorithms and major hardness theorems for related 2-to-2 games constrain the possibilities. The corresponding results with imperfect completeness do not establish the required near-perfect-completeness statement for unique constraints.
why: Would establish sharp approximation barriers for many combinatorial optimization problems from one constraint-satisfaction hypothesis.
key_works: Subhash Khot (2002), [*On the power of unique 2-prover 1-round games*](https://doi.org/10.1145/509907.510017); Subhash Khot, Dor Minzer and Muli Safra (2023), [*Pseudorandom sets in Grassmann graph have near-perfect expansion*](https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2023.198.1.1).

title: Log-rank conjecture
open: For every nonzero finite Boolean communication matrix \(M\), is its deterministic communication complexity bounded by a fixed polynomial in \(1+\log\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb R}(M)\), with universal constants independent of the matrix dimensions?
status: Formulated by Lovász–Saks in 1988. Sudakov–Tomon improve the general upper bound to \(O(\sqrt{\operatorname{rank}M})\) in work published in 2025. Hambardzumyan–Lovett–Shirley’s February 2026 revision gives new equivalent formulations, leaving the polylogarithmic target open.
why: Would connect linear-algebraic simplicity with efficient two-party communication.
key_works: Benny Sudakov and István Tomon (2025), [*Matrix discrepancy and the log-rank conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.18524); Lianna Hambardzumyan, Shachar Lovett and Morgan Shirley (2026), [*The Log-Rank Conjecture: New Equivalent Formulations*](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2025/141/).

title: Certified ATSP gap census beyond twelve vertices
open: Extend the exact census of half-integral asymmetric-subtour extreme points beyond twelve vertices, with checkable extremality, nonisomorphism, and integrality-gap certificates.
status: A proposed data target. Sosso–Bernardelli–Gualandi’s June 2026 enumeration reaches ten, eleven, and twelve vertices; unrestricted extreme-point enumeration becomes infeasible earlier.
why: Would provide auditable extremal examples for testing the ATSP gap-two conjecture and evaluating structural hypotheses.
key_works: Alessandro Sosso, Ambrogio Maria Bernardelli and Stefano Gualandi (2026), [*The cloven traveling salesman: cycle covers and the integrality gap of small ATSP instances*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11590-026-02312-x).

title: Sharp Matrix Spencer constant
open: Determine the least universal \(C\) such that every collection of \(n\) real symmetric \(n\times n\) matrices \(A_i\), each of operator norm at most one, admits signs with
status: August–September 2026 preprints prove the former Matrix Spencer existence conjecture. Song–Zhang give an upper constant below \(7.88\) and examples requiring \((2-o(1))\sqrt n\); their algorithm has a larger constant. The sharp universal constant remains unknown.
why: Determines unavoidable spectral imbalance under noncommuting matrix constraints and the achievable precision of matrix rounding.
key_works: Emrullah Akbas and Suvrit Sra (2026), [*A Proof of the Matrix Spencer Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.28816); Zhao Song and Lichen Zhang (2026), [*Matrix Spencer: Eight Standard Deviations Suffice and an Almost-Linear Time Algorithm for Dense Input*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15025).

title: Toeplitz’s square-peg problem for arbitrary Jordan curves
open: Does every continuous simple closed curve in the plane contain four distinct points forming a square? No smoothness, rectifiability, or finite-length assumption may be imposed.
status: Posed in 1911. Smooth curves and many other regularity classes are settled. Greene–Lobb’s 2026 paper establishes new Lipschitz two-graph cases. Approximation by smooth curves can produce squares collapsing to a point, leaving the arbitrary continuous case open.
why: Tests whether topology alone forces a universal finite geometric pattern.
key_works: Joshua Evan Greene and Andrew Lobb (2021), *The rectangular peg problem*; Greene and Lobb (2026), [*Square pegs between two graphs*](https://doi.org/10.4171/CMH/619), [arXiv:2407.07798](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.07798).

title: Sharp three-dimensional first-selection constant
open: Determine the largest \(c_3\) such that every \(n\)-point set in general position in \(\mathbb R^3\) has a point lying in at least \((c_3-o(1))\binom n4\) of its spanned tetrahedra. The conjectured value is \(3/32\).
status: Studied since the 1980s. Clustered constructions give the upper bound \(3/32\) in this normalization. Gromov’s method and Matoušek–Wagner’s refinements improve positive lower bounds without reaching that value.
why: Would determine the strongest universal simplicial-depth guarantee for three-dimensional point clouds.
key_works: Boris Bukh, Jiří Matoušek and Gabriel Nivasch (2010), *Stabbing simplices by points and flats*; Jiří Matoušek and Uli Wagner (2014), [*On Gromov’s method of selecting heavily covered points*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.3515).

title: Efficient refutation of sparse random 3-SAT
open: For some sufficiently large fixed \(c\), construct a polynomial-time algorithm that certifies unsatisfiability with high probability for a uniformly random 3-CNF with \(n\) variables and \(cn\) clauses, while never certifying a satisfiable formula. Alternatively, prove a computational obstruction under a clearly stated assumption.
status: A central average-case complexity problem since the 1980s–2000s. Feige–Ofek give polynomial-time refutation at order \(n^{3/2}\) clauses. The existence of shorter certificates in sparser regimes does not imply efficient discovery of certificates at constant density.
why: Separates efficiently recognizing typical unsatisfiability from proving that random formulas are almost surely unsatisfiable.
key_works: Uriel Feige and Eran Ofek (2007), [*Easily refutable subformulas of large random 3CNF formulas*](https://doi.org/10.4086/toc.2007.v003a002); Sarah Allen, Ryan O’Donnell and David Witmer (2015), [*How to refute a random CSP*](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/random-csp-refutation.pdf).

title: Algorithmic threshold of the symmetric binary perceptron
open: For fixed \(\kappa>0\), determine the largest constraint density \(\alpha\) at which a polynomial-time algorithm can, with high probability, find \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\) satisfying \(|Gx|\le\kappa\sqrt n\) coordinatewise, where \(G\) has \(\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor\) independent standard-Gaussian rows.
status: The satisfiability threshold is known, but the efficient-search threshold is not. Gamarnik–Kızıldağ–Perkins–Xu establish a multi-overlap-gap barrier for stable algorithms below the satisfiability threshold. Low-density search algorithms leave the general threshold unresolved.
why: Provides a precise test of how the geometry of a random solution space obstructs training discrete classifiers.
key_works: David Gamarnik, Eren Kızıldağ, Will Perkins and Changji Xu (2022), [*Algorithms and Barriers in the Symmetric Binary Perceptron Model*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15667).

title: Unrestricted uniform sampling for the symmetric binary perceptron
open: At fixed positive density below the satisfiability threshold, can a randomized polynomial-time algorithm output an approximately uniform satisfying assignment of the symmetric binary perceptron, with total-variation error tending to zero? Settle feasibility or establish a suitable complexity-theoretic obstruction.
status: Efficient search succeeds at sufficiently low density. El Alaoui’s 2025 theorem rules out approximate uniform sampling by stable algorithms and bounded-depth Boolean circuits at every positive density; these restrictions do not cover all polynomial-time algorithms.
why: Would determine whether efficiently found solutions can represent a typical feasible configuration.
key_works: Ahmed El Alaoui (2025), [*Hardness of Sampling Solutions From the Symmetric Binary Perceptron*](https://doi.org/10.1002/rsa.70021).

title: Infinite interchange cycles in dimensions three and four
open: Prove that nearest-neighbor random interchange on \(\mathbb Z^3\) and \(\mathbb Z^4\) has infinite permutation cycles with positive probability for all sufficiently large fixed times. Each edge rings independently at rate one and swaps its endpoint labels.
status: Part of Tóth’s 1993 conjecture. Elboim–Sly establish existence in every dimension at least five in their 2022–2024 work. Numerical evidence supports macroscopic cycles in dimension three, but the low-dimensional theorem remains open.
why: Would establish a spatial permutation phase transition in dimensions where repeated encounters defeat current high-dimensional methods.
key_works: Dor Elboim and Allan Sly (2022/2024), [*Infinite cycles in the interchange process in five dimensions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17023); Alessandro Barp et al. (2015), [*A numerical study of the 3D random interchange and random loop models*](https://doi.org/10.1088/1751-8113/48/34/345002).

title: Exact dynamic exponent of critical two-dimensional Ising
open: For critical nearest-neighbor Ising heat-bath dynamics on the \(L\times L\) torus, with each site updated at rate one, prove existence and determine the exponent \(z\) in the inverse spectral gap \(L^{z+o(1)}\).
status: Numerical work suggests approximately \(2.17\). Lubetzky–Sly establish polynomial relaxation at criticality. Masaoka–Soejima–Watanabe’s 2025 theorem gives the rigorous lower bound \(z\ge2\), if the exponent exists, without identifying its exact value.
why: Would quantify critical slowing down for the standard local Ising sampler.
key_works: Eyal Lubetzky and Allan Sly (2012), [*Critical Ising on the square lattice mixes in polynomial time*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.1613); Rintaro Masaoka, Tomohiro Soejima and Haruki Watanabe (2025), [*Rigorous Lower Bound of the Dynamical Critical Exponent of the Ising Model*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10955-025-03456-3).

title: Roughening transition of the three-dimensional Ising interface
open: Prove that the standard nearest-neighbor three-dimensional Ising model has a roughening transition strictly below its bulk critical temperature: its Dobrushin interface is rigid at low temperature but delocalized in a nonempty higher-temperature ordered regime.
status: Predicted for roughly half a century. Low-temperature rigidity is classical. Related solid-on-solid models have rigorous roughening theorems; overhangs and bubbles obstruct transfer to the full Ising interface. A 2026 tensor-network study supplies further numerical evidence.
why: Would rigorously explain how crystal facets disappear while bulk order survives.
key_works: Roland Dobrushin (1972), *Gibbs state describing coexistence of phases for a three-dimensional Ising model*; Atsushi Ueda, Lander Burgelman, Luca Tagliacozzo and Laurens Vanderstraeten (2026), [*Interface roughening in the 3-D Ising model with tensor networks*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.07829).

title: Planar Abelian-sandpile avalanche tail exponent
open: In the infinite-volume stationary Abelian sandpile on \(\mathbb Z^2\), obtained from wired boxes, add a grain at the origin and let \(S\) be the total number of topplings. Establish whether
status: Open since the development of self-organized-criticality models in the 1980s. Spanning-tree methods give substantial estimates, and high-dimensional avalanche exponents are known. The planar total-toppling exponent remains unresolved; avalanche area and individual wave sizes are different observables.
why: Would provide a rigorous avalanche law for a canonical model of self-organized criticality.
key_works: Deepak Dhar (1999), [*The Abelian sandpile and related models*](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0378-4371(98)00493-2); Tom Hutchcroft (2020), [*Universality of high-dimensional spanning forests and sandpiles*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.04120).

title: Bounded fluctuations of planar rotor-router aggregation
open: For clockwise rotor-router aggregation on \(\mathbb Z^2\), with all rotors initially aligned and particles launched successively from the origin, is the occupied cluster after \(N\) particles within a bounded radial distance of the disk of area \(N\), uniformly in \(N\)?
status: The Euclidean limit shape is proved, and Levine–Peres establish \(O(\log r)\) fluctuations at radius \(r\). Simulations suggest an \(O(1)\) radial error for standard initial configurations.
why: Would quantify the unusually strong fluctuation suppression produced by a deterministic local rule.
key_works: Lionel Levine and Yuval Peres (2017), [*Laplacian growth, sandpiles and scaling limits*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.00411); Levine and Peres (2009), [*Strong Spherical Asymptotics for Rotor-Router Aggregation and the Divisible Sandpile*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11118-008-9104-6).

title: Rigorous Coulomb phase of the cubic-lattice dimer model
open: Prove that the uniform perfect-matching model on the three-dimensional cubic lattice, in its zero-flux thermodynamic state, has the predicted dipolar \(|x|^{-3}\) asymptotics for connected dimer correlations and a divergence-free Gaussian-field scaling limit.
status: Huse–Krauth–Moessner–Sondhi’s 2003 gauge-field analysis and simulations predict this phase. Three-dimensional dimer behavior remains an active numerical subject in 2026; planar determinant and height-function methods do not establish the cubic-lattice scaling theory.
why: Would derive an emergent gauge field directly from a local combinatorial matching constraint.
key_works: David Huse, Werner Krauth, Roderich Moessner and Shivaji Sondhi (2003), [*Coulomb and Liquid Dimer Models in Three Dimensions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0305318); Hu-Xiao Peng, Zheng Yan and Shuai Yin (2026), [*Short-time critical dynamics in the classical cubic dimer model*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.15730).

title: Ferrari–Spohn limit for the top SOS level line above a wall
open: For the low-temperature \((2+1)\)-dimensional solid-on-solid model in an \(L\times L\) square with zero boundary heights and a hard floor, prove a Ferrari–Spohn diffusion limit for the top macroscopic level line near the middle of a side, with horizontal scale \(L^{2/3}\) and vertical scale \(L^{1/3}\). Take subsequences along which the fractional part of \((4\beta)^{-1}\log L\) converges away from a layering-transition value, and identify the limiting diffusion and its parameters.
status: Cube-root fluctuation bounds are known. Caddeo–Kim–Lubetzky prove a matching-order lower bound and the diffusion limit for a related setup with specially chosen boundary heights. The spontaneously selected top loop in the original box remains unresolved.
why: Would identify the complete fluctuation process of a random crystal facet.
key_works: Patrizio Caddeo, Yujin H. Kim and Eyal Lubetzky (2024), [*On level line fluctuations of SOS surfaces above a wall*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.09106).

title: Antimagic graph conjecture
open: Does every connected graph other than \(K_2\) admit a bijection from its edges to \(1,\ldots,m\) such that all vertex sums of incident labels are distinct?
status: Hartsfield–Ringel, 1990. Regular graphs and many tree and bipartite classes are settled. Deng’s 2026 results extend the bipartite cases without resolving arbitrary connected graphs.
why: Would show that connectivity alone permits globally unique vertex identifiers using the smallest possible edge-label set.
key_works: Hartsfield–Ringel (1990), *Pearls in Graph Theory*; Kecai Deng (2026), [*Beyond biregular: antimagicness of uni-regular bipartite graphs*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2026.115208).

title: Bijective harmonious labeling of every tree
open: For every \(n\)-vertex tree, find a bijection \(f:V(T)\to\mathbb Z_n\) such that its \(n-1\) edge sums \(f(u)+f(v)\) are distinct.
status: Part of the harmonious-labeling program originating in 1980. Müyesser–Pokrovskiy’s 2025 preprint establishes bounded-degree cases for sufficiently large trees; unrestricted degree patterns remain open.
why: Connects additive permutations with rainbow tree embeddings in algebraically colored complete graphs.
key_works: Graham–Sloane (1980), *On additive bases and harmonious graphs*; Müyesser–Pokrovskiy (2025), [*On the Graham–Sloane harmonious labelling conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.05280).

title: Graham–Sloane harmonious tree conjecture
open: Label an \(m\)-edge tree’s \(m+1\) vertices by \(\mathbb Z_m\), using every label and repeating exactly one, so that all \(m\) edge sums are distinct modulo \(m\).
status: Proposed in 1980; verified computationally for trees through 31 vertices. Bounded-degree cases for sufficiently large trees are now known. The modulus and permitted repetition distinguish this from the preceding problem.
why: Would realize every cyclic-group element exactly once as an edge sum.
key_works: Fang (2011), [*New Computational Result on Harmonious Trees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.3490); Müyesser–Pokrovskiy (2025), [*On the Graham–Sloane harmonious labelling conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.05280).

title: Super edge-magic tree conjecture
open: Label the vertices and edges of every \(n\)-vertex tree bijectively with \(1,\ldots,2n-1\), assigning \(1,\ldots,n\) to vertices, so that \(f(u)+f(uv)+f(v)\) is constant over all edges.
status: Enomoto–Lladó–Nakamigawa–Ringel, 1998. Caterpillars, additional families, and all trees through 17 vertices are established.
why: Tests whether arbitrary tree structure supports simultaneous bijectivity and a rigid additive conservation rule.
key_works: Enomoto et al. (1998), *Super edge-magic graphs*; Ichishima–López–Muntaner-Batle–Takahashi (2022), [*Recent studies on the super edge-magic deficiency of graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.04029).

title: Faudree–Lehel irregularity-strength conjecture
open: Is there an absolute \(C\) such that every \(d\)-regular \(n\)-vertex graph, \(d\ge2\), has edge weights in \(1,\ldots,\lceil n/d\rceil+C\) making all weighted vertex degrees distinct?
status: Open since 1987. Asymptotic bounds approach \(n/d\), and an additive 28 is available in sufficiently dense degree ranges. A uniform additive constant remains missing.
why: Would determine whether the elementary counting obstruction explains essentially the entire labeling cost.
key_works: Faudree–Lehel (1987), *Bound on the irregularity strength of regular graphs*; Przybyło–Wei (2023), [*Short Proof of the Asymptotic Confirmation of the Faudree–Lehel Conjecture*](https://doi.org/10.37236/11413).

title: Adjacent-vertex-distinguishing edge-coloring conjecture
open: Does every connected graph of order at least three, except \(C_5\), have a proper edge coloring with \(\Delta+2\) colors such that adjacent vertices see different sets of incident colors?
status: Proposed in 2002. Joret–Lochet improve Hatami’s \(\Delta+300\) bound to \(\Delta+19\) for sufficiently large maximum degree; additive two remains open.
why: Measures the extra scheduling information needed to distinguish neighboring vertices.
key_works: Zhang–Liu–Wang (2002), *Adjacent strong edge coloring of graphs*; Joret–Lochet (2020), [*Progress on the Adjacent Vertex Distinguishing Edge Coloring Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.06104).

title: Proper neighbor-sum-distinguishing edge-coloring conjecture
open: For every graph with no isolated edge or \(C_5\) component, properly color its edges with integers \(1,\ldots,\Delta+2\) so that adjacent vertices have different sums of incident colors.
status: Proposed in 2013. The general asymptotic bound is \(\Delta+O(\sqrt\Delta)\). Requiring proper edge colors makes this a surviving problem after the 1–2–3 theorem.
why: Combines conflict-free edge schedules with locally readable numerical identifiers.
key_works: Flandrin–Marczyk–Przybyło–Saclé–Woźniak (2013), *Neighbor sum distinguishing index*; Kalinowski–Pilśniak–Sidorowicz–Turowska (2026), [*Quasi-majority neighbor sum distinguishing edge-colorings*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.01835).

title: The 1–2 total-weighting conjecture
open: Weight every graph’s vertices and edges from \(\{1,2\}\) so that \(w(v)+\sum_{e\ni v}w(e)\) differs across every edge.
status: Przybyło–Woźniak, 2010. Deng–Qiu proved the conjecture for regular graphs in 2025; the unrestricted case remains open.
why: Asks for the smallest alphabet supporting a proper vertex coloring generated entirely by additive local data.
key_works: Przybyło–Woźniak (2010), *On a 1,2 conjecture*; Deng–Qiu (2025), [*The 1–2 conjecture holds for regular graphs*](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0095895625000371).

title: Locally irregular total 2-coloring conjecture
open: Color vertices and edges with two colors so that every edge of color \(c\) joins vertices with different \(c\)-degrees, counting incident \(c\)-edges plus one when the vertex itself has color \(c\).
status: Introduced in 2015. The 2026 work of Flaszczyńska and collaborators establishes further classes, including cacti, subcubic graphs, and split graphs.
why: Would show that vertex colors remove all obstructions to a two-class local irregularity decomposition.
key_works: Flaszczyńska–Gorzkowska–Grzelec–Onderko–Woźniak (2026), [*Locally irregular total colorings of graphs*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2026.115319).

title: Four locally irregular edge classes
open: If a graph admits any edge partition into locally irregular subgraphs, must four such subgraphs suffice? In each subgraph, adjacent vertices must have different degrees.
status: The three-class conjecture from 2015 is false; four is the revised target following the bow-tie counterexample. General constant upper bounds remain above four.
why: Seeks the correct universal decomposition number after identifying a genuine obstruction to three.
key_works: Sedlar–Škrekovski (2021), [*Remarks on the Local Irregularity Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.08111); Grzelec–Woźniak (2022), [*On decomposing multigraphs into locally irregular submultigraphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.08809).

title: Wegner’s planar-square coloring conjecture
open: Prove that the square of every planar graph is colorable with \(\Delta+5\) colors for \(4\le\Delta\le7\), and \(\lfloor3\Delta/2\rfloor+1\) for \(\Delta\ge8\).
status: Proposed in 1977. The subcubic case is solved. At \(\Delta=4\), nine colors are conjectured while twelve suffice; the exact large-degree bound also remains open.
why: Gives sharp frequency-assignment guarantees under interference at distance two.
key_works: Wegner (1977), *Graphs with given diameter and a coloring problem*; Liu–Xu–Zhang (2026), [*Between proper and square colorings of planar graphs with maximum degree at most four*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.01126).

title: Acyclic edge-coloring conjecture
open: Does every simple graph have a proper edge coloring with at most \(\Delta+2\) colors and no bichromatic cycle?
status: Fiamčík, 1978; independently Alon–Sudakov–Zaks. General bounds remain linear with a larger coefficient. Anto–Basavaraju–Kulamarva prove the conjecture for 3-sparse graphs in 2026.
why: Ensures that every pair of color classes forms a forest, excluding alternating cyclic conflicts.
key_works: Alon–Sudakov–Zaks (2001), *Acyclic edge colorings of graphs*; Anto–Basavaraju–Kulamarva (2026), [*Acyclic edge coloring of 3-sparse graphs*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2026.115135).

title: Sharp oriented chromatic number of planar graphs
open: Determine the smallest \(C\) such that every orientation of a planar graph has a proper vertex coloring with \(C\) colors in which no two arcs induce opposite directions between the same color pair.
status: The general interval remains \(18\le C\le80\). Clow’s 2026 work extends surface results while recording the unresolved planar gap.
why: Determines how much directional information planar adjacency forces a finite target digraph to retain.
key_works: Raspaud–Sopena (1994), *Good and semi-strong colorings of oriented planar graphs*; Clow (2026), [*On Oriented Colourings of Graphs on Surfaces*](https://doi.org/10.1002/jgt.70042).

title: Exact nonrepetitive chromatic number of the square grid
open: Determine the fewest colors for the infinite square grid such that no simple path has a color sequence consisting of two consecutive identical blocks.
status: Graph nonrepetitive coloring dates to around 2000. Tianyi Tao’s work, published in 2026, gives bounds of five and twelve.
why: Tests how one-dimensional repetition avoidance behaves under Cartesian products.
key_works: Alon–Grytczuk–Hałuszczak–Riordan (2002), *Nonrepetitive colorings of graphs*; Tianyi Tao (2026), [*The nonrepetitive coloring of grids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.16237).

title: Subcubic star edge-coloring conjecture
open: Does every graph of maximum degree three admit a proper edge coloring with six colors containing no bichromatic four-edge path or cycle?
status: Dvořák–Mohar–Šámal, 2013. Seven colors suffice, six can be necessary, and many restricted classes satisfy the conjecture.
why: Isolates the smallest unresolved degree case of star edge coloring.
key_works: Dvořák–Mohar–Šámal (2013), *Star chromatic index*; Cui–Han (2022), [*List star edge-coloring of claw-free subcubic multigraphs*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dam.2021.12.014).

title: Optimal polynomial relation between linear coloring and treedepth
open: Determine the smallest asymptotic bound on treedepth in terms of the linear chromatic number \(k\), where every simple path must contain a uniquely occurring color.
status: Hodor–Micek’s August 2026 preprint disproves a linear relationship, obtaining separation \(\Omega(k^2/\log k)\). The known upper bound is \(k^{10}(\log k)^{O(1)}\).
why: Quantifies how uniqueness on individual paths controls global recursive graph structure.
key_works: Hilaire–Krnc–Milanič–Raymond (2026), *Linear colorings of graphs*; Hodor–Micek (2026), [*Superlinear separation between linear and centered colorings*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18620).

title: Overfull subgraph conjecture
open: For an \(n\)-vertex simple graph with \(\Delta>n/3\), is \(\chi'(G)>\Delta\) equivalent to containing a subgraph \(H\) with \(|E(H)|>\Delta\lfloor|V(H)|/2\rfloor\)?
status: Chetwynd–Hilton, 1986. Chen–McDonald–Shan’s July 2026 preprint proves the assertion for sufficiently large \(n\) when \(\Delta\ge(1+\varepsilon)n/2\), for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\).
why: Would replace difficult edge-coloring obstructions with explicit density certificates.
key_works: Shan (2026), *Towards the Overfull Conjecture*; Chen–McDonald–Shan (2026), [*Towards the Overfull Conjecture II*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.02270).

title: Vizing’s 2-factor conjecture
open: Must every connected edge-chromatic critical graph with chromatic index \(\Delta+1\) contain a spanning 2-regular subgraph? Critical means deleting any edge lowers the chromatic index.
status: Open since the 1960s. Cases with \(\Delta\ge n/2\) are known; additional results combine degree and toughness, including toughness at least \(3/2\) and \(\Delta\ge n/3\).
why: Would force a spanning cycle system inside every minimal obstruction to optimal edge coloring.
key_works: Vizing (1968), *Some unsolved problems in graph theory*; Kanno–Shan (2019), [*Vizing’s 2-Factor Conjecture Involving Toughness and Maximum Degree Conditions*](https://doi.org/10.37236/7353).

title: Erdős–Lovász Tihany conjecture
open: Whenever \(\chi(G)=s+t-1>\omega(G)\), with \(s,t\ge2\), partition \(V(G)\) into sets inducing chromatic numbers at least \(s\) and \(t\).
status: Proposed in 1968. Many parameter pairs and graph classes are settled. Song’s July 2026 preprint proves the conjecture for all even-hole-free graphs.
why: Asks whether chromatic complexity exceeding clique size always separates into two substantial pieces.
key_works: Song (2026), [*The Erdős–Lovász Tihany Conjecture holds for all even-hole-free graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20376); Longbrake–Tariq (2024/2026), [*Some Cases of the Erdős–Lovász Tihany Conjecture for Claw-free Graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.15164).

title: The \(K_5\) and \(K_6\) cases of Hajós’ subdivision conjecture
open: Must every graph of chromatic number at least \(k\) contain a subdivision of \(K_k\), for \(k=5\) and separately for \(k=6\)?
status: Hajós, 1961. The assertion is true through \(k=4\), false for \(k\ge7\), and unresolved at these two intermediate values.
why: Locates the boundary at which chromatic complexity ceases to force topological cliques.
key_works: Catlin (1979), [*Hajós’ Graph-Coloring Conjecture: Variations and Counterexamples*](https://doi.org/10.1016/0095-8956(79)90062-5); Hayashi–Kawarabayashi–Yoo (2025), [*Chasing Tripods to Obtain a Rooted Subdivision*](https://doi.org/10.1137/23M157082X).

title: Sharp quantitative excluded-grid theorem
open: Determine the least growth rate of \(f(k)\) such that treewidth at least \(f(k)\) forces a \(k\times k\) grid minor, approaching the quadratic lower-bound scale with its logarithmic factor.
status: Chuzhoy–Tan’s published bound is \(O(k^9\operatorname{polylog}k)\). An exponent-eight improvement was reported in a 2026 formalization submission; a large quantitative gap remains.
why: The exponent governs quantitative consequences of graph-minor structure in parameterized algorithms.
key_works: Chuzhoy–Tan (2021), [*Towards tight(er) bounds for the Excluded Grid Theorem*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jctb.2020.09.010); Bonnet (2026), [*An Exponent 8 Bound for the Grid-Minor Theorem*](https://laxarchive.org/lax-17/index.html), formalization submission.

title: Sharp order of surface-embedding obstructions
open: Determine, as a function of Euler genus \(g\), the largest order of a minor-minimal graph not embeddable in a surface of genus \(g\).
status: Graph-minor theory gives finite obstruction sets. Houdaigoui–Kawarabayashi’s September 2026 revision proves an upper bound \(g^{2+o(1)}\); the known lower-bound scale is linear.
why: Quantifies the size of certificates for non-embeddability as surface complexity increases.
key_works: Houdaigoui–Kawarabayashi (2025), [*A quasipolynomial bound for the minimal excluded minors for a surface*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.15212); the same authors (2026), [*An almost quadratic bound for the minimal excluded minors for a surface*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02796v2).

title: Bouchet’s signed 6-flow conjecture
open: Does every flow-admissible signed graph admit a nowhere-zero integer flow whose edge values have absolute value at most five, with signed incidence conventions governing conservation?
status: Proposed in 1983. An 11-flow theorem holds generally. Nurse’s January 2026 preprint establishes the conjecture for cyclically 5-edge-connected cubic signed graphs.
why: Extends the nowhere-zero flow program to obstructions introduced by negative edges.
key_works: Bouchet (1983), *Nowhere-zero integral flows on a bidirected graph*; Nurse (2026), [*Bouchet’s conjecture for cyclically 5-edge-connected, cubic signed graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.05692).

title: Seymour’s planar multigraph edge-coloring conjecture
open: Is every loopless planar \(r\)-regular multigraph with \(|\delta(S)|\ge r\) for every odd-cardinality vertex set \(S\) properly edge-colorable with \(r\) colors?
status: Proposed in the 1970s. The cubic case is the four-color theorem. Chen–Naserasr’s 2025 preprint establishes further cases through signed bipartite partial 3-trees and planar duality.
why: Would turn the relevant fractional matching conditions into an exact perfect-matching decomposition theorem.
key_works: Chen–Naserasr (2025), [*Bounding signed bipartite partial \(t\)-trees and application to edge-coloring*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14304).

title: Planar circular flow conjecture
open: Does every \(2k\)-edge-connected planar graph admit a circular \((2+2/k)\)-flow, meaning a conservative real flow with edge magnitudes between \(1\) and \(1+2/k\)?
status: Related to Jaeger’s 1980s conjectures. The unrestricted-graph version is false. Known planar results include \(5/2\)-flows at edge connectivity ten and \(7/3\)-flows at connectivity sixteen.
why: Planar duality turns this into sharp circular-coloring guarantees from girth.
key_works: Jaeger (1988), *Nowhere-zero flow problems*; Cranston–Li (2020), [*Circular Flows in Planar Graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.09833).

title: Five-cycle double-cover conjecture
open: Cover every edge of every bridgeless graph exactly twice using at most five Eulerian subgraphs. These subgraphs may be disconnected.
status: Celmins and Preissmann, 1980s. The 2026 ordinary cycle-double-cover proof supplies eight Eulerian subgraphs; five remains open, while four cannot work universally.
why: Seeks the optimal bounded number of even edge sets underlying all bridgeless graphs.
key_works: Hoffmann-Ostenhof (2012), [*A note on 5-cycle double covers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.0096); Oum (2026), [*A proof of the cycle double cover conjecture by OpenAI: An exposition*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16356), §9.

title: Orientable cycle double covers
open: Does every bridgeless graph have consistently oriented simple cycles using every edge exactly once in each direction? Traversing an edge forward and immediately backward is not an allowed cycle.
status: A classical strengthening of cycle double covering. The 2026 ordinary existence theorem does not supply compatible orientations; many special classes are known.
why: Connects circuit decompositions to orientable embeddings and algebraic flows.
key_works: Bagheri Gh.–Omoomi (2016), *Small oriented cycle double cover of graphs*; Hušek–Šámal (2020), [*Homomorphisms of Cayley graphs and Cycle Double Covers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.03112).

title: Bondy’s small cycle double-cover conjecture
open: Does every simple 2-edge-connected \(n\)-vertex graph admit an edge double cover using at most \(n-1\) simple cycles?
status: Proposed in 1980. Ordinary existence is now proved. The stronger cubic bound \(n/2\), with \(K_4\) excepted, is known; the general \(n-1\) target survives.
why: Controls the number of connected circuits, which is not controlled by a bounded number of disconnected Eulerian subgraphs.
key_works: Bondy (1980), *Perfect path double covers of graphs*; Oum (2026), [*A proof of the cycle double cover conjecture by OpenAI: An exposition*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16356), §9.1.

title: Exponentially many circuit double covers
open: Does every 2-edge-connected cubic graph on \(n\) vertices have at least \(2^{n/2-1}\) distinct circuit double covers, counting collections of connected 2-regular subgraphs?
status: Hušek–Šámal exhibit an infinite sharp family. Their July 2026 preprint proves the target for 3-edge-colorable graphs and a weaker exponential bound under higher connectivity and girth at least sixteen.
why: Upgrades existence to abundance and identifies how scarce circuit covers can be.
key_works: Hušek–Šámal (2025), *Counting circuit double covers*; the same authors (2026), [*Exponentially Many Circuit Double Covers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24724).

title: DeVos’ Cayley-homomorphism flow-transfer conjecture
open: If \(\mathrm{Cay}(M,B)\to\mathrm{Cay}(M',B')\) is a graph homomorphism between Cayley graphs of finite abelian groups with symmetric connection sets, must every graph with a \(B\)-valued \(M\)-flow have a \(B'\)-valued \(M'\)-flow?
status: Formulated by DeVos and investigated by Hušek–Šámal in 2020. A stronger proposed transfer statement is false; the original remains open.
why: Would connect homomorphism order with constrained flow existence.
key_works: Hušek–Šámal (2020), [*Homomorphisms of Cayley graphs and Cycle Double Covers*](https://doi.org/10.37236/8456).

title: Kotzig’s perfect 1-factorization conjecture
open: Decompose every \(K_{2n}\) into perfect matchings such that the union of any two distinct matchings is Hamiltonian.
status: Proposed in the 1960s. Many individual orders are solved. Cheng–Sgueglia’s July 2026 preprint constructs almost the full number of pairwise Hamiltonian matchings, leaving exact factorization open.
why: Produces exceptionally structured round-robin schedules and erasure-code constructions.
key_works: Kotzig (1964), *Hamilton graphs and Hamilton circuits*; Cheng–Sgueglia (2026), [*The perfect 1-factorisation conjecture holds asymptotically*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09459).

title: Pullman’s path-decomposition conjecture for odd-regular orientations
open: Partition every orientation \(D\) of an odd-regular graph into exactly \(\frac12\sum_v|d^+(v)-d^-(v)|\) directed paths.
status: Originates in the 1960s–1970s path-decomposition literature. Patel–Yıldız’s 2026 paper proves sufficiently high-girth cases and random regular cases in the relevant fixed-degree regime.
why: Asks whether local flow imbalance is the only obstruction to optimal directed path decomposition.
key_works: Patel–Yıldız (2026), [*Path decompositions of oriented graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.06982).

title: Bollobás–Eldridge–Catlin graph-packing conjecture
open: If two \(n\)-vertex graphs satisfy \((\Delta(G)+1)(\Delta(H)+1)\le n+1\), can their vertices be identified so that their edge sets are disjoint?
status: Independently proposed in the 1970s. Many degree ranges and graph classes are known; Allen–Böttcher–Skokan–Sudakov’s July 2026 work advances bipartite guest graphs.
why: Predicts a sharp degree-only criterion for fitting two networks on the same vertices without edge conflicts.
key_works: Bollobás–Eldridge (1978), *Packings of graphs and applications to computational complexity*; Allen et al. (2026), [*Breaking the Bollobás–Eldridge–Catlin Barrier for Bipartite Graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17808).

title: Mader’s sharp connectivity-preserving tree bound
open: Does every \(k\)-connected graph of minimum degree at least \(\lfloor3k/2\rfloor+m-1\) contain every \(m\)-vertex tree as a subgraph whose vertex deletion leaves a \(k\)-connected graph?
status: Mader, 2012. Paths and several tree families are settled. Ma–Liu–Zhang–Hong’s September 2026 preprint proves all pendant extensions of paths.
why: Quantifies the degree surplus needed to remove a prescribed structure without reducing fault tolerance.
key_works: Mader (2012), *Connectivity keeping trees in \(k\)-connected graphs*; Ma et al. (2026), [*Connectivity keeping pendant extensions of paths in \(k\)-connected graphs and triangle-free graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23634).

title: Every longest cycle has a chord in 3-connected graphs
open: Must every longest cycle in every finite simple 3-connected graph contain a chord?
status: Thomassen, 1976. His 2026 paper proves that at least one longest cycle has a chord. The assertion about every longest cycle remains open.
why: Tests whether connectivity forces additional structure inside an arbitrarily selected extremal cycle.
key_works: Thomassen (2026), [*Chords in longest cycles in 3-connected graphs*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jctb.2026.03.001).

title: Smith’s longest-cycle intersection conjecture
open: For \(k\ge2\), must any two longest cycles in a \(k\)-connected graph have at least \(k\) common vertices?
status: Attributed to Smith in 1984 by modern references. Small-connectivity cases are known. Ma–Ning–Zhao’s September 2026 preprint proves a first linear bound, \(k/600\).
why: Links global vertex connectivity with unavoidable overlap between extremal cycles.
key_works: Gutiérrez–Valqui (2024), *On two conjectures about the intersection of longest paths and cycles*; Ma–Ning–Zhao (2026), [*Longest cycles intersect linearly in highly connected graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20724).

title: Three longest paths have a common vertex
open: Must every three longest paths in a connected graph share a vertex?
status: Popularized by Zamfirescu since the 1980s. Every pair intersects, but Gallai’s stronger question about one vertex common to all longest paths is false.
why: Is the first unresolved Helly-type intersection condition after the pairwise case.
key_works: Axenovich (2009), *When do three longest paths have a common vertex?*; Groenland–Longbrake–Steiner–Turcotte–Yepremyan (2025), [*Longest cycles in vertex-transitive and highly connected graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.04618), §5.

title: Bounded longest-path transversals
open: Is there an absolute \(C\) such that every connected graph has a set of at most \(C\) vertices meeting every longest path?
status: Motivated by Gallai’s 1966 question; one vertex need not suffice. Norin–Steiner–Thomassé–Wollan’s 2026 paper gives the upper bound \(\sqrt{8n}\).
why: Would provide a bounded-size certificate controlling all maximum-length routes.
key_works: Norin–Steiner–Thomassé–Wollan (2026), [*Small hitting sets for longest paths and cycles*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.08634).

title: Lovász’s path-removal conjecture
open: For every \(k\), does some \(f(k)\) ensure that every \(f(k)\)-connected graph and prescribed vertices \(x,y\) admit an induced \(x\)-\(y\) path whose vertex deletion leaves a \(k\)-connected graph?
status: Proposed in 1975. Initial cases are solved. Kawarabayashi–Lee–Reed–Wollan establish a weaker edge-removal statement in 2008.
why: Asks whether sufficiently robust connectivity can absorb any prescribed connecting route.
key_works: Chen–Gould–Yu (2003), *Graph connectivity after path removal*; Kawarabayashi et al. (2008), [*A weaker version of Lovász’ path removal conjecture*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jctb.2007.11.003).

title: Kriesell’s Steiner-tree packing conjecture
open: If every edge cut separating a terminal set \(T\) has size at least \(2k\), must there be \(k\) edge-disjoint trees each spanning \(T\)? Nonterminal vertices may be shared.
status: Proposed in 2003. DeVos–McDonald–Pivotto prove that \(5k+4\) terminal connectivity suffices; the factor-two threshold remains open.
why: Extends spanning-tree packing to redundant terminal networks.
key_works: DeVos–McDonald–Pivotto (2016), [*Packing Steiner Trees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.7621).

title: Degree two in minimally 1-tough graphs
open: Must every graph of toughness exactly one, for which deleting any edge lowers toughness below one, contain a degree-two vertex?
status: Kriesell, 2003. The broader prediction of degree \(\lceil2t\rceil\) in minimally \(t\)-tough graphs is false. The original \(t=1\) case survives the 2026 constructions.
why: Tests whether critical global toughness forces a simple local structural feature.
key_works: Cheng–Li–Liu (2026), [*Constructions of minimally \(t\)-tough regular graphs*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2026.114993).

title: Laborde–Payan–Xuong stable-set conjecture
open: Does every digraph have an independent vertex set meeting every longest directed path?
status: Proposed in 1983. Havet proves the conjecture when the independence number is at most two; further structured classes are known.
why: Would supply a strong structural relationship between independent sets and extremal directed paths.
key_works: Laborde–Payan–Xuong (1983), *Independent sets and longest directed paths in digraphs*; Havet (2004), *Stable set meeting every longest path*, and [author’s problem statement](https://www.openproblemgarden.org/op/stable_set_meeting_all_longest_directed_paths).

title: Bang-Jensen–Yeo strong spanning decomposition conjecture
open: Does an absolute \(k\) exist such that every \(k\)-arc-connected digraph contains two arc-disjoint strongly connected spanning subdigraphs?
status: Formulated in 2004. The existence assertion holds for tournaments and other special classes but remains open for general digraphs.
why: Asks whether sufficiently redundant directed connectivity always separates into two independently functioning spanning networks.
key_works: Bang-Jensen–Yeo (2004), *Decomposing \(k\)-arc-strong tournaments into strong spanning subdigraphs*; Havet’s [research problem statement](https://www.openproblemgarden.org/op/arc_disjoint_strongly_connected_spanning_subdigraphs).

title: Thomassen’s 4-strong Hamilton-connectedness conjecture
open: Is every 4-strong \(n\)-vertex digraph satisfying \(d(x)+d(y)\ge2n+1\) for each nonadjacent pair Hamilton-connected, with a spanning directed path from every prescribed vertex to every other?
status: Proposed in 1980. Darbinyan’s 2025 paper disproves related lower-connectivity conjectures while retaining this assertion.
why: Seeks a sharp combination of directed resilience and degree conditions guaranteeing every spanning route.
key_works: Darbinyan (2025), [*On Three Conjectures of Thomassen and the Extremal Digraphs for Two Conjectures of Nash-Williams*](https://doi.org/10.1002/jgt.23233).

title: Burr’s oriented-tree embedding conjecture
open: Does every digraph whose underlying graph has chromatic number at least \(2k-2\) contain every oriented tree on \(k\) vertices?
status: Burr, 1980. Fan–Lu–Chen’s September 2026 preprint obtains an \(O(k\log k)\) sufficient threshold, specifically \(\lfloor31\log(k!)\rfloor\).
why: Asks how ordinary chromatic complexity forces every orientation of a sparse connected pattern.
key_works: Burr (1980), *Subtrees of directed graphs and hypergraphs*; Fan–Lu–Chen (2026), [*A near-linear upper bound for Burr’s conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18175).

title: Linear Ramsey growth for hypercubes
open: Is \(R(Q_d)\le C2^d\) for an absolute constant \(C\)?
status: Burr–Erdős, 1970s. Tikhomirov proves \(R(Q_d)=O(2^{(2-c)d})\), with \(c=0.03656\) permissible. The conjectured exponent one remains open.
why: Tests whether symmetry can keep Ramsey growth linear despite unbounded maximum degree.
key_works: Burr–Erdős (1975), *On the magnitude of generalized Ramsey numbers for graphs*; Tikhomirov (2024), [*A remark on the Ramsey number of the hypercube*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.14568).

title: Exact value of \(R(3,10)\)
open: Is \(R(3,10)=40\) or \(41\)? Equivalently, does a triangle-free 40-vertex graph with independence number at most nine exist?
status: The first unresolved entry of the classical \(R(3,t)\) sequence. Angeltveit’s 2024 revision proves the upper bound 41; the lower bound is 40.
why: A sharply bounded frontier for exhaustive graph classification and certified nonexistence.
key_works: Exoo (1989), *On two classical Ramsey numbers*; Angeltveit (2024), [*\(R(3,10)\le41\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.00392).

title: Exponential dependence on maximum degree in Ramsey’s theorem
open: Prove \(R(H)\le2^{C\Delta}n\) for every \(n\)-vertex graph of maximum degree \(\Delta\), with an absolute \(C\).
status: Bounded-degree linearity dates to 1983. Exponential dependence on \(\Delta\) is necessary; the general upper bound \(2^{O(\Delta\log\Delta)}n\) retains an extra logarithm.
why: Would determine the correct degree penalty in sparse Ramsey theory.
key_works: Chvátal–Rödl–Szemerédi–Trotter (1983), *The Ramsey number of a graph with bounded maximum degree*; Conlon–Fox–Sudakov (2012), [*On two problems in graph Ramsey theory*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.0045).

title: Linear induced Ramsey numbers for bounded-degree graphs
open: For fixed maximum degree \(\Delta\) and color count \(r\), does every \(n\)-vertex graph \(H\) have induced Ramsey number \(O_{\Delta,r}(n)\)?
status: Polynomial bounds have been known since Łuczak–Rödl. Carenini’s July 2026 preprint gives \(Cn^{\Delta+2}(\log n)^A\); general linearity remains open.
why: Determines whether preserving all nonedges has an unavoidable superlinear cost.
key_works: Łuczak–Rödl (1996), *On induced Ramsey numbers for graphs with bounded maximum degree*; Carenini (2026), [*Embedding Induced Bounded Degree Graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04532).

title: Linear top exponent for \(r_4(5,n)\)
open: Is \(r_4(5,n)\ge2^{2^{cn}}\) for an absolute \(c>0\)?
status: The double-exponential tower height was established in 2026. Fan–Li–Lin–Ning improve the lower bound to \(2^{2^{cn^{1/5}}}\). The linear top exponent survives even after the analogous \(r_4(6,n)\) target was proved.
why: Isolates the remaining quantitative obstruction at the smallest nontrivial 4-uniform off-diagonal clique size.
key_works: Du–Hu–Liu–Wang (2026), [*A double-exponential lower bound for \(r_4(5,n)\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23986); Fan–Li–Lin–Ning (2026), [*An improved double-exponential lower bound for \(r_4(5,n)\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04105v2).

title: Multicolor ordered path powers with exponent independent of bandwidth
open: For fixed \(r,t\), prove \(R_<^r(P_n^t)\le C_{r,t}n^{Cr}\), with an absolute \(C\) independent of the path power \(t\).
status: Girão–Janzer–Janzer’s 2026 paper proves the two-color bound \(n^{4+o(1)}\) and formulates the multicolor target as Conjecture 4.4.
why: Asks whether bandwidth changes only the prefactor rather than the exponent.
key_works: Gishboliner–Jin–Sudakov (2024), *Ramsey Problems for Monotone Paths in Graphs and Hypergraphs*; Girão–Janzer–Janzer (2026), [*Ordered Ramsey Numbers of Powers of Paths*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02360).

title: Growth of the generalized Ramsey function \(f(n,4,3)\)
open: Determine the order of the minimum number of edge colors for \(K_n\) such that every four vertices span at least three colors.
status: Part of the Erdős–Gyárfás program. Bounds remain between \(\Omega(\log n)\) and \(\exp(O(\sqrt{\log n}))\).
why: Captures an intermediate regime between avoiding monochromatic cliques and requiring locally diverse colors.
key_works: Erdős–Gyárfás (1997), *A variant of the classical Ramsey problem*; Mubayi (1998), *Edge-coloring cliques with three colors on all 4-cliques*; Conlon–Fox–Lee–Sudakov (2015), [*The Erdős–Gyárfás problem on generalized Ramsey numbers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.0250).

title: Sharp tree supersaturation at the Erdős–Sós threshold
open: Must an \(n\)-vertex graph of average degree \(d\ge t-1\) contain at least \(n\,d(d-1)\cdots(d-t+1)\) injective labeled copies of every \(t\)-edge tree?
status: Mubayi–Verstraëte, 2016. Known when \(d\) is sufficiently large relative to \(t\); Wilson obtains a threshold of order \(t^4\). The sharp threshold remains after the existence theorem’s resolution.
why: Would determine the minimum number of tree embeddings, rather than merely their existence.
key_works: Mubayi–Verstraëte (2016), *Counting trees in graphs*; Wilson (2025), [*A Tight Lower bound on Trees in Graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.14890).

title: Ordinary Turán density of the broken tetrahedron
open: Is \(\pi(K_4^{(3)-})=2/7\), where \(K_4^{(3)-}\) consists of three triples on four vertices?
status: Frankl–Füredi constructions give \(2/7\); upper bounds remain slightly larger. The ordinary density remains open, despite solved codegree and uniform-density variants.
why: One of the smallest hypergraphs whose extremal density is still unknown.
key_works: Frankl–Füredi (1984), *An exact result for 3-graphs*; Falgas-Ravry–Pikhurko–Vaughan–Volec (2023), [*The codegree threshold of \(K_4^-\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09396); Piga–Schülke (2026), [*Hypergraphs with arbitrarily small codegree Turán density*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.02876).

title: Extremal number of the cube graph
open: Determine the asymptotic order of \(\operatorname{ex}(n,Q_3)\).
status: Erdős–Simonovits proved \(O(n^{8/5})\) in 1970. \(C_4\)-free constructions provide \(\Omega(n^{3/2})\); the exponent remains unsettled.
why: The cube is a small symmetric bipartite graph for which standard extremal methods still leave an exponent gap.
key_works: Erdős–Simonovits (1970), *Some extremal problems in graph theory*; [author problem archive](https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~erdosproblems/erdos/newproblems/TuranCube.html); Allen–Keevash–Sudakov–Verstraëte (2014), [*Turán numbers of bipartite graphs plus an odd cycle*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.3805).

title: Erdős–Simonovits odd-cycle compactness
open: For every finite family \(\mathcal F\) of bipartite graphs, does forbidding \(\mathcal F\) and all sufficiently short odd cycles recover asymptotically the extremal number of \(\mathcal F\)-free bipartite graphs?
status: Proposed in 1982. Strong versions are proved for smooth bipartite families, including several complete bipartite cases; arbitrary finite families remain open.
why: Asks whether finitely many odd-cycle exclusions can reproduce a global bipartiteness constraint.
key_works: Erdős–Simonovits (1982), *Compactness results in extremal graph theory*; Allen–Keevash–Sudakov–Verstraëte (2014), [*Turán numbers of bipartite graphs plus an odd cycle*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.3805).

title: Tuza’s saturation-limit conjecture
open: For every fixed graph \(F\) with an edge, does \(\operatorname{sat}(n,F)/n\) converge? Here saturation means \(F\)-free, but adding any missing edge creates \(F\).
status: Tuza, 1986. Calbet–Freschi’s 2026 paper repairs a gap in a classical partial theorem. Finite forbidden families can have nonconvergent ratios; the singleton case remains open.
why: Would establish a stable asymptotic density for minimal saturation.
key_works: Calbet–Freschi (2026), [*The Asymptotic Behaviour of \(\operatorname{sat}(n,\mathcal F)\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10847).

title: Sharp subpolynomial overhead for acyclic matrix patterns
open: Determine the optimal general growth of \(\operatorname{Ex}(n,P)/n\) for fixed acyclic 0–1 patterns \(P\), with containment respecting row and column order.
status: Pettie–Tardos refute the old polylogarithmic-overhead conjecture in 2025. Gishboliner–Li’s September 2026 preprint proves \(\operatorname{Ex}(n,P)\le n^{1+O_P(1/\log\log n)}\), leaving the sharp overhead open.
why: Controls ordered graph avoidance and geometric formulations of data-structure complexity.
key_works: Pettie–Tardos (2025), *A Refutation of the Pach–Tardos Conjecture for 0–1 Matrices*; Gishboliner–Li (2026), [*Proof of the Pach–Tardos conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20726).

title: Subdivision exponent-halving conjecture
open: For every fixed bipartite \(F\), does \(\operatorname{ex}(n,F)=O(n^{1+\alpha})\) imply \(\operatorname{ex}(n,\operatorname{sub}(F))=O(n^{1+\alpha/2})\), where every edge is subdivided once?
status: Kang–Kim–Liu, 2018. The predicted behavior is established for subdivisions of complete bipartite graphs, but the universal implication remains open.
why: Predicts a general transformation law for Turán exponents.
key_works: Kang–Kim–Liu (2021), [*On the rational Turán exponents conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.06916); Conlon–Janzer–Lee (2021), [*More on the extremal number of subdivisions*](https://authors.library.caltech.edu/records/sqbep-vc039).

title: Sharp crossing-lemma constant
open: Determine the optimal limiting \(c\) in \(\operatorname{cr}(G)\ge c\,m^3/n^2\) when \(m/n\to\infty\) and \(m/n^2\to0\).
status: The crossing lemma dates to the early 1980s. A July 2026 revision by Büngener–Franz–Kaufmann–Pfister improves the lower constant to \(1/27.3\); matching constructions remain unavailable.
why: Improvements propagate to incidence geometry and geometric sparsity bounds.
key_works: Büngener–Kaufmann (2026), *Improving the Crossing Lemma by Characterizing Dense 2-Planar and 3-Planar Graphs*; Büngener et al. (2026 revision), [*A first view on the density of 5-planar graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24364).

title: Pair-crossing number versus crossing number
open: Does every graph have equal pair-crossing and crossing numbers, counting crossing edge pairs and individual crossing points respectively?
status: Studied systematically around 2000. Solé Pi proves \(\operatorname{cr}(G)=O(\operatorname{pcr}(G)^{3/2})\) in 2025; equality or a counterexample remains unknown.
why: Determines whether repeated crossings between the same two edges can improve an optimal drawing.
key_works: Pach–Tóth (2000), *Which crossing number is it anyway?*; Solé Pi (2025), [*Pair Crossing Number, Cutwidth, and Good Drawings on Arbitrary Point Sets*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.03322).

title: Linear density of \(k\)-quasiplanar graphs
open: For every fixed \(k\), must an \(n\)-vertex topological graph with no \(k\) pairwise crossing edges have at most \(C_kn\) edges?
status: Conjectured in the 1990s. Linear bounds hold for small \(k\); general bounds retain logarithmic or slightly larger factors.
why: Tests whether excluding a fixed crossing clique controls density almost as strongly as planarity.
key_works: Fox–Pach–Suk (2013), [*The number of edges in \(k\)-quasi-planar graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2361); Suk–Walczak (2016), [*New bounds on the maximum number of edges in \(k\)-quasi-planar graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.0395).

title: Sharp star chromatic number of planar graphs
open: Determine the smallest \(C\) such that every planar graph has a proper vertex coloring with \(C\) colors and no bichromatic four-vertex path.
status: Albertson and collaborators proved \(10\le C\le20\) in 2004. The general planar gap remains open.
why: Determines the cost of requiring every pair of color classes to induce a star forest.
key_works: Albertson–Chappell–Kierstead–Kündgen–Ramamurthi (2004), [*Coloring with no 2-colored \(P_4\)’s*](https://doi.org/10.37236/1779); West, [*Star colorings and acyclic colorings*](https://dwest.web.illinois.edu/regs/starcol.html).

title: Shareshian–Wachs coefficientwise \(q\)-\(e\)-positivity
open: For every natural unit interval order \(P\), prove that \(X_{\operatorname{inc}(P)}(\mathbf x;q)\) has elementary-basis coefficients in \(\mathbb N[q]\), with \(q\) recording ascending edges of proper colorings.
status: Proposed in the 2010s. Ordinary Stanley–Stembridge positivity settles \(q=1\); the coefficientwise refinement survives. Three-column coefficients have further 2026 results.
why: Refines the representation-theoretic information carried by Hessenberg cohomology.
key_works: Shareshian–Wachs (2016), [*Chromatic quasisymmetric functions*](https://www.math.miami.edu/~wachs/papers/chrom.advances.pdf); Sagan–Tom (2026), [*Chromatic symmetric functions and change of basis*](https://doi.org/10.5802/alco.468).

title: Elementary-basis unimodality of chromatic quasisymmetric functions
open: Prove that every elementary-basis coefficient of \(X_G(\mathbf x;q)\), for natural unit interval graphs \(G\), is unimodal with symmetry center \(|E(G)|/2\).
status: A Shareshian–Wachs conjecture. Symmetry and special cases are known. The stronger coefficientwise log-concavity proposal has a reported 13-vertex counterexample in 2026.
why: Seeks a hard-Lefschetz-like distributional shape in the coordinates relevant to permutation representations.
key_works: Shareshian–Wachs (2016), *Chromatic quasisymmetric functions*; Cho–Huh (2017), [*On \(e\)-positivity and \(e\)-unimodality of chromatic quasisymmetric functions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.07152).

title: Positive combinatorial formula for Stanley–Stembridge coefficients
open: Give a uniform cancellation-free counting rule for \([e_\lambda]X_G\) for all unit interval graphs \(G\).
status: Nonnegativity is proved, but a general combinatorial interpretation remains open. Siegl’s 2025–2026 work supplies tableau-based lower bounds and special coefficient formulas.
why: Would make the positivity theorem computationally transparent and could expose its \(q\)-refinement.
key_works: Siegl (2025, revised 2026), [*Toward Lower Bounds for Chromatic Symmetric Functions in the Elementary Basis*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02841); Sagan–Tom (2026), *Chromatic symmetric functions and change of basis*.

title: A positive Schur rule for arbitrary LLT polynomials
open: Find a uniform combinatorial rule for every Schur coefficient of an LLT polynomial indexed by an arbitrary tuple of skew diagrams, using nonnegative \(q\)-weights.
status: Algebraic Schur positivity is known. Direct coefficient rules exist for restricted shapes and graph families; the unrestricted positive rule remains missing.
why: Could explain substantial parts of Macdonald positivity and improve coefficient computation.
key_works: Lascoux–Leclerc–Thibon (1997), *Ribbon tableaux, Hall–Littlewood functions, quantum affine algebras, and unipotent varieties* (verify); Wang (2025), [*Expanding the unicellular LLT polynomials of two-headed melting lollipops into ribbon Schurs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.08187).

title: Schur positivity of Macdonald cumulants
status: Dołęga, 2017. Polynomiality, monomial and fundamental positivity, and hook Schur coefficients are known.
why: Isolates connected contributions concealed inside individual Macdonald polynomials.
key_works: Dołęga (2017), [*Macdonald cumulants, \(G\)-inversion polynomials and \(G\)-parking functions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.02656).

title: Schur positivity of LLT cumulants
open: Prove that every LLT cumulant of a colored tuple of skew shapes, in Dołęga–Kowalski’s normalization, has Schur coefficients in \(\mathbb N[q]\).
status: Conjectured in 2022. Monomial and fundamental positivity, hook coefficients, vertical-shape results, and melting-lollipop cases are established.
why: Would imply Macdonald-cumulant Schur positivity through a positive expansion.
key_works: Dołęga–Kowalski (2022), [*LLT Cumulants and Graph Coloring*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.12676), [journal version](https://doi.org/10.37236/10977).

title: Goulden–Jackson Matchings–Jack positivity
open: Prove that Jack connection coefficients \(c_{\mu,\nu}^{\lambda}(1+b)\), in the triple-Cauchy normalization, lie in \(\mathbb N[b]\), and explain them using a nonnegative statistic on matchings.
status: Open since 1996. Polynomiality and top-degree positivity are known; further labeled cases were established in 2024.
why: Would explain the interpolation between symmetric-group class algebra and double-coset algebra.
key_works: Goulden–Jackson (1996), [*Connection coefficients, matchings, maps and combinatorial conjectures for Jack symmetric functions*](https://uwaterloo.ca/math/sites/default/files/uploads/documents/gjtams1996.pdf); Burchardt (2021), [*The Top-Degree Part in the Matchings-Jack Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.09330).

title: Falling-factorial positivity for shifted Jack polynomials
open: Prove that \(\alpha^{\ell(\mu)-1}H_\mu P_\mu^\#(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) is nonnegative in the basis
status: Alexandersson–Féray, 2017. Computational evidence and special cases exist; no general shifted Knop–Sahi-type rule is known.
why: Would explain positivity at partition arguments and support positive multiplication recurrences.

title: Zabrocki’s full superspace diagonal-coinvariant conjecture
open: For diagonal \(S_n\)-coinvariants with two commuting variable sets and one anticommuting set, prove
status: Proposed in 2019. González–Lentfer–Mularczyk’s September 2026 preprint settles the sign-isotypic component; the full graded character remains open.

title: Positive restriction rule from \(GL_n\) to \(S_n\)
open: Give a positive combinatorial formula for Specht-module multiplicities in the restriction of every irreducible polynomial \(GL_n\)-module along \(S_n\)’s permutation-matrix embedding.
status: A longstanding branching problem. Hooks and several small-shape families are known; Lee’s 2026 theorem handles indexing partitions with at most three columns.
why: Would make this basic transition between continuous and finite symmetry computationally explicit.
